title: Trevor Noah: My Depression Was Linked To ADHD! Why I Left The Daily Show!
speaker: Steven Bartlett & Trevor Noah

sentences.en: It felt like life was meaningless. I would think to myself, I hate this.
sentences.zh: 感觉生活毫无意义。我当时心想，我讨厌这样。

sentences.en: This sucks. I don't know what I want to do with life anymore.
sentences.zh: 这太糟糕了。我不知道自己的人生到底想要什么。

sentences.en: And that's sometimes where the depression would kick in.
sentences.zh: 而这有时就是抑郁症开始发作的时候。

sentences.en: But I didn't realize that the depression that I was suffering from was untreated ADHD depression.
sentences.zh: 但我当时没意识到，我所遭受的抑郁症其实是未经治疗的ADHD（注意力缺陷多动障碍）引发的抑郁。

sentences.en: And so I've learned rules now for myself and for anyone out there.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在为自己，也为所有有同样困扰的人总结了一些准则。

sentences.en: If you are suffering from this, ask yourself a few simple questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你正为此受苦，问自己几个简单的问题。

sentences.en: Mr. Trevor Noah, the former host of The Daily Show, where he gained a massive following for his humorous yet incisive take on politics and society.
sentences.zh: Trevor Noah先生，The Daily Show的前任主持人，他因对政治和社会幽默而深刻的见解而收获了大量粉丝。

sentences.en: I was born to a black mother and a white father in South Africa at a time when it was illegal in the country.
sentences.zh: 我出生在南非，母亲是黑人，父亲是白人，而那时在南非，这种结合是违法的。

sentences.en: They were scared the police were going to take me away, and then my mother met my stepfather.
sentences.zh: 他们很害怕警察会把我带走，后来我母亲遇到了我的继父。

sentences.en: And it became an unsafe household. Your mother had been shot point blank in the head by this man.
sentences.zh: 那变成了一个不安全的家庭。你的母亲曾被这个男人近距离开枪击中头部。

sentences.en: Yeah, and from that day onwards, everything changes.
sentences.zh: 是的，从那天起，一切都变了。

sentences.en: You arrive in America to pursue your dream as being a comedian.
sentences.zh: 你来到美国追求你的喜剧梦想。

sentences.en: You are very hardworking, to say the least.
sentences.zh: 至少可以说，你非常努力。

sentences.en: Which led to you being the host of The Daily Show, but it didn't go so well at first.
sentences.zh: 这让你成为了The Daily Show的主持人，但起初并不顺利。

sentences.en: It was absolutely terrible. People would just be like, go back to where you came from, death threat.
sentences.zh: 那简直太糟糕了。人们只会说，滚回你来的地方去，还有死亡威胁。

sentences.en: It was really hard, but I persevered. And I would get home at 9 p.m., work until midnight, get back to the office at 7 the next day, and do it all over again.
sentences.zh: 那段日子真的很艰难，但我坚持了下来。我晚上9点到家，工作到午夜，第二天早上7点又回到办公室，周而复始。

sentences.en: And then The Daily Show went on to become a smash hit, but it was the cost of it.
sentences.zh: 后来The Daily Show大获成功，但代价也是巨大的。

sentences.en: I had made my life about work, and I had made everything else secondary.
sentences.zh: 我把生活重心全放在了工作上，其他一切都成了次要的。

sentences.en: And to be honest with you, a lot of people are doing this.
sentences.zh: 老实说，很多人都在这样做。

sentences.en: We've neglected connection, and I think we're experiencing a generation of men in particular who are not just isolated, but not practiced in the arts of connecting.
sentences.zh: 我们忽视了人际连接，我认为我们这一代人，尤其是男性，不仅感到孤立，而且不擅长建立人际关系。

sentences.en: And it's affecting society now. So those men that are struggling, where do they need to start?
sentences.zh: 这正在影响社会。那么，那些正在挣扎的男性，他们该从哪里开始呢？

sentences.en: This is a lesson that I've learned if you're struggling with this.
sentences.zh: 如果你正为此挣扎，这是我学到的一课。

sentences.en: Trevor, what are the most important things that I need to understand about your earliest years to understand the man that sits in front of me today?
sentences.zh: Trevor，为了了解今天坐在我面前的这个人，我需要了解你早年生活中的哪些重要事情？

sentences.en: Well, that's a tough one because I feel like my perception of what the most important things are may not be the most important things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很难回答，因为我觉得我所认为的“重要事情”，可能并不是真正重要的。

sentences.en: I could say it would be my sense of humor.
sentences.zh: 我可以说是因为我的幽默感。

sentences.en: And then it might be where the sense of humor comes from, which might be my family or my country.
sentences.zh: 然后可能还要追溯到幽默感的来源，也许是我的家庭或我的国家。

sentences.en: It might be which schools I went to. It might be where I've lived or where I've traveled to.
sentences.zh: 也许是我上过的学校。也许是我住过的地方或去过的地方。

sentences.en: It's one of those, if you ever try to break down food or something that you consume and you go like, what is the most important ingredient?
sentences.zh: 这就像如果你试图拆解食物或你所摄入的东西，然后问：最重要的成分是什么？

sentences.en: What are the ingredients that really make it what it is?
sentences.zh: 到底是什么成分让它成为了它自己？

sentences.en: And it's like, is it the crunch? Is it the acid?
sentences.zh: 是那种脆感吗？是酸味吗？

sentences.en: Is it the salt? Is it the fats? What is it?
sentences.zh: 是盐分吗？是脂肪吗？到底是什么？

sentences.en: I don't know. I genuinely don't know. If I knew, then I would be able to either create more of me or maybe like, you know, figure out which parts I want to tweak.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。我真的不知道。如果我知道，我就能要么创造出更多的我，要么找出我想调整的部分。

sentences.en: But I honestly don't know the answer to that question.
sentences.zh: 但我真的不知道这个问题的答案。

sentences.en: I often think of everyone that I meet, but also myself through the context of like, I guess a similar analogy, like a set of ingredients that came together that were then put into an oven and like, the heat was turned on and we were bait not to say that we can't be changed after that moment but um what are those ingredients so my mother south african and hossa woman uh my father swiss from switzerland but was living in south africa so those are those are the parental ingredients you know my grandmother i think is a key ingredient because i spent a lot of time with her as a young child my grandfather was a crazy funny man was bipolar but we didn't know at the time i think we knew towards the end of his life but it made him wildly entertaining.
sentences.zh: 我经常通过一种类比来审视我遇到的每一个人，也包括我自己，就像是一堆成分混合在一起，放进烤箱，加热，然后我们就出炉了——并不是说在那之后我们就不能改变了，但那些成分是什么呢？我母亲是南非科萨族女性，我父亲是瑞士人，但他当时住在南非，所以这些是父母给的成分。我觉得我祖母是一个关键成分，因为我小时候和她待在一起的时间很长。我祖父是个疯狂有趣的人，他患有躁郁症，但当时我们不知道，我想直到他生命末期我们才意识到，但这让他变得极其有娱乐性。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's an interesting and tough one, you know, because I often think as much as we're baked to what you're saying, I think that we're baked, but then we are very much a product of the people that we then come into contact with, you know?
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个有趣且沉重的话题，因为我常想，虽然我们像你所说的那样被“烘焙”出来，但我认为我们很大程度上也是我们所接触之人的产物，你明白吗？

sentences.en: So I think of most people sort of like a sponge cake.
sentences.zh: 所以我把大多数人看作海绵蛋糕。

sentences.en: Like most cakes are very basic, most of them.
sentences.zh: 大多数蛋糕都很基础，大部分都是这样。

sentences.en: And then what really makes them special is what the baker does to them afterwards. you know, but the fundamental cake is pretty much the same.
sentences.zh: 真正让它们变得特别的是烘焙师之后对它们做了什么，你懂的，但蛋糕本身基本是一样的。

sentences.en: And I think people are like that. Yeah, there's certain things, you know, like, you know, the color of our skin and tone of voice and all of that.
sentences.zh: 我认为人也是如此。是的，有些东西是固定的，比如我们的肤色、嗓音等等。

sentences.en: But then I think it's everyone we come into contact with, that gives us the icing that gives us the shape that gives us the dynamic texture that makes us who we are.
sentences.zh: 但我认为正是我们接触到的每一个人，给了我们糖霜，给了我们形状，给了我们那份塑造我们个性的质感。

sentences.en: You know, and so I, strangely enough, I feel like it's all of these people that I was lucky enough, or unlucky enough to bump into that gave me a little bit of that texture and shape.
sentences.zh: 所以，奇怪的是，我觉得正是所有这些我有幸或不幸遇到的人，给了我那一点点质感和形状。

sentences.en: And I think that's the same for everyone, you know.
sentences.zh: 我想每个人都是这样，你知道的。

sentences.en: That's probably why I'm so conscious of choosing my friends.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是我为什么如此刻意地选择朋友的原因。

sentences.en: Because I think that's me actively choosing the people who are going to keep shaping me as I live my life.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得那是我在主动选择那些将继续塑造我余生的人。

sentences.en: I've seen you on TV. I've seen you all over the place over the last 10 years of my life. but I had no idea of your early context.
sentences.zh: 我在电视上见过你。在过去10年里，我到处都能看到你，但我对你早年的背景一无所知。

sentences.en: I had no idea. And it's funny because sometimes you kind of see, I don't know, domino 35 in all these dominoes that fall.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道。这很有趣，因为有时你会看到，我不知道，就像多米诺骨牌里的第35块骨牌倒下。

sentences.en: But those early dominoes, I think, often lead a lot of clues as to the domino 35 that we see on the screen.
sentences.zh: 但那些早期的骨牌，我认为，往往为我们在屏幕上看到的第35块骨牌提供了很多线索。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, yeah, definitely, definitely. So for someone that might not know your earliest context, like I didn't, what should they know to understand you?
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，绝对是这样。所以对于那些可能不了解你早期背景的人，像我之前那样，他们应该知道些什么才能理解你？

sentences.en: So, I mean, you know, first of all, I was born and raised in South Africa, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我是在南非出生长大的，对吧？

sentences.en: I was born in 1984. So that was, you know, six years before apartheid ended, born to a black mother and a white father at a time when it was illegal in the country.
sentences.zh: 我出生于1984年。那是种族隔离制度结束前6年，我出生在一个黑人母亲和白人父亲的家庭，当时这种结合在南非是违法的。

sentences.en: And it was strangely unique, you know, I guess because it was illegal, you know?
sentences.zh: 那是非常独特的，我想，因为它是违法的，你懂吗？

sentences.en: So I grew up in a world where I didn't see many people like me who had my background.
sentences.zh: 所以我成长的世界里，我看不到多少像我这样背景的人。

sentences.en: I saw some people who looked similar to me, but they had a completely different background.
sentences.zh: 我见过一些长相相似的人，但他们的背景完全不同。

sentences.en: And, you know, South Africa's racial dynamics are very complicated and sometimes throw people off, especially like internationally, you know.
sentences.zh: 而且，南非的种族动态非常复杂，有时会让人们感到困惑，尤其是在国际上，你知道的。

sentences.en: But yeah, I think that's one of the, you know, that's the beginning of me.
sentences.zh: 但是的，我认为那是我的起点。

sentences.en: And then I think, you know, I look at these ingredients, which aren't necessarily the best in choosing your starting points.
sentences.zh: 然后我看着这些成分，它们未必是最好的起点。

sentences.en: But then there was a series of lucky breaks, you know, the dominoes, as you say. there was a series of lucky breaks so one of those was apartheid ends you know so apartheid ends when i'm six years old and i i always think to myself about how much that changes my entire life because if if apartheid let's say apartheid went for 10 more years then now i'm 16 and i i haven't been able to go to the schools that i went to because you know only white kids were allowed to go to them.
sentences.zh: 但后来发生了一系列幸运的转折，就像你说的多米诺骨牌。有一系列幸运的转折，其中之一就是种族隔离结束了。种族隔离在我6岁时结束，我常想这改变了我整个人生，因为如果种族隔离再持续10年，那时我就16岁了，我就无法进入我后来上的那些学校，因为当时只有白人孩子被允许进入。

sentences.en: And, you know, children of color, black children in South Africa were restricted from going to the same schools and weren't allowed to live in certain areas.
sentences.zh: 而且，南非的有色人种孩子、黑人孩子被限制进入同样的学校，也不被允许住在某些地区。

sentences.en: And your whole life was defined by the color of your skin.
sentences.zh: 你的一生都被你的肤色所定义。

sentences.en: And so that becomes like one of the first dominoes that I didn't have anything to do with that changes my life.
sentences.zh: 所以这成了我无法左右的、改变我人生的第一块多米诺骨牌之一。

sentences.en: People that are growing up today aren't aware of what the apartheid is.
sentences.zh: 今天成长起来的人们并不了解什么是种族隔离。

sentences.en: No, no, no. I've had to research as an adult to make sure I know what it is.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。我成年后不得不去研究，以确保我了解它是什么。

sentences.en: I was born in 92. So for anyone that doesn't know what it's like to be a child that has a white father and a black mother growing up in apartheid South Africa, where, as it says on the front of your book, you're considered a crime because your father and mother have different skin colors.
sentences.zh: 我出生于92年。所以对于任何不了解在种族隔离时期的南非，作为一个有白人父亲和黑人母亲的孩子是什么感觉的人来说，正如你书的封面上所写，你被视为一种犯罪，因为你的父母肤色不同。

sentences.en: What does that environment feel like emotionally for you?
sentences.zh: 那种环境对你来说在情感上是什么感觉？

sentences.en: So I was lucky. I was lucky in that I think at least on the surface, I didn't feel it.
sentences.zh: 我很幸运。我幸运的是，至少在表面上，我没有感觉到它。

sentences.en: Because one of the most important things I've learned from my upbringing is... a child's reality for the most part is defined and created by their parents or their caregivers.
sentences.zh: 因为我从成长过程中学到的最重要的事情之一是……一个孩子的现实在很大程度上是由他们的父母或照顾者定义和创造的。

sentences.en: You know, so I didn't know that my world was strange.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道我的世界很奇怪。

sentences.en: I didn't know that my mother wasn't legally allowed to have me.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我母亲在法律上是不被允许生下我的。

sentences.en: You know, when, to understand the apartheid system, I always try and break it down for people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，为了理解种族隔离制度，我总是试着为人们拆解它。

sentences.en: You know, people think of like racism and they go like, oh, okay, it's racism.
sentences.zh: 人们想到种族主义时会说，哦，好吧，那是种族主义。

sentences.en: And I'm like, no, it's a much more insidious system that was designed to oppress people based on the color of their skin.
sentences.zh: 而我会说，不，这是一个更阴险的系统，旨在基于肤色压迫人们。

sentences.en: So where America just said there's black and white, and if you had like one drop of blood that was black, you were black, and it was a very simplistic system.
sentences.zh: 在美国，他们说只有黑人和白人，如果你有一滴黑人血统，你就是黑人，那是一个非常简单的系统。

sentences.en: The apartheid system was a culmination of all of the worst ideas from around the world in and around race.
sentences.zh: 而种族隔离制度是全世界关于种族的最糟糕想法的集合。

sentences.en: So the architects of apartheid explored what the Australians did with the Aboriginal people.
sentences.zh: 种族隔离的建筑师们研究了澳大利亚人对原住民所做的事情。

sentences.en: They explored what the Dutch did. That's where the word apartheid comes from.
sentences.zh: 他们研究了荷兰人所做的事情。这就是“种族隔离”（Apartheid）这个词的由来。

sentences.en: They looked at what the Germans did, you know, during the rule of the Nazis in Germany, like Nazi Germany.
sentences.zh: 他们研究了德国人在纳粹统治期间所做的事情，比如纳粹德国。

sentences.en: They looked at every type of racism, including in the US, you know.
sentences.zh: 他们研究了各种类型的种族主义，包括在美国的种族主义。

sentences.en: It's crazy how much effort they put into doing such a terrible thing.
sentences.zh: 他们为了做这种可怕的事情投入了如此多的努力，这真是太疯狂了。

sentences.en: I often joke with my friends and I go, if they put that amount of effort into making a great country, South Africa it probably would have been like one of the most powerful countries in the world by now because there was a lot of efforts and it's a genius system but just in the wrong direction so what that meant for me was I could be born by my mother you know I could be the seed of my father but I couldn't live with him we couldn't live with him we couldn't live together he couldn't live in our areas I could you know technically speaking my mother my father and myself weren't allowed to live in the same area.
sentences.zh: 我经常和朋友开玩笑说，如果他们把那种努力投入到建设一个伟大的国家上，南非现在可能已经是世界上最强大的国家之一了，因为他们投入了巨大的努力，这是一个天才的系统，只是方向完全错了。所以这对我的意义在于，我可以由我母亲生下，我可以是我父亲的种子，但我不能和他住在一起。我们不能和他住在一起，我们不能住在一起，他不能住在我们的区域。从技术上讲，我母亲、我父亲和我自己是不被允许住在同一个区域的。

sentences.en: That's how granular the system was. So I was considered superior to my mother, and then my father was considered superior to me.
sentences.zh: 这个系统就是如此细致。所以，我被认为比我母亲优越，而我父亲又被认为比我优越。

sentences.en: And so when I was really young, for instance, I'm still an indoor kid.
sentences.zh: 所以当我年纪很小的时候，比如，我一直是个喜欢待在室内的孩子。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of that is because when I was young, when I was with my grandmother, for instance, and my mom was working, my grandma would lock me in the house.
sentences.zh: 我想这很大程度上是因为当我小时候，比如我和祖母在一起，而我妈妈在工作时，祖母会把我锁在屋里。

sentences.en: I couldn't go outside and play with the other kids.
sentences.zh: 我不能出去和别的孩子玩。

sentences.en: I would escape now and again. She'd always tell me stories about how I would like dig a hole under the gate to go and play with other kids in the street.
sentences.zh: 我偶尔会逃出去。她总是告诉我，我是怎么在门下挖个洞，跑去街上和别的孩子玩的。

sentences.en: But she was terrified. And I thought it was just because she was strict and she loved me, but it was because she was scared the police were going to take me away if they found me running around in Soweto, which was a township where only black people were supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 但她很害怕。我以为那只是因为她很严厉且爱我，但其实是因为她害怕如果警察发现我在索韦托（Soweto）到处跑，他们会把我带走，而索韦托是一个只允许黑人居住的城镇。

sentences.en: And so in the apartheid system, this skin color wasn't considered black.
sentences.zh: 在种族隔离制度下，这种肤色不被视为黑人。

sentences.en: It didn't, your culture didn't matter. All that mattered was your shade.
sentences.zh: 你的文化并不重要。唯一重要的是你的肤色深浅。

sentences.en: And that was instrumental in keeping people, keeping a majority as broken up as possible to ensure that they were oppressing many minorities as opposed to one majority of people.
sentences.zh: 这对于尽可能地分裂多数群体，确保他们压迫的是许多少数群体，而不是一个多数群体，起到了关键作用。

sentences.en: So it's really complicated. I mean, you know, you've read up on it, but it's an infinitely complex system around a ridiculous idea.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很复杂。我是说，你读过相关资料，但这围绕着一个荒谬的想法，是一个无限复杂的系统。

sentences.en: So you weren't allowed to be seen in public with your mother?
sentences.zh: 所以你不被允许和母亲一起出现在公共场合？

sentences.en: No, no, no, no, not at all. And you weren't allowed to be seen in public with your father?
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，完全不允许。那你也不被允许和父亲一起出现在公共场合？

sentences.en: No, no. My mom, so when I'd go out in public with my mom, she would, she would, I don't even know where she came up with this, but she would act like she was supposed to be with me, but not related to me.
sentences.zh: 不，不。我妈妈，所以当我跟我妈去公共场合时，她会，她会，我甚至不知道她是怎么想出这一招的，但她会表现得好像她应该和我在一起，但和我没有血缘关系。

sentences.en: You know, so she would, she would dress up as, you know, everyone has different words for these in different countries, but like nanny, maid, domestic worker.
sentences.zh: 所以她会打扮成，你知道，不同国家对这些有不同的称呼，比如保姆、女佣、家政工人。

sentences.en: And she would just act like she's my caretaker, you know.
sentences.zh: 她会表现得好像她是我的看护人。

sentences.en: So it would look like my parents, I guess, have hired her to look after me.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来就像是我父母雇了她来照顾我。

sentences.en: And so that's how she'd move seamlessly with me in the streets because nobody would suspect it.
sentences.zh: 这就是她如何能带着我在街上无缝穿行，因为没人会怀疑。

sentences.en: Couldn't be with my father at all in public.
sentences.zh: 我根本不能在公共场合和我父亲在一起。

sentences.en: That was just out of the question. Second ago, you said you didn't feel this environment.
sentences.zh: 那根本是不可能的。刚才你说你没有感觉到这种环境。

sentences.en: Or at least you didn't feel these things to some degree.
sentences.zh: 或者至少在某种程度上你没有感觉到这些事情。

sentences.en: I sat with a guy called Gabor Mate. I don't know if you're familiar with Gabor.
sentences.zh: 我曾和一位叫Gabor Mate的人坐下来谈过。不知道你是否熟悉Gabor。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, of course, yeah. Yeah, and one of the things Gabor talked to me about from his early childhood was this moment when he was younger where, because he was Jewish, his, I believe he was Jewish, his mother had to give him up just for a couple of days, two or three days, because the Nazis were going to come and take her away.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然，当然。Gabor和我谈到他童年早期的一件事，当时他年纪很小，因为他是犹太人，我相信他是犹太人，他母亲不得不把他送走几天，两三天，因为纳粹要来把她带走。

sentences.en: So she thought, to save him, I'll give him up.
sentences.zh: 所以她想，为了救他，我把他送走。

sentences.en: It turned out she was okay, so she went back and got him.
sentences.zh: 结果她没事，所以她回去接了他。

sentences.en: Now, he cites that moment of trauma of losing his mother just for a little while as being really pivotal to his life, but also in the development of his ADHD and a lot of his sort of internalized shame.
sentences.zh: 现在，他把那段失去母亲的创伤时刻视为他生命中非常关键的时刻，也与他ADHD的发展以及他内心深处某种羞耻感有关。

sentences.en: And when he said that to me, I was quite shocked that even a couple of days away from a parent, a subtle feeling of neglect at such a young age, he cites as sort of putting shame into his soul, but also being responsible for some of his ADHD in the context that he thinks of ADHD as being this thing where we learn because our environment is so externally stressful, we start to avert our attention to other things sometimes.
sentences.zh: 当他对我这么说时，我感到非常震惊，即使是离开父母几天，在这么小的年纪感受到轻微的被忽视，他认为这会在灵魂中植入羞耻感，也是他ADHD的部分原因，因为他认为ADHD是一种我们学习到的东西，因为我们的环境在外部压力太大，我们有时会开始把注意力转移到其他事情上。

sentences.en: Now, the reason I say this is because it highlighted to me the chance and the probability that maybe we might not feel it consciously, but maybe subconsciously at a deeper level, these things shape us in a way that's harder to spot.
sentences.zh: 我之所以这么说，是因为它向我强调了这种可能性：也许我们可能没有在意识层面感觉到它，但在潜意识的更深层次上，这些事情以一种难以察觉的方式塑造了我们。

sentences.en: I wouldn't disagree with that. I'm sure his instance was probably harder if he A, remembers it, and then B, is separated from his mother.
sentences.zh: 我不会不同意这一点。我相信他的情况可能更严重，如果他A，记得这件事，然后B，与母亲分离。

sentences.en: You know, I'm not an expert in the field, but I think your mom holds a very different place in your life as a child.
sentences.zh: 我不是这个领域的专家，但我认为母亲在孩子的生活中占据着非常不同的位置。

sentences.en: You know, I think we're wired that way. And then I was lucky in that I was seeing my dad.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们天生就是这样。而且我很幸运，因为我能见到我父亲。

sentences.en: Does that make sense? So being in public with a parent is not really something of consequence if there isn't that in the world, you know?
sentences.zh: 这有道理吗？所以，如果世界上没有那种（正常的）环境，那么在公共场合和父母在一起并不是什么大不了的事，你懂吗？

sentences.en: And so when I think of like how we shape realities, I had no other reality to compare it to.
sentences.zh: 所以当我想到我们是如何塑造现实时，我没有其他现实可以比较。

sentences.en: So it's not like I was seeing other kids thinking, oh, wow, I'm left out.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是说我看到其他孩子，然后心想，哦，哇，我被排挤了。

sentences.en: There were many other kids. You know, even when I talk about my story, I always say to people, don't think of this as like a unique and special story.
sentences.zh: 还有很多其他的孩子。你知道，即使当我讲述我的故事时，我总是对人们说，不要认为这是一个独特而特别的故事。

sentences.en: It's just that I happen to be in a place where people talk to me about it.
sentences.zh: 只是我碰巧处在一个人们愿意和我谈论它的地方。

sentences.en: But I am but one story of many others. I knew many kids whose dads had been killed by the police or had been arrested by the apartheid police or had left into exile.
sentences.zh: 但我只是众多故事中的一个。我认识很多孩子，他们的父亲被警察杀害，或者被种族隔离警察逮捕，或者流亡海外。

sentences.en: And so they couldn't be with their dads for other reasons.
sentences.zh: 所以他们因为其他原因不能和父亲在一起。

sentences.en: So in a weird way, I used to think I was like the lucky kid.
sentences.zh: 所以奇怪的是，我过去常认为自己是那个幸运的孩子。

sentences.en: I knew my dad. My dad loved me and I would see this man.
sentences.zh: 我认识我父亲。我父亲爱我，我能见到这个男人。

sentences.en: And it was so like the feeling of that, I think at that age, maybe wasn't apparent for me.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉，我想在那个年纪，对我来说可能并不明显。

sentences.en: I'm sure I've been more affected by things that happened in my latter years because I was more aware of them.
sentences.zh: 我相信我后来受到的影响更大，因为我更了解这些事情。

sentences.en: But as a child, I'm just having a good time.
sentences.zh: 但作为一个孩子，我只是玩得很开心。

sentences.en: I'm spending time with my mom. I'm never not seeing her.
sentences.zh: 我和我妈妈在一起。我从不离开她。

sentences.en: And if I'm not with her, I'm with my grandmother, which is, again, normal in many cultures all over the world.
sentences.zh: 如果我不和她在一起，我就和祖母在一起，这在世界各地的许多文化中都是正常的。

sentences.en: But there was never a moment where I'm separated from this person because of the system.
sentences.zh: 但从来没有一个时刻是因为这个系统而让我与这个人分离。

sentences.en: And she was brilliant to figure out how to do that. and so I that's why I say I don't I don't disagree with what you're saying but I think everything affects us and everything can be thought to affect us negatively and positively and you know I've yet to meet a human being who's had a perfect existence so I'm very careful to then sort of like point to everything as the reason for because everything is already the reason for which does that make sense yeah your mother and your father were they in love in your view oh yeah Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 她很聪明，想出了如何做到这一点。所以我才说我不同意你的说法，但我认为一切都会影响我们，一切都可以被认为对我们有负面和正面的影响，而且我还没见过一个拥有完美存在的人，所以我非常谨慎地不去把一切都归结为原因，因为一切都已经成为了原因，这有道理吗？是的，你的母亲和父亲，在你看来他们相爱吗？哦，是的，绝对相爱。

sentences.en: Definitely. She eventually married someone else?
sentences.zh: 绝对的。她后来嫁给了别人？

sentences.en: Yeah, she eventually married. She was never married to my dad.
sentences.zh: 是的，她后来结婚了。她从未和我父亲结婚。

sentences.en: So they couldn't get married because of the laws.
sentences.zh: 因为法律原因他们无法结婚。

sentences.en: And then I think afterwards, my mom was just like, we are where we are.
sentences.zh: 后来我想，我妈妈当时就是觉得，我们现在处境如此。

sentences.en: And... And then I think there was a seminal moment in their lives, you know, where she became very religious and my dad was not at all.
sentences.zh: 然后我想在他们的生活中有一个重大的时刻，她变得非常虔诚，而我父亲一点也不。

sentences.en: And my mom was like, well, I'm going down a religious path.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈当时觉得，好吧，我要走上一条宗教道路。

sentences.en: And so this is my new life, you know. And he was called Abel.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我的新生活。他叫Abel。

sentences.en: Yeah. That's my stepfather. Your stepfather.
sentences.zh: 是的。那是我的继父。你的继父。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I read about the relationship your mother had with him and it seemed to be a very complicated and at times violent relationship.
sentences.zh: 我读过你母亲和他之间的关系，那似乎是一段非常复杂且有时充满暴力的关系。

sentences.en: Yeah. Yeah, it really was Do you understand what that means at that age?
sentences.zh: 是的。确实如此。你在那个年纪明白这意味着什么吗？

sentences.en: You know, it's tough It's tough to process Because I don't even think I fully know what it means at this age You know, like Love Violence, domestic abuse These are things that I don't think Anyone fully comprehends Even when I talk to like therapists about it It's always like It's a theoretical understanding It's not a fact.
sentences.zh: 这很难。处理这些很难。因为我甚至不认为我在这个年纪完全明白这意味着什么。爱、暴力、家庭虐待，这些事情我不认为任何人能完全理解。即使我和治疗师谈论它，它总是像是一种理论上的理解，而不是事实。

sentences.en: It's like, we think that this, and this could be because, and this could cause, and therefore that could be, you know, and we have brilliant minds who think on what this does and how it creates and, you know, but man, I, you know, I will never take for granted what it was like, you know, for myself and for any other kid who's experienced it growing up in a home where there's domestic violence.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们认为这可能是因为，这可能导致，因此那可能发生，你知道，我们有才华横溢的思想家在思考这会造成什么以及它是如何产生的，但是伙计，我永远不会认为任何经历过家庭暴力成长的孩子所经历的一切是理所当然的。

sentences.en: Like it's one of the worst things you experience because you live in a world where your parents are like the president in a weird way.
sentences.zh: 这就像你所经历的最糟糕的事情之一，因为你生活在一个父母在某种程度上就像总统的世界里。

sentences.en: You know, when you're a child, your parents are the most powerful beings you know.
sentences.zh: 当你还是个孩子时，父母是你所知道的最强大的存在。

sentences.en: In your head, no one is more powerful than them.
sentences.zh: 在你的脑海里，没有人比他们更强大。

sentences.en: And if you ever have the terrible fortune of seeing your parents, most times your mother being in a position where she's being violently harmed, I mean, it rocks your fundamental understanding of what the world is. you know?
sentences.zh: 如果你有幸看到你的父母，大多数时候是你的母亲，处于一种她正受到暴力伤害的位置，这意味着它动摇了你对世界本质的理解。

sentences.en: So for me, I mean, that's something I still deal with in therapy today, you know, because I'm always trying to chip away and trying to understand what is still on me and what is calloused that I don't wish to be.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这是我今天在治疗中仍然要处理的事情，因为我一直在试图剥离，试图理解什么仍然留在我身上，什么是我不希望有的老茧。

sentences.en: And then what is too soft or what is like, I'm always trying to understand it because I don't think there's one concrete answer for what the experience does to you is there anything still on you oh definitely i think i think there always will be you know because uh you know i didn't ever see that in my home but i can only imagine how much that would have exacerbated my further um my early perception of what a relationship and what love means to some degree so so you see like my curiosity my question to you then is like when you go you didn't experience it i go but what did you experience and this is this is the weird thing about the mind, right, is I find whenever I speak to, I mean, like brilliant thinkers and, you know, the therapists and, you know, psychologists and all these people, what I find fascinating is how sometimes your traumas or your perception of your traumas is directly proportional to what you lived in your life.
sentences.zh: 还有什么是太软弱的，或者是什么，我一直在试图理解它，因为我不认为对于这种经历对你造成的影响有一个具体的答案。有什么东西还留在你身上吗？哦，绝对有，我想永远都会有，因为我从未在家里见过那种情况，但我只能想象那会多么加剧我早期对人际关系和爱的理解。

sentences.en: So in a weird way, you might have the exact same experience that I have.
sentences.zh: 所以你看，我的好奇心，我对你的问题是，当你去的时候，你没有经历过它，但我会问，你经历了什么？这就是关于大脑的奇怪之处，对吧？我发现每当我与才华横溢的思想家、治疗师、心理学家以及所有这些人交谈时，我发现令人着迷的是，有时你的创伤或你对创伤的感知与你生活中所经历的事情成正比。

sentences.en: It's just that mine might have been more physical.
sentences.zh: 所以奇怪的是，你可能和我有着完全相同的经历。

sentences.en: Does that make sense? It's an interpretation, right?
sentences.zh: 只是我的可能更具身体性。

sentences.en: I'm always fascinated by that. Like by how I can connect with somebody where in their house, it was more about like fighting and bickering and people saying things to each other and shouting.
sentences.zh: 这有道理吗？这是一种解读，对吧？

sentences.en: And I didn't grow up in that kind of house.
sentences.zh: 我总是对此感到着迷。比如我如何能与某人产生共鸣，在他们的家里，更多的是关于争吵、拌嘴、人们互相说狠话和喊叫。

sentences.en: But then I've met people who did. And we seem to be kindred spirits because we've both experienced fundamentally an unsafe household, you know, the feeling of an unsafe household.
sentences.zh: 我没有在那种家庭中长大。

sentences.en: And I think that's something that many adults are still dealing with or not dealing with.
sentences.zh: 但我遇到过经历过那种家庭的人。我们似乎是志同道合的人，因为我们都从根本上经历过一个不安全的家庭，那种不安全家庭的感觉。

sentences.en: But as a child, I don't think we're sitting there with a little notepad going, well, nothing physical happened here.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是许多成年人仍在处理或未处理的事情。

sentences.en: And that was only words. And this was because of stress.
sentences.zh: 但作为一个孩子，我不认为我们坐在那里拿着小笔记本写着：好吧，这里没有发生身体上的事情。

sentences.en: And no, we're just experiencing an unsafe environment.
sentences.zh: 那只是言语。这是因为压力。

sentences.en: I only really learned about myself in this context through my triggers as an adult.
sentences.zh: 不，我们只是在经历一个不安全的环境。

sentences.en: And then kind of matching the cards. There's this game where you match the cards together and go snap.
sentences.zh: 我真正了解自己是在成年后通过我的触发点。

sentences.en: And it was me pursuing a young lady, the young lady turning to me after me trying to get her to date me for like three years.
sentences.zh: 然后有点像配对卡片。有个游戏是把卡片配对在一起，然后喊“啪”。

sentences.en: And be like, let's be in a relationship.
sentences.zh: 那是我在追求一位年轻女士，在我试图让她和我约会大约三年后，她转向我。

sentences.en: And then the feeling I got matched. the feeling I had when I was like six or seven and I watched my mother screaming in my father's face.
sentences.zh: 说，让我们建立一段关系吧。

sentences.en: And that happened enough times, me avoiding romantic relationships.
sentences.zh: 然后我得到的感觉配上了对。那种我在六七岁时，看着母亲在我父亲面前尖叫的感觉。

sentences.en: Oh, that's fascinating. Rejecting everyone.
sentences.zh: 那发生了足够多次，我开始逃避浪漫关系。

sentences.en: And the minute of connection, the minute where we were about to form a relationship because, oh, this is that feeling from my childhood.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太迷人了。拒绝所有人。

sentences.en: They're the same thing. How did you match them?
sentences.zh: 在连接的那一刻，在我们即将建立关系的那一刻，因为，哦，这就是我童年的那种感觉。

sentences.en: Because the way I would describe the feeling was impending prison time. i've seen like prison time was watching my father sit there passively as as screamed at and thinking why doesn't this guy leave why does it why is he why is he with her and so that's kind of where i formed the hypothesis and once i had something to aim at i could resolve it and i resolved it wow but i don't know no that's interesting you see yeah, on my side, it was the other way around.
sentences.zh: 它们是同一回事。你是怎么把它们配对上的？

sentences.en: It's like, I think when I looked at how I saw relationships and love in that way, it was like, I never saw it as like a prison, but in a similar way, I think in a way that sort of informed my avoidance, it was more me realizing I don't have an opportunity or I'll never have an opportunity to hurt you if I don't fully give to you.
sentences.zh: 因为我描述那种感觉的方式是“即将到来的牢狱之灾”。我见过像牢狱之灾一样，看着我父亲被动地坐在那里，被尖叫着，心想为什么这家伙不离开？为什么他要和她在一起？所以这就是我形成假设的地方，一旦我有了目标，我就能解决它，我解决了它。哇，但我不知道，不，那很有趣，你看，是的，在我这边，情况正好相反。

sentences.en: That's why I say we can be in the same boat, but realize we have different tickets that brought us here.
sentences.zh: 就像，我想当我以那种方式看待人际关系和爱时，我从未把它看作是一个监狱，但以一种类似的方式，我想它以某种方式影响了我的回避，更多的是我意识到如果我不完全付出，我就没有机会伤害你。

sentences.en: The outcome is the same, but we end up in the same place.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我说我们可以在同一条船上，但意识到我们有不同的船票来到这里。

sentences.en: And so in my world, I'm without a doubt, think that seeing a relationship where somebody was hurt because they allowed somebody into their lives affected my ability to allow people into of my life because I was like, oh, if that happens to me, then what happens?
sentences.zh: 结果是一样的，但我们最终到达了同一个地方。

sentences.en: Are you a prisoner? Like, are you subject?
sentences.zh: 所以在我的世界里，我毫无疑问地认为，看到一段关系中有人因为允许某人进入他们的生活而受到伤害，影响了我允许人们进入我生活的能力，因为我在想，哦，如果那发生在我身上，那会怎样？

sentences.en: And you grow up in a world where people just don't seem to take it seriously.
sentences.zh: 你是囚犯吗？你是从属的吗？

sentences.en: You know, this is still a problem in South Africa till this day.
sentences.zh: 你成长在一个人们似乎并不认真对待它的世界里。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a problem in many countries around the world.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这在南非至今仍然是一个问题。

sentences.en: I was in, where was I recently? I was in Amsterdam recently.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是世界许多国家的一个问题。

sentences.en: And I saw they had this huge campaign around femicide and gender-based violence.
sentences.zh: 我最近在哪里？我最近在阿姆斯特丹。

sentences.en: And it's a problem all over the world where people sort of don't take it seriously.
sentences.zh: 我看到他们围绕杀害女性和基于性别的暴力开展了大规模运动。

sentences.en: You know, they call it a crime of passion.
sentences.zh: 这是全世界的一个问题，人们似乎并不认真对待它。

sentences.en: You know, a woman goes to the police and says, you know, my husband beat me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们称之为“激情犯罪”。

sentences.en: And they go like, oh, but what did you do?
sentences.zh: 你知道，一个女人去警察局说，你知道，我丈夫打我。

sentences.en: This is between you and your husband. Go home, sort it out, figure the whole thing out.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，哦，但你做了什么？

sentences.en: And I think that definitely left me as a child, even though I was a child, looking at the world going like, oh, wow, okay.
sentences.zh: 这是你和你丈夫之间的事。回家去，解决它，把整件事搞定。

sentences.en: So the world thinks this is normal. then, you know, then that means the world won't keep me safe either.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对让我作为一个孩子，尽管我还是个孩子，看着世界心想，哦，哇，好吧。

sentences.en: Does that make sense?
sentences.zh: 所以世界认为这是正常的。那么，这意味着世界也不会保护我。

sentences.en: You went through something that, again, really, really horrific, and you got a phone call one day that your mother had been shot by this man.
sentences.zh: 这有道理吗？你经历了一些，再次强调，真的非常非常可怕的事情，有一天你接到一个电话，说你母亲被这个男人开枪击中了。

sentences.en: Yeah. And she'd been shot point blank in the head by this man.
sentences.zh: 是的。她被这个男人近距离开枪击中了头部。

sentences.en: Yeah. How old were you then? Twenties, when this happened.
sentences.zh: 是的。那时你多大？二十多岁，当这件事发生时。

sentences.en: Let me think. No, I was in my... I was closer to my 30s because my younger brother was old enough-ish to drive, but shouldn't have been able to drive.
sentences.zh: 让我想想。不，我当时在我的……我快30岁了，因为我弟弟大到可以开车了，但不应该开车。

sentences.en: So maybe he was like 40. So yeah, maybe I'm like 24 at the time, somewhere there.
sentences.zh: 所以也许他大约40岁。所以是的，也许我当时24岁左右，就在那里。

sentences.en: 24. You get a phone call from him, your younger brother?
sentences.zh: 24岁。你接到他，你弟弟的电话？

sentences.en: Yeah. Saying mom's been shot.
sentences.zh: 是的。说妈妈被开枪击中了。

sentences.en: What goes through your head in that moment when you get a call like that?
sentences.zh: 那一刻你接到那样的电话，你脑子里在想什么？

sentences.en: What went through my head was I knew exactly who did it.
sentences.zh: 我脑子里想的是，我确切地知道是谁干的。

sentences.en: I knew what had happened. Like it's, you know, one of the worst things that comes with growing up in a house of domestic abuse and a house where you're dealing with an alcoholic is you become hypersensitive and you become really good at predicting things, you know.
sentences.zh: 我知道发生了什么。就像，你知道，在家庭虐待家庭中长大，在处理酗酒者的家庭中长大，最糟糕的事情之一就是你变得高度敏感，你变得非常擅长预测事情，你知道。

sentences.en: So, I mean, my friends know till this day, I'll be the kind of person, I'll tell you when we should leave a party before a fight breaks out.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的朋友们至今都知道，我会是那种人，我会告诉你我们应该在打架爆发前离开派对。

sentences.en: I'm never around for the fight because I can feel it.
sentences.zh: 我从不在打架现场，因为我能感觉到。

sentences.en: I can feel energy. I can feel, and not like woo-woo, like, no, I just start noticing people are not having as much fun as they were 20 minutes ago.
sentences.zh: 我能感觉到能量。我能感觉到，不是那种玄学，不，我只是开始注意到人们不像20分钟前那样玩得开心了。

sentences.en: And a few of the guys are stepping on each other and the ratio in the room has gotten bad and the music's not connecting with people.
sentences.zh: 几个家伙在互相踩踏，房间里的比例变差了，音乐也没有和人们产生共鸣。

sentences.en: And I'll just, I'll be like, ah, it's time to leave.
sentences.zh: 我就会说，啊，是时候离开了。

sentences.en: You know? And I think that from what I've understood in therapy and in working with people who do the research around this is children start to develop an acute sense.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？我认为从我在治疗中了解到的，以及与从事这方面研究的人一起工作所了解到的，孩子们开始发展出一种敏锐的感觉。

sentences.en: It's like a spidey sense. You know, you hear the sound of a car and you know which car is bringing danger to the house.
sentences.zh: 就像蜘蛛感应。你知道，你听到汽车的声音，你就知道哪辆车给家里带来了危险。

sentences.en: You know, I would know by the sounds of the footsteps whether or not my stepfather was sober or drunk.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我通过脚步声就能知道我的继父是清醒还是喝醉了。

sentences.en: Just by his footsteps, I knew. By the way he would close or open a door, I would know whether to be on edge or not. and so when i got that call everything in me let go like it was it was one of the most still is sort of like a painful memory you know is is like the first thought i had was damn it it happened i thought it would but not like this but it it it happened it happened yeah what is the cost you know because you described that spotty sense it almost sounds like a gift and the interesting thing to some degree it can be a gift yeah it is a gift i think every gift is a curse and i think every curse is a gift and what is the curse that comes with the gift so the curse that comes with it is i exist in a space where i am too aware of how other people feel you know and and as i've come to understand it what happens to a lot of children who are in abusive households is they develop their hypersensitivity as a tool to protect the parent because they start in the same way you were saying with your dad, why is he just sitting here?
sentences.zh: 仅仅通过他的脚步声，我就知道。通过他关门或开门的方式，我就知道是否要保持警惕。所以当我接到那个电话时，我内心的一切都崩溃了，就像它仍然是一种痛苦的记忆，你知道，第一个念头是：该死，它发生了。我以为会发生，但不是这样，但它发生了，它发生了。是的，代价是什么？因为你描述的那种蜘蛛感应听起来几乎是一种天赋，有趣的是，在某种程度上它确实可以是天赋。是的，它是一种天赋，我认为每种天赋都是一种诅咒，我认为每种诅咒都是一种天赋。那么伴随天赋而来的诅咒是什么？伴随它而来的诅咒是我存在于一个空间里，我对别人的感受太敏感了，你知道，正如我所理解的那样，很多处于虐待家庭的孩子会发展出这种高度敏感作为保护父母的工具，因为他们开始以你和你父亲的方式，为什么他只是坐在那里？

sentences.en: What happens in a household of domestic abuse is a child goes, oh, my parent does not know when danger is impending.
sentences.zh: 在家庭虐待的家庭中发生的事情是，孩子会想，哦，我的父母不知道危险即将来临。

sentences.en: And so I then need to be on alert for them.
sentences.zh: 所以我需要为他们保持警惕。

sentences.en: Because if they don't know, then I need to be alert.
sentences.zh: 因为如果他们不知道，那么我就需要警惕。

sentences.en: And if I'm alert, I can keep everybody safe.
sentences.zh: 如果我警惕，我就能保证每个人的安全。

sentences.en: And so you develop that acute sense. You develop, you know, your nervous system doesn't rest.
sentences.zh: 所以你发展出了那种敏锐的感觉。你发展出，你知道，你的神经系统不会休息。

sentences.en: I would sit in a room and I would feel the people and I still have that.
sentences.zh: 我会坐在房间里，我会感觉到人们，我仍然有那种感觉。

sentences.en: I have to like, I now have to practice letting that go.
sentences.zh: 我必须，我现在必须练习放下它。

sentences.en: And so part of it is probably why I'm a good comedian, but it's like learning when I want to use it and when I don't.
sentences.zh: 所以部分原因可能是我为什么是个好喜剧演员，但这就像学习我什么时候想用它，什么时候不想用它。

sentences.en: So learning when to ignore it. Do you have a choice?
sentences.zh: 所以学习什么时候忽略它。你有选择吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, you do. you definitely do you know i think emotions you don't really have a choice about your emotions most of the time but you do choose how you react or how it affects you.
sentences.zh: 是的，你有。你绝对有，你知道，我认为情绪，大多数时候你真的没有选择，但你确实可以选择你如何反应，或者它如何影响你。

sentences.en: And so what I'll try and do is genuinely, sometimes I'll be, even in a conversation, I practice it when it's low stakes.
sentences.zh: 所以我尝试做的是，真诚地，有时我会，即使在谈话中，我也会在风险较低时练习它。

sentences.en: I'll be with friends and I can feel the conversation getting heated and I can feel someone's gonna say something that'll hurt somebody else.
sentences.zh: 我和朋友在一起，我能感觉到谈话变得激烈，我能感觉到有人会说出伤害别人的话。

sentences.en: And then what I'll practice doing is just keeping quiet and breathing.
sentences.zh: 然后我练习做的是保持安静和呼吸。

sentences.en: Whereas what I used to do was I would jump in immediately.
sentences.zh: 而我过去常做的是我会立即跳进去。

sentences.en: I would jump, I would interrupt. I'd interrupt, you know, and I'd be like, oh, did you guys see the, and I would diffuse and I'd find a way.
sentences.zh: 我会跳，我会打断。我会打断，你知道，我会说，哦，你们看到那个了吗？我会化解，我会找到办法。

sentences.en: And I was very good at it, I still am, But now I'll just breathe and I'll be like, well, let's see where this goes.
sentences.zh: 我非常擅长，我现在仍然擅长，但现在我会呼吸，我会想，好吧，看看这会走向何方。

sentences.en: I know my friends are not going to hit each other, but I now breathe and go like, it's not my job to protect everybody.
sentences.zh: 我知道我的朋友们不会互相打架，但我现在呼吸并想，保护每个人不是我的工作。

sentences.en: And so I just try and breathe through the feeling and see how it turns out.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是试着通过呼吸来感受这种感觉，看看结果如何。

sentences.en: Sometimes I even do it as a game to see if I am right, because sometimes you're predicting what one of the outcomes and it may not be the outcome, you know, and I then trust that they can also resolve things themselves.
sentences.zh: 有时我甚至把它当作一个游戏来看看我是否正确，因为有时你在预测结果之一，而它可能不是那个结果，你知道，然后我信任他们也能自己解决问题。

sentences.en: And that's probably one of the hardest things is as a child, because as you said, you're not understanding how your father's a prisoner on this chair getting berated.
sentences.zh: 这可能是最难的事情之一，作为一个孩子，因为正如你所说，你不理解你父亲为什么像个囚犯一样坐在那张椅子上被辱骂。

sentences.en: And I, as a child, am going, I don't understand why my mother doesn't understand the danger.
sentences.zh: 而我，作为一个孩子，在想，我不明白为什么我母亲不明白危险。

sentences.en: Why doesn't she leave? And why is she even getting into a conversation with this man?
sentences.zh: 为什么她不离开？为什么她甚至要和这个男人进行谈话？

sentences.en: He's not sober. Why is this happening? Many children experience this.
sentences.zh: 他没清醒。为什么会发生这种情况？许多孩子经历过这种情况。

sentences.en: And then you then go, this person cannot protect themselves, so I have to do it for them.
sentences.zh: 然后你会想，这个人无法保护自己，所以我必须为他们做。

sentences.en: And how did you try and do that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么尝试那样做的？

sentences.en: Sometimes I would just disrupt anything.
sentences.zh: 有时我只是破坏任何事情。

sentences.en: You know, I could disrupt a conversation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我可以破坏谈话。

sentences.en: I could find a way to, you know, sort of like...
sentences.zh: 我可以找到一种方法，你知道，有点像……

sentences.en: Distracting. Yeah. You know, like Chris Pratt with those raptors in Jurassic Park.
sentences.zh: 分散注意力。是的。你知道，就像《侏罗纪公园》里克里斯·帕拉特（Chris Pratt）对付那些迅猛龙一样。

sentences.en: Just find a way to, like, snap and, you know, just pull attention. find ways to it sounds ridiculous but literally it was it was me just thinking of ways you know do you close a door that then has to be open that then alerts more people to the presence of somebody or or do you turn the tv up in this way or do you say something to him so that he you know his mood might shift in a certain way do you you know all of all of these things I was I I was thinking of.
sentences.zh: 只是找到一种方法，比如，啪，你知道，只是吸引注意力。找到方法，这听起来很荒谬，但实际上就是我想出办法，你知道，你关上一扇门，然后必须打开，这会让更多人注意到某人的存在，或者你把电视声音调大，或者你对他说些什么，这样他的情绪可能会以某种方式转变，你知道，所有这些事情我都在想。

sentences.en: And this is me thinking of these things at the age of, let's say, 9, 10, 11, 12, you know, all the way through.
sentences.zh: 这是我在9岁、10岁、11岁、12岁时想到的，你知道，一直以来。

sentences.en: And does it ever go the other way, where you're also trying to cheer up your mother at all, or take care of her spirits?
sentences.zh: 有没有反过来，你也会尝试逗你母亲开心，或者照顾她的精神？

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不。

sentences.en: I think my mother's gift and curse has always been the fact that her religion has powered her through, you know.
sentences.zh: 我认为我母亲的天赋和诅咒一直在于她的宗教信仰支撑着她度过难关，你知道。

sentences.en: And if you know somebody who's very religious, you'll know that their connection with God and their purpose pushes them through obstacles that most human beings would never be able to survive.
sentences.zh: 如果你认识一个非常虔诚的人，你会知道他们与上帝的联系和他们的目标推动他们克服了大多数人类永远无法生存的障碍。

sentences.en: Never, never, never. So there was never despair on the other side that I could feel from my mom.
sentences.zh: 永远，永远，永远。所以另一边从来没有我能从我妈妈那里感受到的绝望。

sentences.en: I never felt like I had to cheer her up. you know um the house definitely descended into like a like a doom and you could feel there was a there was a palpable sense of tension post what had happened that day you you presumably rushed to the hospital yeah um you arrived there you speak to doctors i imagine yeah did you speak to him did you did you tell the police about him did you yeah yeah i mean this is all happening and the chaos and the panic.
sentences.zh: 我从来没觉得我必须逗她开心。你知道，房子肯定陷入了一种厄运，你能感觉到那天发生的事情后有一种明显的紧张感。你大概冲到了医院，是的，你到达那里，你和医生交谈，我想，是的，你和他说过话吗？你告诉警察关于他的事了吗？你，是的，是的，我的意思是这一切都在发生，混乱和恐慌。

sentences.en: You called him. I don't remember if I called him or if he called.
sentences.zh: 你给他打了电话。我不记得是我打的还是他打的。

sentences.en: I don't remember how it happened. Did you speak to him after this event?
sentences.zh: 我不记得是怎么发生的。这件事之后你和他说过话吗？

sentences.en: No. No.
sentences.zh: 没有。没有。

sentences.en: And then you find out that there's been a bit of a miracle, I guess, because the bullet has missed all of the fatal parts of the head.
sentences.zh: 然后你发现发生了一个小小的奇迹，我想，因为子弹错过了头部所有致命的部分。

sentences.en: I mean, find out is a... It's such a... It's such a drawn out feeling and moment because, you know, time is weird in that it stands still when you're experiencing the worst of it and it flies when it's the best of it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，发现是一个……这是一个……这是一个漫长的感觉和时刻，因为，你知道，时间很奇怪，当你经历最糟糕的事情时它会静止，而当它是最好的时候它会飞逝。

sentences.en: And so that moment, even when you say the word, you do find out or go like, no, what felt like forever was us waiting for the inevitable news that, you know, my mom, our mom was dead.
sentences.zh: 所以那一刻，即使你说这个词，你确实发现了，或者说，不，感觉像是永远的是我们等待着不可避免的消息，你知道，我妈妈，我们的妈妈死了。

sentences.en: Like that seemed like the conclusion. I mean, I've watched movies, you've watched movies, someone gets shot in the head and it's over, you know?
sentences.zh: 那似乎是结论。我的意思是，我看过电影，你看过电影，有人头部中弹，然后就结束了，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So that was a, yeah, that was me grieving.
sentences.zh: 所以那是一个，是的，那是我在悲伤。

sentences.en: It's a very strange experience to have because I grieved somebody.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常奇怪的经历，因为我为某人悲伤。

sentences.en: I grieved the loss of my mother, but then she didn't die.
sentences.zh: 我为失去母亲而悲伤，但她没有死。

sentences.en: But I completely grieved her as if she was gone.
sentences.zh: 但我完全为她悲伤，好像她已经走了。

sentences.en: Like I genuinely, I cried because she was gone.
sentences.zh: 我真的，我哭了，因为她走了。

sentences.en: I didn't cry because she was hurt. I didn't, I was like, it's over.
sentences.zh: 我不是因为她受伤而哭。我不是，我当时想，结束了。

sentences.en: It's finished. Every thought ran through my head.
sentences.zh: 完成了。每一个念头都闪过我的脑海。

sentences.en: I was like, wow, I'm raising my brothers now.
sentences.zh: 我想，哇，我现在要抚养我的弟弟们了。

sentences.en: I was like, okay, I guess now I'm the head of the household.
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，我想现在我是户主了。

sentences.en: It's amazing. Like my brain spun and every day I was already now thinking 10 years ahead.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了。就像我的大脑在旋转，每一天我已经在思考10年后的事情了。

sentences.en: I was like, oh man, okay. Where, where are we living?
sentences.zh: 我想，哦天哪，好吧。我们住在哪里？

sentences.en: What are we doing? How's this going to work?
sentences.zh: 我们在做什么？这会怎么运作？

sentences.en: And you know, where's my little brother and what do I tell him?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我弟弟在哪里，我该告诉他什么？

sentences.en: And how do I, you know?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么，你知道？

sentences.en: In that moment, you, you must, you're so interesting because you get to see in that most horrific way the fragility of the most important relationship of your in your life to come out the other side and realize how fragile that because you know when you talked about our parents almost being these like presidents you also live under the assumption that they're always kind of going to be there yeah and in that moment you got to see that that's not that's not guaranteed yeah and that curse ended up being one of my greatest gifts because from that day onwards I have never seen my mother the same way.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，你，你一定，你太有趣了，因为你以最可怕的方式看到了你生命中最重要关系脆弱的一面，走出另一面并意识到它是多么脆弱，因为你知道当你谈论我们的父母几乎像总统一样时，你也生活在他们总是会一直存在的假设中，是的，在那一刻，你看到了那不是保证，是的，那个诅咒最终成为了我最大的礼物之一，因为从那天起，我再也没有以同样的方式看待我的母亲。

sentences.en: You know, I've never, like I, every time I look at her, I'm grateful that she exists.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我从来没有，每次我看着她，我都感激她存在。

sentences.en: Every time I hold her, I, like I hold her like it's the last time.
sentences.zh: 每次我拥抱她，我，就像我拥抱她，好像是最后一次。

sentences.en: She even like pushes me off sometimes. Like I hug her hard, hug her hard and I hug her for long.
sentences.zh: 她甚至有时会把我推开。就像我用力拥抱她，用力拥抱她，我拥抱了很久。

sentences.en: And I think this is extended to other people in my world, to be honest with you, is I'm very cognizant of the fact that this thing is ephemeral.
sentences.zh: 我认为这已经扩展到我世界里的其他人，老实说，我非常清楚这件事是短暂的。

sentences.en: I don't know when it'll disappear. So it has made me more appreciative of that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它什么时候会消失。所以它让我更欣赏这一点。

sentences.en: I don't assume, you know. I hope and I think there's a possibility that we will meet again, you know.
sentences.zh: 我不假设，你知道。我希望，我认为我们有再次见面的可能性，你知道。

sentences.en: But as they say in Arabic, inshallah, God willing, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 但正如阿拉伯语所说，Inshallah，上帝保佑，我不知道。

sentences.en: And it was a bit of a miracle. I was reading because you're right.
sentences.zh: 这确实有点奇迹。我当时在读，因为你是对的。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, it was. In movies, you hear someone get shot in the head, you never hear that they survive a bullet to the head.
sentences.zh: 是的，不，确实是。在电影里，你听到有人头部中弹，你永远不会听到他们能在头部中弹后幸存。

sentences.en: Whereas in your mother's case, she survived it by some...
sentences.zh: 而在你母亲的情况下，她幸存了下来，通过某种……

sentences.en: Yeah, that's where we have to go miracle.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是我们必须称之为奇迹的地方。

sentences.en: And that's where we still joke till this day, because my mom's very religious.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们至今仍在开玩笑的地方，因为我妈妈非常虔诚。

sentences.en: I grew up very religious, but very skeptical of religion or anything really.
sentences.zh: 我成长过程中非常虔诚，但对宗教或任何事情都非常怀疑。

sentences.en: And I was taught to question, ironically, by my mother.
sentences.zh: 而且具有讽刺意味的是，我被我母亲教导要质疑。

sentences.en: My mother taught me to question. She still questions things.
sentences.zh: 我母亲教导我要质疑。她仍然质疑事情。

sentences.en: She doesn't follow blindly. So I think I was in this position, and I think many of us were aware, I'm seeing what I think is the end.
sentences.zh: 她不会盲目跟随。所以我认为我处于这个位置，我想我们很多人都意识到了，我看到了我认为是终点的东西。

sentences.en: The doctors are saying to me, we're going to try what we can, but it looks terrible.
sentences.zh: 医生对我说，我们会尽力而为，但这看起来很糟糕。

sentences.en: And then we find out that the bullet entered the back of her skull, went through her head, and then exited.
sentences.zh: 然后我们发现子弹进入了她头骨的后部，穿过了她的头，然后出来了。

sentences.en: It shattered. It basically missed the bottom of the brain.
sentences.zh: 它破碎了。它基本上错过了大脑的底部。

sentences.en: You know, went past the spinal cord all the way through and then hit her cheekbone, which then deflected the bullet and then went out of her nose.
sentences.zh: 你知道，穿过了脊髓，一直穿过去，然后击中了她的颧骨，这使子弹偏转，然后从她的鼻子里出去了。

sentences.en: So it like cut off a little piece of her nose, but the exit wound wasn't as bad as it could have been.
sentences.zh: 所以它切掉了她鼻子的一小部分，但出口伤口并没有那么严重。

sentences.en: And yeah. And the doctors couldn't do anything.
sentences.zh: 是的。医生什么也做不了。

sentences.en: So there was no brain surgery. There was no opening of it.
sentences.zh: 所以没有脑部手术。没有打开它。

sentences.en: It was just stopping bleeding, closing wounds, and now praying.
sentences.zh: 只是止血，缝合伤口，现在祈祷。

sentences.en: And the doctor was the one who said miracle.
sentences.zh: 医生是那个说“奇迹”的人。

sentences.en: And he said, I hate this word because I'm a man of science and I'm a doctor.
sentences.zh: 他说，我讨厌这个词，因为我是科学人，我是医生。

sentences.en: He said, but this was a miracle. He said, this shouldn't have happened like this. and then my mom was like yeah of course of course it's a miracle and of course this is how it was going to happen she's like you know my my lord protects me so he didn't go to prison no no he didn't how how does how does that so in south africa um i don't think it's unique to south africa as well you know i've when i've traveled to other african countries i've learned this is unfortunately true the crime that a man commits against his wife or his partner isn't given the same validity as if it were committed against a stranger.
sentences.zh: 他说，但这确实是一个奇迹。他说，这不应该这样发生。然后我妈妈说，是的，当然，当然这是一个奇迹，当然事情会这样发生。她说，你知道，我的主保护我。所以他没有坐牢？不，不，他没有。这怎么，怎么会这样？在南非，嗯，我不认为这在南非是独一无二的，你知道，当我前往其他非洲国家时，我了解到这不幸是事实，一个男人对他妻子或伴侣犯下的罪行，并不像对陌生人犯下罪行那样具有同样的有效性。

sentences.en: You know, the court system doesn't treat it the same.
sentences.zh: 你知道，法院系统对待它的方式不同。

sentences.en: The law is somehow not applied with the same level of ferocity as if it were somebody else.
sentences.zh: 法律不知何故没有像对待其他人那样以同样的力度应用。

sentences.en: And so in this instance, you know, they basically ruled something to the effect of like, oh, it was his first offense, and would he repeat it or not?
sentences.zh: 所以在这个例子中，你知道，他们基本上裁定了一些类似的话，比如，哦，这是他的初犯，他会再犯吗？

sentences.en: But it's a failing of the justice system that has meant that many women in South Africa and other parts of the world don't feel like justice gets served.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种司法系统的失败，意味着南非和世界其他地区的许多女性觉得正义没有得到伸张。

sentences.en: You see it time and time again. You see it in the US all the time, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 你一次又一次地看到它。不幸的是，你在美国一直看到它。

sentences.en: You'll see man kills wife and family and themselves possibly. and the case just isn't treated with the same it's always seen as like there's like a oh something went wrong or in a you know in a tragic love affair it's always it's always labeled like that and I think that's affected our ability in society to um yeah I think to treat it the way we should when you described the miracle that that bullet traveled from the back of your mother's head through her head and then out her nose.
sentences.zh: 你会看到男人杀害妻子和家人，可能还有他们自己。而这个案件并没有得到同样的对待，它总是被视为像，哦，出了什么问题，或者在一段悲惨的爱情故事中，它总是被贴上那样的标签，我认为这影响了我们在社会中处理它的能力，嗯，我认为我们应该以我们应该的方式对待它。当你描述那个奇迹时，那颗子弹从你母亲的后脑穿过她的头，然后从她的鼻子出来。

sentences.en: It made me think about what we said at the start of the conversation about dominoes and how, in this case, millimeters change the course of your life.
sentences.zh: 这让我想到了我们在谈话开始时说的关于多米诺骨牌的事情，以及在这种情况下，毫米如何改变了你的人生轨迹。

sentences.en: Because as you say, the responsibilities you would have then had to assume.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，你当时必须承担的责任。

sentences.en: You see? Everything changes. By millimeters?
sentences.zh: 你看？一切都变了。因为毫米？

sentences.en: Yeah, everything changes. I probably don't move to America.
sentences.zh: 是的，一切都变了。我可能不会搬到美国。

sentences.en: I don't explore the world in the same way i i take on a whole different role in my life everything changes what about anger towards him towards abel oh geez yeah that's that's been a tough one for me because i i because i experienced every emotion you know i talk about it in my book like i i have experienced every emotion because i mean fear was the first one the idea that this person could take away you know the life of of someone who arguably I loved the most.
sentences.zh: 我不会以同样的方式探索世界，我在生活中扮演了完全不同的角色，一切都变了。那么对他的愤怒呢？对Abel的愤怒？哦，天哪，是的，那对我来说一直是个难题，因为我经历了每一种情绪，你知道，我在书里谈到了它，就像我经历了每一种情绪，因为我的意思是恐惧是第一个，这个想法是这个人可能会夺走，你知道，一个可以说我最爱的人的生命。

sentences.en: Then like rage, helplessness, even like shame, feeling like I didn't protect her.
sentences.zh: 然后是愤怒，无助，甚至像羞耻，觉得我没有保护她。

sentences.en: Because I knew from the beginning. Literally, I write about this in the book.
sentences.zh: 因为我从一开始就知道。字面上，我在书里写到了这一点。

sentences.en: My grandmother would tell us stories of how, because she had the best memory in the family.
sentences.zh: 我祖母会给我们讲故事，因为她是家里记忆力最好的人。

sentences.en: She would tell us stories of how when I was young, when my mom first met my stepdad, she, like I was saying to the family, I was like, this guy's great and everything, but I don't think this is a good idea.
sentences.zh: 她会给我们讲故事，当我年轻时，当我妈妈第一次见到我继父时，她，就像我说的，我对家人说，我当时说，这家伙很棒，什么都好，但我不认为这是个好主意。

sentences.en: I don't think he's a good man. I don't think we should trust him.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他是个好人。我不认为我们应该信任他。

sentences.en: I was saying this as a child. You know, and the one thing that I think confuses people sometimes when it comes to domestic abuse is that we think of it as a binary.
sentences.zh: 我还是个孩子时就这么说了。你知道，我认为在涉及家庭虐待时，人们有时会感到困惑的一件事是，我们认为它是二元的。

sentences.en: You know, so people go like, how can these bad men live these lives?
sentences.zh: 所以人们会说，这些坏男人怎么能过这样的生活？

sentences.en: But we don't realize that oftentimes the moment of bad is the explosion. but everything around it is charisma and charm and jokes.
sentences.zh: 但我们没有意识到，往往坏的时刻就是爆炸。但周围的一切都是魅力、魅力和笑话。

sentences.en: And I laughed with this man most of my life.
sentences.zh: 我一生中大部分时间都和他一起笑。

sentences.en: I had some of my favorite experiences with him as a human being.
sentences.zh: 我作为一个人和他有过一些我最喜欢的经历。

sentences.en: When he was wonderful, he was the most wonderful human being you'd ever meet.
sentences.zh: 当他很棒的时候，他是你见过的最棒的人。

sentences.en: And it took me a while to understand how to how to consolidate those ideas, how to, you know, how to resolve the fact that somebody who you love, someone who treated you with respect and joy in some moments was also the person who brought you the most pain, you know?
sentences.zh: 我花了一段时间才明白如何整合这些想法，如何，你知道，如何解决这样一个事实：一个你爱的人，一个在某些时刻以尊重和快乐对待你的人，也是给你带来最大痛苦的人，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So I definitely, anger was like a big one for me.
sentences.zh: 所以我绝对，愤怒对我来说是一个很大的问题。

sentences.en: I thought everything, anger at myself, anger at my mom for staying to the point that that could happen.
sentences.zh: 我想到了一切，对自己愤怒，对妈妈留下来直到发生那种事感到愤怒。

sentences.en: Anger at him, anger at the system for not protecting, anger just everywhere.
sentences.zh: 对他愤怒，对系统没有保护感到愤怒，愤怒无处不在。

sentences.en: And then anger dipping into pain and anguish and then crying it out and then being angry again and then being scared and then just going through waves and waves and waves of that.
sentences.zh: 然后愤怒陷入痛苦和苦恼，然后哭出来，然后再次愤怒，然后害怕，然后经历一波又一波的浪潮。

sentences.en: And so that was a lot of my time in therapy and a lot of my time having conversations with my mom.
sentences.zh: 所以那是我在治疗中花费的很多时间，也是我和我妈妈进行很多对话的时间。

sentences.en: And my mom would always say to me, she'd be like, you know, over time you learn to forgive.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈总是对我说，她会说，你知道，随着时间的推移，你学会了宽恕。

sentences.en: And I was like, I don't think I could ever forgive.
sentences.zh: 我说，我不认为我能宽恕。

sentences.en: And she was like, yeah, she's like, but, you know, forgiving doesn't mean forgetting.
sentences.zh: 她说，是的，她说，但是，你知道，宽恕并不意味着忘记。

sentences.en: It means letting go of the thing that the person is holding of you as opposed to, you know, it's not you letting them into your life.
sentences.zh: 这意味着放下那个人对你持有的东西，而不是，你知道，这不是你让他们进入你的生活。

sentences.en: It's not, it's just going like, yeah, that happened.
sentences.zh: 不是，这只是说，是的，那件事发生了。

sentences.en: I feel for them. I understand many of the things that made them do what they did. and then trying to let go of that anger that's like burning inside you, that rage.
sentences.zh: 我同情他们。我理解很多导致他们做出那些行为的原因。然后我试着放下内心燃烧的那种愤怒，那种狂怒。

sentences.en: And I'm glad my mom did that because in the years since, you know, I've spent more time reading about domestic abuse and learning about domestic abuse and speaking to experts about it.
sentences.zh: 我很庆幸我妈妈那样做了，因为在随后的几年里，我花了很多时间阅读关于家庭暴力的资料，了解家庭暴力，并与相关专家探讨过这个问题。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, there's a reason there's a vicious cycle.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，恶性循环是有原因的。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of young boys who grow up in homes where their moms are abused grow up to then become abusers themselves, even though they hated the very idea of what they were experiencing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多在母亲遭受虐待的家庭中长大的小男孩，长大后自己也成了施暴者，尽管他们内心非常痛恨自己所经历的一切。

sentences.en: And so to your point, I think it's because of that now unreleased and unrealized anger that they didn't get to express when they were children because they weren't safe.
sentences.zh: 所以回到你的观点，我认为这是因为他们小时候因为缺乏安全感而无法表达，导致那种愤怒至今未得到释放和化解。

sentences.en: And then now at some point it comes out of them.
sentences.zh: 然后到了某个时刻，这种情绪就爆发出来了。

sentences.en: And so I genuinely had to deal with that.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实不得不去面对这一点。

sentences.en: I had to even accept the idea that I was as angry as I was, angry and helpless, which is a terrible combination for a human being to experience.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不得不接受这样一个事实：我曾经那么愤怒，既愤怒又无助，这对一个人来说是一种极其糟糕的体验。

sentences.en: Have you forgiven him? I think in moments, yes, I think I have.
sentences.zh: 你原谅他了吗？我想在某些时刻，是的，我想我已经原谅了。

sentences.en: I think the levels of my forgiveness won't reach my mom's because she was in love with him.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我原谅的程度不会达到我妈妈那种地步，因为她曾经深爱过他。

sentences.en: You know, to me, this was still a person who came into my life.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对我来说，他依然只是一个出现在我生命中的人。

sentences.en: You know, he's not my biological father.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他不是我的亲生父亲。

sentences.en: So I think my, I don't think I've ever reached like the level of like pure, like, I forgive you.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，我不觉得我达到了那种纯粹的“我原谅你了”的境界。

sentences.en: But I do understand. You know, I think I understand a lot of it.
sentences.zh: 但我确实理解。你知道，我想我理解其中的很多缘由。

sentences.en: I think I feel sorry for him I think I Yeah, I've learned to come to terms with it But like pure forgiveness I'd be lying to you if I'm like Yeah, I'm forgiven I'm like, no, I think so sometimes And then other times I go like No, actually I don't That experience has left fingerprints on you in some way Oh, definitely And how do those fingerprints still show up today In your day-to-day life, in your profession?
sentences.zh: 我想我为他感到难过，我想，是的，我已经学会了接受这一切。但说到纯粹的原谅，如果我说“是的，我原谅了”，那是在骗你。我会说，不，有时候我觉得是，但另一些时候我又会想，不，其实我没有。那种经历在某种程度上给你留下了烙印。噢，绝对是。那么这些烙印今天是如何显现的呢？在你的日常生活中，在你的职业生涯中？

sentences.en: Oh, I wouldn't know the answer to that question.
sentences.zh: 噢，我不知道该怎么回答这个问题。

sentences.en: Because the strange thing, again, I think about the mind, is that the things that affect us sometimes may not be the things that are as obvious to us as we may think.
sentences.zh: 因为关于思维，奇怪的一点是，那些影响我们的事情，有时可能并不像我们想象中那样显而易见。

sentences.en: You know, you can get into a car accident and experience an acute trauma and you know how this affects you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可能会遭遇车祸并经历严重的创伤，你知道这会如何影响你。

sentences.en: And you'll be shocked that many of the other things you're dealing with in your life where you're struggling aren't actually from that car accident.
sentences.zh: 但你会惊讶地发现，你生活中正在应对和挣扎的许多其他事情，其实并不是源于那场车祸。

sentences.en: They're from like the minute moments in your life where somebody rejected you.
sentences.zh: 它们源于你生命中那些微小的时刻，比如有人拒绝了你。

sentences.en: You weren't chosen to play on a team as a kid.
sentences.zh: 小时候你没被选入球队。

sentences.en: You failed a test. You were bullied. And I don't say this like dismissively.
sentences.zh: 你考试不及格。你被霸凌了。我这么说并不是为了轻描淡写。

sentences.en: I say it cautiously. I go like, oh, I would be careful to put all of it on that moment because in a weird way, that moment was contained.
sentences.zh: 我是谨慎地表达。我会想，噢，我会小心不要把一切都归咎于那一刻，因为从某种奇怪的角度来看，那一刻是孤立的。

sentences.en: It came with many other instances. But yeah, as I've sat and explored myself and my brain and my mind in therapy, I've realized that some of the things that you think will affect you the most might not.
sentences.zh: 它伴随着许多其他事件。但确实，当我坐在那里，在心理治疗中探索自我、大脑和思想时，我意识到，有些你认为会影响你最深的事情，可能并不会。

sentences.en: They might stay in that world. And then there's all these other things that affect you way more than you would ever think they even have the right to.
sentences.zh: 它们可能就停留在那个世界里。而另一些你根本没想过会有那么大影响的事情，却对你产生了深远的影响。

sentences.en: So I wouldn't know, to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 所以老实说，我不知道。

sentences.en: I wouldn't be able to say to you, oh, I'm like this because of that, or I'm like that because of that.
sentences.zh: 我无法告诉你，噢，我变成这样是因为那个，或者我变成那样是因为这个。

sentences.en: No, I do think I appreciate people more.
sentences.zh: 不，我确实认为我更懂得欣赏他人了。

sentences.en: I'm very present when I'm with my loved ones.
sentences.zh: 和爱的人在一起时，我非常专注。

sentences.en: Um, yeah, but other than that, I couldn't give you a concrete answer that would be, that would be genuine.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，但除此之外，我无法给出一个具体且真诚的答案。

sentences.en: You said something about young men struggling, which is, um, came to mind as you're talking about you being that young man who seemed to be quite confused with a variety of emotions and, um, less experience about what the correct outlets were for those emotions.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到年轻人挣扎的问题，这让我想起你谈到自己曾经也是那个年轻人，似乎对各种情绪感到困惑，而且对于如何正确宣泄这些情绪缺乏经验。

sentences.en: You said recently, in fact, one of the big things I've been worried about recently is young men and how angry they've become, how alone they've become, how isolated they've become.
sentences.zh: 你最近提到，事实上，我最近担心的一大问题就是年轻人，他们变得多么愤怒，多么孤独，多么与世隔绝。

sentences.en: And then ironically, how they've turned anger, isolation into a community.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，他们又如何将愤怒和孤立变成了一种群体认同。

sentences.en: There's a couple of words there that seem to fit the shoe that would go on your foot.
sentences.zh: 那里有几个词似乎很适合描述你曾经的处境。

sentences.en: Anger, isolation, as a young man. Loneliness.
sentences.zh: 愤怒，孤立，作为一个年轻人。孤独。

sentences.en: Can you relate to what young men are going through in the sort of modern world today? because the stats on young men are quite shocking.
sentences.zh: 你能感同身受当今现代世界中年轻人所经历的一切吗？因为关于年轻人的统计数据相当令人震惊。

sentences.en: Yeah. The mental health stats, the suicidality stats, the depression stats, the stats around purposelessness.
sentences.zh: 是的。心理健康数据、自杀率数据、抑郁症数据，以及关于缺乏目标的数据。

sentences.en: And I wanted to know how you're looking at young men today.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是如何看待当今的年轻人的。

sentences.en: I get asked all the time by people that listen to the show.
sentences.zh: 我经常被听节目的听众问到。

sentences.en: They say they've got a young son and the son is struggling.
sentences.zh: 他们说他们有个正在挣扎的年轻儿子。

sentences.en: They don't know who they are, where they belong, what their purpose is.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道自己是谁，属于哪里，人生目标是什么。

sentences.en: How to make friends is a big one. What are you seeing when you look out into the world, the state of young men?
sentences.zh: 如何交朋友也是个大问题。当你放眼世界，看到年轻人的现状时，你看到了什么？

sentences.en: So I think I can empathize with a lot of it. and I think I can relate to some of it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我能对其中的很多感受产生共鸣。而且我想我能理解其中的一部分。

sentences.en: But on my side, you know, other than the anger, let's say, I wasn't isolated.
sentences.zh: 但在我这边，你知道，除了愤怒之外，可以说，我并没有被孤立。

sentences.en: I didn't feel isolated at all. Because I got to play with other kids and because I was with other kids and because I had my cousins and everybody, I never felt isolated, you know.
sentences.zh: 我一点也不觉得孤立。因为我有机会和其他孩子一起玩，因为我和其他孩子在一起，因为我有表兄弟姐妹和大家在一起，我从未感到孤立，你知道。

sentences.en: So even when I was talking to you about my grandmother, I think you used isolated, but I didn't because I genuinely never perceived it as that because I was in the home with people.
sentences.zh: 所以即使当我跟你谈到我祖母时，我想你用了“孤立”这个词，但我没有，因为我真的从未那样感知过，因为我一直和人们生活在一起。

sentences.en: It's just they were grannies. So do you get what I'm saying?
sentences.zh: 只是他们是祖母辈的。所以你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: So I didn't feel like isolated in that way.
sentences.zh: 所以我并没有那种意义上的孤立感。

sentences.en: Definitely felt like an outsider though, which is a different feeling that's adjacent.
sentences.zh: 不过我确实感觉像个局外人，这是一种不同的、但又相近的感觉。

sentences.en: I think it occupies the same lexical field, but it isn't the exact same thing.
sentences.zh: 我认为它占据了相同的词汇领域，但并不是完全一样的东西。

sentences.en: You know, because isolation, I think, can come with it like a certain solitude and a certain, you know, a feeling of like knowing that you are in this thing alone because you are in this thing alone.
sentences.zh: 你知道，因为我认为孤立可能伴随着某种孤独，以及某种你知道自己独自承受这一切的感觉，因为你确实是独自一人。

sentences.en: But then being an outsider is a different, you know, it's a different type of torture.
sentences.zh: 但作为局外人是另一种，你知道，是另一种折磨。

sentences.en: And I think that's maybe what a lot of men are experiencing that I can relate to.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能就是许多男人正在经历的，我能感同身受。

sentences.en: I think for a long time, we've lived in a world where we've told people what they're supposed to do, how they're supposed to do it.
sentences.zh: 我认为很长一段时间以来，我们生活在一个告诉人们应该做什么、应该怎么做的世界里。

sentences.en: And it was sort of easily realized, right?
sentences.zh: 而且这很容易实现，对吧？

sentences.en: And now I'm not a historian. I don't know every, you know, history that we've gone through.
sentences.zh: 我不是历史学家。我不知道我们经历过的每一段历史。

sentences.en: But from the little that I've read and from the historians that I have spoken to, you know, society goes in these waves and we move through these waves.
sentences.zh: 但从我读过的有限资料和与历史学家的交谈中，你知道，社会是呈波浪式发展的，我们随着这些浪潮前进。

sentences.en: And I think we shouldn't take for granted now that there was a whole generation of young men who were given a purpose by war, a lot of war.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们现在不应该想当然地认为，曾经有一整代年轻人被战争赋予了目标，很多战争。

sentences.en: And war is one of the most powerful thrusts of purpose that a nation will ever experience.
sentences.zh: 而战争是一个国家所能经历的最强大的目标推动力之一。

sentences.en: Young men are told what they're supposed to be doing.
sentences.zh: 年轻人被告知他们应该做什么。

sentences.en: Your country needs you. You need to go and fight, young man.
sentences.zh: 你的国家需要你。年轻人，你需要去战斗。

sentences.en: You need to protect this country. and you're like, I need to protect this country.
sentences.zh: 你需要保卫这个国家。然后你会想，我需要保卫这个国家。

sentences.en: Now, even if you don't want to dodge the draft, you've been given a purpose in a strange way.
sentences.zh: 现在，即使你不想逃避征兵，你也以一种奇怪的方式被赋予了目标。

sentences.en: Even if you're like, I'm anti-war, now you have a purpose.
sentences.zh: 即使你觉得，我是反战的，现在你也有了目标。

sentences.en: Your purpose is to be against the war. Your purpose is to oppose the war.
sentences.zh: 你的目标是反对战争。你的目标是抵制战争。

sentences.en: Your purpose is to spread love and peace.
sentences.zh: 你的目标是传播爱与和平。

sentences.en: The other person's purpose is to survive the war.
sentences.zh: 另一个人的目标是在战争中幸存。

sentences.en: Another person's purpose is to win at the war, but you have a purpose and that purpose is powerful and it propels nations forward.
sentences.zh: 另一个人的目标是在战争中获胜，但你确实有一个目标，而那个目标是强大的，它推动着国家前进。

sentences.en: And then you enter into a period of what we would argue is relative peace.
sentences.zh: 然后你进入了一个我们称之为相对和平的时期。

sentences.en: And I say relative because there are many parts of the world where there are just like these constant chronic wars that are waging.
sentences.zh: 我说相对，是因为世界上许多地方仍然存在着持续不断的慢性战争。

sentences.en: But for most people, what are you doing?
sentences.zh: 但对大多数人来说，你在做什么呢？

sentences.en: You know, you're sitting in a world where there is no draft and there is no imminent war.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你坐在一个没有征兵、没有迫在眉睫的战争的世界里。

sentences.en: And it's a choice now. Do you want to go to the military or do you not?
sentences.zh: 现在这成了一种选择。你想去参军还是不想？

sentences.en: And you don't have to. And then also, things aren't just given to you.
sentences.zh: 你不必去。而且，事情也不再是直接给你的。

sentences.en: You know, before when your parents were like, go get a job, it meant there was a job to get.
sentences.zh: 你知道，以前当你的父母说，去弄份工作，那意味着确实有工作可做。

sentences.en: If your parents were like, go get a job, you could, it was almost harder to not get a job back in the day than it is now in a strange way.
sentences.zh: 如果你的父母说，去弄份工作，你就能做到，从某种奇怪的角度来看，过去想要找不到工作比现在还要难。

sentences.en: Because it was just like this thing you do, it was doing.
sentences.zh: 因为它就是你该做的事，它就是一种行为。

sentences.en: I sweep, I clean, I collect, I fix. It was so simple.
sentences.zh: 我扫地、我清洁、我收集、我修理。就是这么简单。

sentences.en: And I think now we're living in a world where many young men are experiencing a purposelessness because it's sort of like not laid out in any way, shape or form.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在我们生活在一个许多年轻人感到迷茫的世界里，因为生活似乎没有任何形式或结构的规划。

sentences.en: And I think we've created such a narrow scope of what people can do or can't do, or, you know, like we've rewarded so few things that I think we've exacerbated the problem.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们把人们能做或不能做的事情范围缩小得太窄了，或者说，我们奖励的事情太少了，以至于我认为我们加剧了这个问题。

sentences.en: You know, gone are the times when being a painter, a philosopher a you know some sort of artisan is like celebrated in that way you know gone are the days where skills are passed down from generation to generation and it seems like that that's that's less and less becoming a thing and I from from from what I've been told a lot of it can be tracked back to like industrialization and this consolidation of of manufacturing you know so an interesting point of this as you were talking was is because more women are graduating with college degrees and because of the equality movement that's meant that men and women now are both in the workforce at high level positions i mean even in that there's going to be less jobs available for those men who would clearly before in the past have yeah they would just have the job yeah yeah and also there's this really interesting thing that a lady was talking about my podcast where she said that um there's still a stigma in society that a man is to be the provider yes but in a world where they're less able to get those top jobs to provide and women are earning more which no one's got an issue with it all um not no one not no one yeah yeah some people have an issue with that that's true i don't have an issue i don't think you do but um but it they were referring to it as the you could say the short man problem or the tall girl problem where effectively they were saying that women want to date up into the right which has been shown in the surveys but there's less people up to the right now and this is so and there was another survey that said 70 or 80 percent of women want their husband to be a provider but math the math doesn't math here because there isn't that many men up there anymore so and when you look at the dating stats the sex stats right age in which men lose their virginity now the amount of men that haven't had sex in the last year it effectively looks like just the top 10 percent of men having all the fun and the bottom 50 percent have been right disenfranchised by the system yeah but i so i i i think about this all the time and i you know i try and spend as much time reading thinking and discussing with people who are far more brilliant than I'll ever be.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那种崇尚画家、哲学家或某种工匠的时代已经一去不复返了，你知道，那种技能代代相传的日子已经过去了，这似乎越来越少见了。据我所知，这很大程度上可以追溯到工业化和制造业的整合。你知道，当你谈到这一点时，一个有趣的观点是，因为越来越多的女性获得了大学学位，因为平权运动，这意味着男性和女性现在都在高层职位上工作。我的意思是，即使在这一点上，对于那些过去显然会得到工作的男性来说，工作岗位也会变少。是的，他们本来就会有工作。是的，而且还有一件非常有趣的事情，一位女士在我的播客中谈到，她说社会上仍然存在一种污名，认为男人应该是供养者。是的，但在一个他们越来越难以获得那些高薪职位来供养家庭，而女性收入更高——没人对此有意见，真的，不是没人，不是没人，是的，有些人确实有意见，这是真的。我没意见，我想你也没有。但他们将其称为“矮个男人的问题”或“高个女人的问题”，实际上他们是说女性想要向上和向右寻找伴侣，这在调查中已经显示出来了，但现在向上和向右的人变少了。所以，还有另一项调查显示，70%或80%的女性希望丈夫是供养者，但数学逻辑在这里行不通，因为上面没有那么多男人了。所以，当你查看约会统计数据、性行为统计数据时，比如男性失去童贞的年龄，过去一年没有发生性行为的男性比例，看起来实际上只有前10%的男性在享受这一切，而底层50%的人被系统剥夺了权利。是的，但我一直都在思考这个问题，我试着花尽可能多的时间阅读、思考，并与那些远比我聪明得多的人讨论。

sentences.en: And what I've come to realize is we may now be experiencing a culmination of the dominoes.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，我们现在可能正在经历多米诺骨牌效应的顶点。

sentences.en: We're experiencing the dominoes of a declining middle class and governments around the world no longer propping up the middle class because anyone who's real about economics knows that the middle class is an invented thing really.
sentences.zh: 我们正在经历中产阶级衰落的多米诺骨牌，世界各地的政府不再支撑中产阶级，因为任何真正了解经济学的人都知道，中产阶级实际上是一个被发明出来的东西。

sentences.en: And it's governments actively saying, we're going to create it.
sentences.zh: 这是政府主动说，我们要创造它。

sentences.en: So as that has declined over time and people have sort of created this illusion that no, everyone can just get there on their own merit and like nothing needs to be created for you.
sentences.zh: 所以随着时间的推移，这种支撑减少了，人们创造了一种错觉，认为每个人都能凭自己的能力达到那里，不需要为你创造什么。

sentences.en: We've seen the middle class decline. What happens then is there's a gap, you know, between the rich and the poor.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了中产阶级的衰落。接下来发生的是，你知道，贫富之间出现了差距。

sentences.en: Then there's another domino that falls and it's like the consolidation of wealth.
sentences.zh: 然后另一张多米诺骨牌倒下了，那就是财富的集中。

sentences.en: You know, these mega corporations around the world that find ways to not pay taxes, that find ways to pay like slave wages to some people and then sell you a cheap product and then give you credit that you shouldn't get and then put you in a debt cycle that you shouldn't be in And that's one domino, you know, and then politics becomes more polarized and more extreme because of algorithms and the way we say that's another domino.
sentences.zh: 你知道，世界各地的这些巨型企业，它们想方设法不交税，想方设法给一些人支付奴隶般的工资，然后卖给你廉价产品，再给你提供你不该得到的信贷，然后把你拖入你不该陷入的债务循环。这是一张骨牌，你知道，然后政治变得更加两极分化，更加极端，因为算法和我们说话的方式，那是另一张骨牌。

sentences.en: That's another domino. That's another domino.
sentences.zh: 那是另一张骨牌。那是另一张骨牌。

sentences.en: That's another domino. Companies find ways, as you said, to hire fewer people to get more out of them or hire different people.
sentences.zh: 那是另一张骨牌。正如你所说，公司想方设法雇佣更少的人来榨取更多价值，或者雇佣不同的人。

sentences.en: That's another domino. And in a strange way, I think of this sometimes.
sentences.zh: 那是另一张骨牌。以一种奇怪的方式，我有时会这样想。

sentences.en: I go, you see gifts and curses.
sentences.zh: 我说，你看到了天赋和诅咒。

sentences.en: This is purely anecdotal in my life. It's not research, but I'm willing to bet on this and I'm willing to stand by it.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是我生活中的轶事。这不是研究，但我敢打赌，我愿意坚持这个观点。

sentences.en: One of the curses that women experience because of being pushed out of the workplace and being like forced to stay at home and for such a long time was they learned how to find purpose in what most people would consider mundane and maybe even meaningless. you know women have found ways to like fill their time with community and with connecting and they found ways to like look after their bodies and and work out and do things and it's different in different communities like knitting clubs book clubs and just just think about that it's like it takes up your time it gives you a purpose we're going to read this book and then we're going to discuss it and we I mean fundamentally it's nothing but it's something you know and it drives you forward it makes you feel like you're supposed to be somewhere you're supposed to doing you're supposed to be doing something.
sentences.zh: 女性因为被挤出职场、被迫长期呆在家里而经历的诅咒之一，就是她们学会了如何在大多数人认为平凡甚至毫无意义的事情中找到目标。你知道，女性找到了用社区和人际连接来填补时间的方法，她们找到了照顾身体、锻炼和做事情的方法。在不同的社区里情况不同，比如编织俱乐部、读书俱乐部，只要想想看，这占据了你的时间，给了你一个目标。我们要读这本书，然后我们要讨论它，我的意思是，从根本上说，这没什么，但它确实是某种东西，你知道，它推动你前进，让你觉得你应该身处某地，你应该正在做某事。

sentences.en: And then when the workplace opened up, the women are like, oh, we can go and work as well.
sentences.zh: 然后当职场开放时，女性说，噢，我们也可以去工作。
