sentences.en: And, you know, I don't know about you, but in school, all the girls were smarter than we were in class anyway.
sentences.zh: 而且，我不知道你怎么样，但在学校里，班上的女生本来就比我们聪明。

sentences.en: And so now they're comfortably working, especially in an office environment, which was sort of like designed perfectly for them in that way.
sentences.zh: 所以现在她们可以舒适地工作，特别是在办公室环境中，这在某种程度上是为她们完美设计的。

sentences.en: And then guys, I think we haven't practiced that.
sentences.zh: 然后对于男生，我认为我们没有练习过这一点。

sentences.en: I don't know many guys, I don't know about you, I don't know about, I don't know many guys who know how to just sit with their male friends and just be, not do a thing, be, like just be.
sentences.zh: 我认识的男生不多，我不知道你怎么样，我不知道，我认识的男生里没几个知道如何只是和男性朋友坐在一起，什么都不做，只是存在着，就像只是存在着。

sentences.en: And I, and I find, and I, you know, I, I'll be careful in saying this, but I have found that it, the, the, the degree of comfort in just being is, is different depending on where you're from in the world.
sentences.zh: 而且我发现，我说话会谨慎一点，但我发现，这种“只是存在”的舒适度，取决于你来自世界的哪个地方。

sentences.en: So like my friends who are from third world countries, developing nations, you know, whether it's South Africa and we're in the township, or whether it's my friends from Trinidad, which my...
sentences.zh: 所以，比如我那些来自第三世界国家、发展中国家的朋友，你知道，无论是在南非的乡镇，还是我来自特立尼达的朋友，我的……

sentences.en: Like in Trinidad, they even have a word for it, liming, they say.
sentences.zh: 比如在特立尼达，他们甚至有一个词来形容，叫“liming”。

sentences.en: They say, let's lime. And liming means spending time together with no purpose whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 他们说，让我们去“lime”。而“liming”的意思就是毫无目的地消磨时间。

sentences.en: That's literally what my Trinidad friends said.
sentences.zh: 这字面上就是我特立尼达朋友说的。

sentences.en: They're like, yo, we're going to lime on Saturday.
sentences.zh: 他们说，嘿，我们周六要去“lime”。

sentences.en: That means we're doing nothing. It doesn't mean we're going to go see a game.
sentences.zh: 那意味着我们什么都不做。这并不意味着我们要去看比赛。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean we're going to watch a movie.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着我们要去看电影。

sentences.en: We're going to lime. It means your friend is going to come.
sentences.zh: 我们要去“lime”。这意味着你的朋友会过来。

sentences.en: They're going to sit on the couch and you're just going to be.
sentences.zh: 他们会坐在沙发上，你们就只是待着。

sentences.en: You'll talk and then you won't talk and then you laugh and then you won't laugh.
sentences.zh: 你们会说话，然后又不说话，然后你们笑，然后又不笑。

sentences.en: And I don't know about you, but I feel like guys are, we're not as good at that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你怎么样，但我感觉男生们，我们不太擅长这个。

sentences.en: You know, like I read something the other day that was great and was talking about how guys always need the third thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，前几天我读到一些很棒的内容，谈到男生总是需要“第三样东西”。

sentences.en: There's always the third thing. There's you, there's me and there's the third thing.
sentences.zh: 总是有第三样东西。有你，有我，还有第三样东西。

sentences.en: Hey, what are you doing on Saturday? Why don't we, we want to go fishing.
sentences.zh: 嘿，你周六做什么？我们为什么不去钓鱼？

sentences.en: It's like, why do we need the fishing? Why can't we just sit like this and be like, hey, what's happening in your heart, Stephen?
sentences.zh: 就像是，为什么我们需要钓鱼？为什么我们不能就这样坐着，然后说，嘿，Stephen，你心里在想什么？

sentences.en: What's what's going on? What's happening in my heart?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？我心里在想什么？

sentences.en: Or let me tell you what's going on. Women can do that.
sentences.zh: 或者让我告诉你发生了什么。女性可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: And some may argue that it's, you know, maybe they've been genetically coded.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能会争辩说，你知道，也许她们在基因上就被编码了。

sentences.en: But I also think they've been forced to practice that because men were like, you can't come to the, you know, the factory, the office, everything for so long.
sentences.zh: 但我认为她们也是被迫练习的，因为男人长期以来一直说，你不能来工厂、办公室，什么都不能做。

sentences.en: And then women are like, all right. And I think that's another thing that men are struggling with.
sentences.zh: 然后女性说，好吧。我认为这是男人正在挣扎的另一件事。

sentences.en: But it's not like their fault. It's the dominoes.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是他们的错。这是多米诺骨牌效应。

sentences.en: When I was young, we used to go to the mall.
sentences.zh: 我小时候，我们常去商场。

sentences.en: We used to go to the mall and we'd hang out with other kids.
sentences.zh: 我们常去商场，和别的孩子一起玩。

sentences.en: And then now malls aren't really a thing.
sentences.zh: 但现在商场已经不怎么流行了。

sentences.en: And then kids don't really hang out anywhere.
sentences.zh: 孩子们也不怎么在外面玩了。

sentences.en: And everything's become about money and transactions.
sentences.zh: 一切都变成了关于金钱和交易。

sentences.en: Think about how few places you can go to connect with people without money now.
sentences.zh: 想想看，现在有多少地方你可以不用花钱就能和人建立联系。

sentences.en: You know what I mean? But when I was growing up, it was quite common.
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？但我成长的时候，这很常见。

sentences.en: You just went and you hung out with other kids.
sentences.zh: 你只是走出去，和其他孩子一起玩。

sentences.en: And that was just what you did. It didn't involve money.
sentences.zh: 那就是你做的事。它不涉及金钱。

sentences.en: And I think we're starting to experience that domino affecting society now.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们现在开始经历那种多米诺骨牌效应影响社会了。

sentences.en: Do you have money for a video game console?
sentences.zh: 你有钱买游戏机吗？

sentences.en: No. Oh, then you can't meet up with your friends on Fortnite. right?
sentences.zh: 没有。噢，那你不能在Fortnite上和朋友见面了，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, do you have money to go to a movie?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你有钱去看电影吗？

sentences.en: No, you don't. Oh, and movies have gone up.
sentences.zh: 没有，你没有。噢，而且电影票价涨了。

sentences.en: Yeah, you can't hang out with your friends at the movies.
sentences.zh: 是的，你不能和朋友在电影院聚会了。

sentences.en: Can you afford an Uber ride? No, you can't.
sentences.zh: 你付得起Uber车费吗？不，你付不起。

sentences.en: Can you? All these things now have meant that I think we're experiencing a generation of men in particular, who are not just isolated, but not practiced in the arts of just like connecting with another male for no other purpose than to just like share hearts and be human beings.
sentences.zh: 你能吗？所有这些事情现在意味着，我认为我们正在经历一代男性，他们不仅是被孤立的，而且没有练习过那种仅仅为了分享内心、作为人类而与另一个男性建立联系的艺术。

sentences.en: I've heard you talk about how you think we're a sort of continuation of our ancestors and their sort of legacy.
sentences.zh: 我听你谈过，你认为我们是祖先及其遗产的一种延续。

sentences.en: I've heard you talk about this before, and as you were saying about this idea that women are able to connect without the third thing, it made me think, you know, I think a lot of women have had that modeled by the generation that came before them.
sentences.zh: 我以前听你谈过这个，当你谈到女性能够在没有“第三样东西”的情况下建立联系时，这让我想起，你知道，我认为很多女性通过上一代人获得了这种示范。

sentences.en: Yeah. Whereas, I don't know about you, but I didn't have that modeled in my house.
sentences.zh: 是的。然而，我不知道你怎么样，但我家里没有这种示范。

sentences.en: I never saw my dad sit with a guy and talk to me.
sentences.zh: 我从未见过我父亲和一个男人坐下来和我谈话。

sentences.en: But that's what I mean. He didn't even talk to us.
sentences.zh: 但我指的就是这个。他甚至不跟我们说话。

sentences.en: We didn't even have those conversations.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至没有过那些对话。

sentences.en: That's what I mean. I call him by his first name.

sentences.en: It's not safe. Yeah, so you don't want to be there.

sentences.en: And so I think that's another place where young men struggle is like, we have to maintain this bravado.

sentences.en: And then we see all these influences online who keep telling us like, yeah, you're a tough guy.

sentences.en: And so they can be the worst of themselves.

sentences.zh: 但我认为礼物也是这种匿名性。你知道，我想很多人会惊讶于你如何在网上以一种非常真诚和美好的方式与人建立联系，因为在某种程度上你更安全。

sentences.en: You know, I've made some of my best friends playing like Warzone. you know, when like when the pandemic hits, I was like, everyone was playing Wars on, I was like, I'll jump on, not really like an FPS guy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在玩《Warzone》的时候交到了我最好的几个朋友。你知道，疫情刚开始的时候，每个人都在玩《Warzone》，我就想，我也加入吧，虽然我不太擅长射击游戏。

sentences.en: And I jumped on and I was decent at it, but I made friends playing this game and would talk to people and you'd regularly meet with them.
sentences.zh: 我加入了，玩得还凑合，但我通过这个游戏交到了朋友，会和人聊天，还会经常和他们见面。

sentences.en: And some people were assholes, but a lot of them weren't.

sentences.zh: 那些不是混蛋的人，我会再联系他们，然后我们一起玩。

sentences.en: And then it goes from talking about the game and talking about your loadouts.
sentences.zh: 然后话题就从讨论游戏和装备配置，变成了讨论家庭、生活、近况、这一周过得怎么样、工作如何、老板怎么样、那个升职机会等等。

sentences.zh: 直到今天，我的一个朋友，我最亲密的朋友之一，一个我视为兄弟的人，就是从那个电子游戏里认识的。

sentences.en: And this is a lesson that I've learned, actually, if you're struggling with this. it may not apply to everybody, but I think it can help.

sentences.zh: 也就是随着年龄增长，你花在不同人身上的时间。

sentences.zh: 当我第一次看到这个时，我真的、真的感到很震惊。

sentences.zh: 事实上，这张图表很大程度上改变了我的生活，因为它让我意识到，如果我不采取行动，我现有的那五个最好的朋友就会离我而去。

sentences.en: Yeah. And I saw this in your story that your relationship with friendship and connection has evolved over time.

sentences.en: Yeah. What has that journey been like? If you take me back from when you left South Africa, you arrive in America to pursue your dream as being this comedian.

sentences.en: How did your priorities shift as it relates to friendship and connection?
sentences.zh: 在友谊和人际关系方面，你的优先事项是如何转变的？

sentences.zh: 我想是因为我小时候独自待的时间太长了，所以我很爱其他人。

sentences.en: And when I became a young adult and I was starting to work, I really appreciated the people who would come into my life and what they would teach me and what they would remind me of myself, which is like an important thing to me.
sentences.zh: 当我成为年轻人并开始工作时，我真的很感激那些走进我生命的人，他们教给我的东西，以及他们让我回想起自己的样子，这对我来说很重要。

sentences.en: I think fundamentally that's what great friendship is, is somebody who sees a part of you that you wish to grow more of.
sentences.zh: 我认为从根本上说，伟大的友谊就是这样：有人看到了你想要更多发展的那个部分。

sentences.en: And then every time you're meeting with them, they're encouraging it and they're reminding you of it.
sentences.zh: 然后每次你和他们见面时，他们都在鼓励它，提醒你它的存在。

sentences.en: And that's why I warn people about bad friends because a bad friend can do the same thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我警告人们要远离坏朋友，因为坏朋友也会做同样的事。

sentences.en: If I say to you, think of the kid who bullied you in school.
sentences.zh: 如果我让你想想学校里欺负你的那个孩子。

sentences.en: Think of that kid who was really mean to you.
sentences.zh: 想想那个对你很刻薄的孩子。

sentences.en: I bet you if you met them today, I don't care how successful you are on this podcast, there's a little bit of that kid that got bullied that they still have.
sentences.zh: 我敢打赌，如果你今天见到他们，不管你在播客里有多成功，那个被欺负的孩子依然存在于你内心深处。

sentences.en: Oh, 100%. Do you know what I mean? 100%.
sentences.zh: 噢，百分之百。你知道我的意思吗？百分之百。

sentences.en: I could kill him like this. There you go.
sentences.zh: 我当时真想杀了他。就是这样。

sentences.en: And where I stood when he called me the M word.
sentences.zh: 就在他叫我那个M开头的词的时候。

sentences.en: Exactly. Exactly. And it's amazing how that happens to us.
sentences.zh: 没错。没错。这发生在我们身上真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: But it's because they hold us in a moment, you know?
sentences.zh: 但这是因为他们把我们困在了那一刻，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And some people hold you in a negative moment and some people hold you in a positive moment.
sentences.zh: 有些人让你停留在负面时刻，而有些人让你停留在正面时刻。

sentences.en: There are some friends I can think of where no matter what is happening in my life, if I meet them, I'm smiling, I'm thinking, I'm being creative I'm laughing I'm loving I'm sharing I'm feeling I can't control it You know It's not something that I'm actively trying to do Because they are constantly seeing that part of me That I wish to encourage And so How do you define a bad friend?
sentences.zh: 我能想到一些朋友，无论我生活中发生了什么，只要见到他们，我就会微笑，我会思考，我会变得有创造力，我会大笑，我会去爱，去分享，去感受，我无法控制它。你知道，这不是我刻意去做的，因为他们一直在看到我想要鼓励的那部分自己。那么，你如何定义坏朋友呢？

sentences.en: Like how do you know? How do you spot one?
sentences.zh: 比如你怎么知道？你怎么发现一个坏朋友？

sentences.en: I don't think you spot them I think you feel it You know And I think it's a lot easier for us to spot than we think it is One of the easiest ones is can you be yourself?
sentences.zh: 我不认为你能发现他们，我认为你能感觉到。你知道，而且我认为这比我们想象的要容易发现得多。最简单的一点是：你能做你自己吗？

sentences.en: You know Sometimes they're not a bad friend They're a bad friend for you because you are not revealing yourself to them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有时候他们并不是坏朋友，他们是对你来说很糟糕的朋友，因为你没有向他们展示真实的自己。

sentences.en: And so they are being friends with the idea of you, but they're not being friends with you.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只是在和你心目中的那个“你”做朋友，而不是在和你本人做朋友。

sentences.en: And then you leave thinking, I don't feel good.
sentences.zh: 然后你离开时会想，我感觉不太好。

sentences.en: But they don't even know you. So you can't blame them for being a bad friend.
sentences.zh: 但他们甚至不了解你。所以你不能怪他们是个坏朋友。

sentences.en: You know, I almost don't think there's such a thing as a bad friend.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我几乎不认为有“坏朋友”这种东西。

sentences.en: I think you're just in a bad friendship.
sentences.zh: 我认为你只是处在一段糟糕的友谊中。

sentences.en: You know, because they could be a great friend to somebody else.
sentences.zh: 你知道，因为他们对别人来说可能是一个很好的朋友。

sentences.en: So I wouldn't even define them as being a good or bad friend.
sentences.zh: 所以我甚至不会把他们定义为好朋友或坏朋友。

sentences.en: I just go, this is a bad friendship for you.
sentences.zh: 我只会说，这对你来说是一段糟糕的友谊。

sentences.en: And what I learned very early on was like the value of good friendships, you know, and I learned because of my mom.
sentences.zh: 我早年学到的是好友谊的价值，你知道，这多亏了我妈妈。

sentences.en: I remember once I was, this was, I was 19, 20.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次，那时我19、20岁。

sentences.en: I just finished high school. So, yeah, I was 19 and just finished high school.
sentences.zh: 我刚高中毕业。所以，是的，我19岁，刚高中毕业。

sentences.en: And I spent all my time hanging out with like friends of mine in the hood, you know, and we just did nothing the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 我所有的时间都和街区里的朋友混在一起，你知道，我们整天无所事事。

sentences.en: And we got up to mischief and was like, how do we make money?
sentences.zh: 我们搞些恶作剧，然后想：我们怎么赚钱？

sentences.en: How do we hustle? How do we do these things?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么去打拼？我们怎么做这些事？

sentences.en: And then my cousin went to university.
sentences.zh: 然后我的表亲上了大学。

sentences.en: And then I, because his university like had this like open-ish policy, you could just hang out on campus all day.
sentences.zh: 因为他的大学有那种开放式的政策，你整天都可以待在校园里。

sentences.en: And so I started hanging out with him on campus pretty much the whole day when he wasn't in lectures.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始整天和他待在校园里，当他没课的时候。

sentences.en: And then I went home one day and my mom was beaming.
sentences.zh: 有一天我回家，我妈妈满面春风。

sentences.en: You know, I walked in with my cousin and my mom was like, oh, how are you, Buti?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我和我表亲走进去，我妈妈说，噢，你好吗，Buti？

sentences.en: And she's so happy. And she's like, oh, nice to see you.
sentences.zh: 她很高兴。她说，噢，很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: And she said, oh, I'm so happy. I'm so happy that you guys are spending this time together.
sentences.zh: 她说，噢，我太高兴了。我很高兴你们在一起度过这段时间。

sentences.en: And I said, why are you so happy? And my mom said, because you spend all your time at the university.
sentences.zh: 我说，你为什么这么高兴？我妈妈说，因为你把所有时间都花在大学里了。

sentences.en: And I said to my mom, I was like, mom, I don't go to university.
sentences.zh: 我对妈妈说，妈，我没上大学。

sentences.en: I just hang around and I do nothing. And she said, yes, but the people you're hanging around and doing nothing with will inspire you to do more with your life because they're doing something with it.
sentences.zh: 我只是在那儿闲逛，什么也没做。她说，是的，但那些和你一起闲逛、什么也不做的人，会激励你为生活做更多的事，因为他们正在做些什么。

sentences.en: And I was like, what? And she said to me, she was like, you cannot be around people who are moving and not wish to move.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，什么？她对我说，她说，你不能和那些正在前进的人待在一起，却不想前进。

sentences.en: Whether we like it or not, the people around us are affecting how we see ourselves and how we wish to be seen.
sentences.zh: 不管我们喜不喜欢，周围的人都在影响我们如何看待自己，以及我们希望被如何看待。

sentences.en: And that stuck with me. I don't think I took it immediately, but it definitely stuck in my brain.
sentences.zh: 那句话深深印在了我脑海里。我不认为我立刻就领悟了，但它绝对留在了我的脑子里。

sentences.en: And the friends that I have today are still, I have new friends, you know, as I grow in life.
sentences.zh: 我今天的朋友依然是……我随着生活成长，也有了新朋友。

sentences.en: But the friends that I have today, my core group of friends, you'll see them with me at the Grammys.
sentences.zh: 但我今天的朋友，我的核心朋友圈，你会看到他们和我一起出现在格莱美奖上。

sentences.en: You'll see them sometimes like when I'd be like, you know, backstage at the Daily Show.
sentences.zh: 有时你会看到他们，比如当我在《The Daily Show》后台的时候。

sentences.en: You'll see them with me at random events in the world.
sentences.zh: 你会看到他们和我一起出现在世界各地的随机活动中。

sentences.en: You'll see them backstage at my comedy shows.
sentences.zh: 你会看到他们在我喜剧演出的后台。

sentences.en: These people have literally been with me on a journey where they've got their own lives. but our journeys have been intertwined because they always make me want to be more and do more and grow more and change it and I think I do the same thing for them and we're constantly challenging each other and and encouraging each other and playing with each other and and and that that has been I mean that's been immeasurable for me you know that that's I even value that more than I do like let's say success on the subject of success friendship sacrifice the moment when you come to the united states um you are very hard working to say the least in fact when we sat down you know you've flown from portugal to where was it seattle seattle to vegas yeah then here to new york right in the last couple of days or so yeah it's four days i think in tot yeah yeah four days you don't have to do that you don't have to do that i mean you don't i mean i don't know what's in your bank account but i would hazard a guess that you don't need the money so i often wonder what is it that's driving you today someone said to me the day on the podcast they said they referred to my driving force in my life as potentially being toxic fuel and i've never had the phrase toxic fuel before but the definition of that is this sort of combination of seemingly negative forces that pushes you to to prove something whether it's to yourself or to others or okay and shame is a big part of that i mean you see it a lot i think with first-generation immigrants when they come to a country.
sentences.zh: 这些人确实陪我走过了一段旅程，他们有自己的生活，但我们的旅程交织在一起，因为他们总是让我想要变得更多、做得更多、成长更多、改变更多。我想我也为他们做了同样的事，我们不断地挑战彼此、鼓励彼此、一起玩耍。那对我来说是不可估量的，你知道，我甚至比所谓的成功更看重这一点。说到成功、友谊和牺牲，当你来到美国时，嗯，你非常努力工作，至少可以这么说。事实上，当我们坐下来时，你知道，你从葡萄牙飞到哪里？西雅图？西雅图到拉斯维加斯，是的，然后到纽约，对吧？在过去几天左右。是的，我想总共四天。是的，四天。你没必要这样做，你没必要这样做。我是说，我不知道你的银行账户里有多少钱，但我敢猜你并不缺钱。所以我经常想，到底是什么在驱动你今天前进？有人在播客上对我说，他们把我的生活动力称为潜在的“有毒燃料”，我以前从未听过“有毒燃料”这个词，但它的定义是：这种看似负面的力量组合，推动你去证明某些事情，无论是对自己还是对他人。羞耻感是其中的很大一部分。我的意思是，我认为第一代移民来到一个国家时，你会经常看到这种情况。

sentences.en: They know what it's like to be without, so they're driven by this toxic fuel.
sentences.zh: 他们知道一无所有是什么感觉，所以他们被这种有毒的燃料所驱动。

sentences.en: How does that land with you? And can you relate to any of that at all?
sentences.zh: 这对你有什么影响？你能感同身受吗？

sentences.en: I can, but I don't think that's been my case.
sentences.zh: 我可以，但我认为那不是我的情况。

sentences.en: If you spoke to me three, four years ago, and you said, Trevor, you went to Portugal, you went to Seattle, you went to Vegas, and now you're in New York, and it would be, yes, because I went to work here, I went to work here, I went to work there, and I went to work there, you know?
sentences.zh: 如果你三四年前问我，你说，Trevor，你去了葡萄牙，去了西雅图，去了拉斯维加斯，现在你在纽约，那会是：是的，因为我去那里工作，去那里工作，去那里工作，去那里工作，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Now, I was in Portugal with my friends. That's why I was in Portugal.
sentences.zh: 现在，我在葡萄牙是和朋友在一起。这就是我在葡萄牙的原因。

sentences.en: I was in Seattle because I was working, I work with Microsoft, but it's like a passion project.
sentences.zh: 我在西雅图是因为我在工作，我和Microsoft合作，但这更像是一个热情项目。

sentences.en: I get to work on tech. I get to explore technology and ideas and work with engineers and just enhance my mind.
sentences.zh: 我有机会研究技术，探索技术和想法，与工程师合作，提升我的思维。

sentences.en: And then I was in Vegas doing work. And then in New York, I'm having a conversation with you, but this is not like in a work world.
sentences.zh: 然后我在拉斯维加斯工作。在纽约，我正在和你谈话，但这不像是在工作世界里。

sentences.en: So I go like, oh, I'm going to have a great conversation with you. and I also love being in New York because my friends are here and this is technically where I live.
sentences.zh: 所以我心想，噢，我要和你进行一次很棒的谈话。而且我也喜欢待在纽约，因为我的朋友在这里，从技术上讲，这就是我住的地方。

sentences.en: So like if you said to me, let's do this interview not in New York, I would have said no.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你对我说，让我们在纽约以外的地方做这个采访，我会说不。

sentences.en: But because you chose a city where my friends are, I'll say yes to you.
sentences.zh: 但因为你选择了一个有我朋友的城市，我会答应你。

sentences.en: And it didn't used to be the case. So now I have made one of the determining factors of how I live my life.
sentences.zh: 以前并不是这样。所以现在，我已经把“朋友”作为我生活方式的决定性因素之一。

sentences.en: I think of it through the lens of friends first because I think that community is literally the most important thing in everybody's life, not just my life, everybody's life.
sentences.zh: 我通过朋友的视角来看待它，因为我认为社区在每个人的生活中确实是最重要的事情，不仅仅是我的生活，是每个人的生活。

sentences.en: I know some people will be like, my family.
sentences.zh: 我知道有些人会说，我的家人。

sentences.en: I'm like, yeah, you think that. And it is true.
sentences.zh: 我说，是的，你是这么想的。这确实是真的。

sentences.en: But as you said on the graphs, you'll see.
sentences.zh: 但正如你在图表上所说，你会看到的。

sentences.en: At some point, you're going to get old and your kids are going to go off and live their own lives and do their own thing.
sentences.zh: 在某个时候，你会变老，你的孩子会离开去过他们自己的生活，做他们自己的事情。

sentences.en: And then you're going to be shocked at how it's you and your spouse, if you're lucky.
sentences.zh: 然后你会震惊地发现，如果幸运的话，最后只剩下你和你的配偶。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, you're alone. And you're like, where are all my friends?
sentences.zh: 突然之间，你孤身一人。你会想，我的朋友们都去哪儿了？

sentences.en: Where are all these people? But friendships are, you know, they're little piggy banks.
sentences.zh: 这些人都在哪儿呢？但友谊，你知道，它们就像一个个小存钱罐。

sentences.en: You're putting money in and they're putting money in yours. and every now and again, you get to break them open and enjoy what's inside.
sentences.zh: 你在往里存钱，他们也在往你的存钱罐里存钱。时不时地，你可以把它们打破，享受里面的收获。

sentences.en: But that's the most important thing. That's how, that's my, like, literally, that's my success now.
sentences.zh: 但这才是最重要的。这就是，这就是我的，真的，这就是我现在所定义的成功。

sentences.en: Now? Yeah, that's my success now.
sentences.zh: 现在？是的，这就是我现在定义的成功。

sentences.en: Before... It was just because I loved solving any puzzle that somebody would put in front of me.
sentences.zh: 以前……那仅仅是因为我喜欢解决别人抛给我的任何难题。

sentences.en: That's all that drove me. And that's a lot of what still drives me now.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所有的动力。而这在很大程度上也是我现在的动力。

sentences.en: I just love puzzles. And what was the puzzle that brought you to America?
sentences.zh: 我就是喜欢解谜。那么，是什么难题把你带到了美国？

sentences.en: So the puzzle was, can somebody host the Daily Show when they're like not from America?
sentences.zh: 所以那个难题是，一个人如果不是美国人，他能主持《The Daily Show》吗？

sentences.en: And, you know, it's like just all these things.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，就是所有这些事情。

sentences.en: Can you even do it? Can you go host a show in America?
sentences.zh: 你真的能做到吗？你能去美国主持一档节目吗？

sentences.en: Like, well, this is a crazy puzzle. Seems impossible.
sentences.zh: 就像是，嗯，这是一个疯狂的难题。看起来不可能。

sentences.en: So let's try it. Was money or fame or anything part of that?
sentences.zh: 所以我们试试吧。金钱、名声或者其他什么东西是其中的一部分吗？

sentences.en: Because fame is often associated with a form of validation.
sentences.zh: 因为名声通常与某种形式的自我证明联系在一起。

sentences.en: No. No? No. That's the curse of what I do.
sentences.zh: 不。不是吗？不。那是我的职业带来的诅咒。

sentences.en: I often say to people, you know, I'm unlucky that a part of my job comes with fame.
sentences.zh: 我常对人说，你知道，我不走运，因为我的工作的一部分伴随着名声。

sentences.en: I don't like that part of my job. Why? Because I don't need it, nor do I want it.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢我工作中的那部分。为什么？因为我不需要它，也不想要它。

sentences.en: What's the cost of it? The curse? Oh, I mean, I'm sure you're starting to experience this in many ways in your life.
sentences.zh: 它的代价是什么？诅咒？哦，我是说，我相信你在生活中很多方面也开始体验到这一点了。

sentences.en: But like it's people will never appreciate the beauty and the and the tranquility that comes with anonymity.
sentences.zh: 但人们永远不会欣赏匿名所带来的那种美好与宁静。

sentences.en: The the ability to write your story whenever you meet someone.
sentences.zh: 那种无论你何时遇见某人，都能重新书写自己故事的能力。

sentences.en: You know, when when you meet a stranger, let's say you're at a bar, at a restaurant, in a train station, wherever you can look at somebody and you can say, hello, my name is. and you can tell them who you are.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你遇见一个陌生人，假设你在酒吧、餐厅、火车站，无论在哪儿，你可以看着某人说，你好，我叫……然后你可以告诉他们你是谁。

sentences.en: And what we never seem to realize as people is every time we meet a new person, we are writing our story from the beginning and from that moment in time, you know?
sentences.zh: 而我们作为人似乎从未意识到的是，每次我们遇见一个新的人，我们都是从头开始书写我们的故事，从那一刻起，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And you think about this, like, I think of it through the lens of, like, characters, characters sometimes.
sentences.zh: 你思考一下，我有时会通过角色的视角来看待这个问题。

sentences.en: I go, like, if Luke Skywalker met you before Luke meets, you know, Yoda, what is Luke?
sentences.zh: 我会想，如果Luke Skywalker在遇见Yoda之前遇见了你，Luke是什么？

sentences.en: Luke is just, like, some random dude who lives on, like, a dusty planet.
sentences.zh: Luke只是一个住在尘土飞扬的星球上的普通家伙。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Luke. I live on a dusty planet.
sentences.zh: 你好，我叫Luke。我住在一个尘土飞扬的星球上。

sentences.en: You meet Luke many years later. Luke's like, hi, I'm a Jedi.
sentences.zh: 多年后你再遇见Luke。Luke会说，你好，我是绝地武士。

sentences.en: What a different way to live as Luke and what a different way to be.
sentences.zh: 作为Luke，这是一种多么不同的生活方式，也是一种多么不同的存在方式。

sentences.en: And I think that's the beauty sometimes that we have, that we take for granted as people, is the ability to rewrite a story or to write it from a different perspective because we've moved on and we've gone somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是我们有时拥有的美，我们作为人却视而不见，那就是重写故事或从不同视角书写故事的能力，因为我们已经向前迈进，去往了别处。

sentences.en: When you are now known, your anonymity is gone. people have a different idea of what privacy you deserve or don't deserve.
sentences.zh: 当你现在出名了，你的匿名性就消失了。人们对你应得或不应得的隐私有不同的看法。

sentences.en: I've had many friends who won't go out with me in public because they go, hey, man, I want to have a meal and not be disturbed.
sentences.zh: 我有很多朋友不愿在公共场合和我一起出去，因为他们会说，嘿，伙计，我想吃顿饭，不想被打扰。

sentences.en: I want to wear whatever clothes I want to wear without worrying that they'll take a picture of me standing next to you and then I'll look terrible.
sentences.zh: 我想穿任何我想穿的衣服，而不必担心他们会拍下我站在你旁边的照片，然后让我看起来很糟糕。

sentences.en: I don't want to think about these things.
sentences.zh: 我不想考虑这些事情。

sentences.en: And I get it. I get where they're coming from.
sentences.zh: 我明白。我明白他们的想法。

sentences.en: I think many of the the downsides of fame are the facts that, as my mom even puts it, you are now owned by the world.
sentences.zh: 我认为名声的许多弊端在于，正如我妈妈所说，你现在属于全世界了。

sentences.en: You know, people have this idea that no matter what day you're having, you should engage with them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们有一种想法，无论你那天过得怎么样，你都应该配合他们。

sentences.en: No matter who you're with, you should afford them the time.
sentences.zh: 无论你和谁在一起，你都应该抽出时间给他们。

sentences.en: And I understand it from their perspective because for them, they're seeing you and they're encountering you.
sentences.zh: 我从他们的角度理解这一点，因为对他们来说，他们是在看你，是在遇见你。

sentences.en: What a beautiful experience. You know, but it's hard for us to imagine that that person is just having a day you know i remember once joking uh with an ex of mine and i was saying it's amazing how like when we're having like dinner or lunch in public we can't even tell like an animated story to each other because if someone just sees us from far it'll look like we fight you know so now we're sitting there and i can't be like yo this guy i was like and if someone takes that picture and go like trevor noah fighting with this and it's like no and that becomes a thing in your world and now friends are, were you fighting and other people?
sentences.zh: 多么美好的体验。你知道，但我们很难想象那个人只是在过普通的一天。你知道，我记得有一次和我的一位前任开玩笑，我说，真神奇，当我们在公共场合吃晚餐或午餐时，我们甚至不能给对方讲一个生动的故事，因为如果有人从远处看到我们，看起来就像我们在吵架，你知道，所以我们坐在那儿，我不能说，嘿，这家伙，我当时想，如果有人拍下那张照片说，Trevor Noah在和这个人吵架，那就不好了，这在你的世界里就成了一件事，现在朋友们会问，你们在吵架吗？还有其他人？

sentences.en: You'll be shocked at how pervasive it is.
sentences.zh: 你会震惊于这种现象有多普遍。

sentences.en: And I think it's why so many celebrities or famous people or people in the public eye. have lived very depressed lives, have lived lives where they're isolated, have lived lives where they don't leave their homes, and then you find them passed out in their bathtub, overdosed on something.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是为什么这么多名人、知名人士或公众人物过着非常抑郁的生活，过着与世隔绝的生活，过着不离开家门的生活，然后你发现他们昏倒在浴缸里，药物过量。

sentences.en: Think about how many times you've heard that story.
sentences.zh: 想想你听过多少次这样的故事。

sentences.en: A really famous person has died. You never hear that they've died in public.
sentences.zh: 一个非常有名的人去世了。你从来没听说过他们是在公共场合去世的。

sentences.en: You never hear that they've died while with their friends.
sentences.zh: 你从来没听说过他们是在和朋友在一起时去世的。

sentences.en: No, it's always them alone in like... A hotel room.
sentences.zh: 不，他们总是独自一人在……酒店房间里。

sentences.en: Yeah, a hotel room, a bathtub, tub you know a hot tub but it's always like a such a solitary like ending for somebody that and then the whole world cries for them and with them it's like oh i can't believe this what what do you oh this is so and i'm like yeah because you'll be shocked at how lonely being well known can actually be because it means you can never be alone in many places and that's where i think core friends are very important you said in there that you what they don't know is that you're a human and that you're going through life in all the same ways as everyone else yeah well no not in the same ways but in different ways and i think that's that's the you know i i do talk about awareness yeah i'm very careful i you know i and maybe it's because of how i was raised as well very careful to not make it like a woe is me thing i'm not like fame has hurt me and it's harmed me and you know there are many things that have come with it every gift is a curse, you know?
sentences.zh: 是的，酒店房间，浴缸，你知道，热水浴缸，但对于某人来说，这总是一个非常孤独的结局，然后全世界都为他们哭泣，和他们一起哭，就像，哦，我不敢相信，这，这太……而我会说，是的，因为你会震惊于出名实际上有多孤独，因为这意味着你在很多地方永远无法独处，这就是我认为核心朋友非常重要的原因。你在里面说，他们不知道的是你是一个人，你正在经历和每个人一样的生活。是的，嗯，不，不是以同样的方式，而是以不同的方式，我认为这就是，你知道，我确实谈论过意识。是的，我非常小心，你知道，我，也许是因为我的成长方式，非常小心，不让它变成一种“我好可怜”的事情。我不是说名声伤害了我，你知道，它确实带来了一些东西，每一份礼物都是诅咒，你知道吗？

sentences.en: But many of the things that it came with, I did not want, nor did I need.
sentences.zh: 但它带来的许多东西，我既不想要，也不需要。

sentences.en: I like waiting for a table at a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢在餐厅等位。

sentences.en: I genuinely do, and I don't mind that. You know, I don't care for, I've never been somebody, because my friends have always been the thing.
sentences.zh: 我真心喜欢，我不介意。你知道，我不在乎，我从来不是那种人，因为我的朋友一直是最重要的。

sentences.en: In fact, one of the days I learned the lesson in one of the most practical ways was, I love roller coasters, and I love going to theme parks.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有一天我以最实际的方式学到了这一课，我喜欢过山车，我喜欢去主题公园。

sentences.en: And we used to go with my friends, and you do the usual thing.
sentences.zh: 我们过去常和朋友一起去，做些常规的事情。

sentences.en: You stand in a line for an hour and then you ride for like 60 seconds and then you walk for like 30 minutes to the next one and then you do it all over again.
sentences.zh: 你排队一小时，然后玩60秒，然后走30分钟去下一个，然后一切重来。

sentences.en: And I loved it. And then one day I was going to a theme park and then the theme park knew I was coming and now I was the host of The Daily Show and they're like, hey, listen, we heard that you're at the theme park.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那样。然后有一天我要去一个主题公园，公园知道我要来，那时我是《The Daily Show》的主持人，他们说，嘿，听着，我们听说你在主题公园。

sentences.en: We would like to take you around to all the rides.
sentences.zh: 我们想带你去玩所有的游乐设施。

sentences.en: And there's like no skip, you skip the lines and you get to ride as many times as you want.
sentences.zh: 而且不用排队，你可以跳过队伍，想玩多少次就玩多少次。

sentences.en: And I was like, this, I was like, this is it.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，就是这个。我当时想，这就是了。

sentences.en: The Daily Show has paid off. Finally, finally, all the death threats are worth it.
sentences.zh: 《The Daily Show》终于有回报了。终于，终于，所有的死亡威胁都值了。

sentences.en: And we went and we rode on the rides and we were just manic.
sentences.zh: 我们去了，玩了那些设施，我们简直疯了。

sentences.en: We did every, I mean, we did every ride that you couldn't do in a day.
sentences.zh: 我们玩了所有设施，我是说，我们玩了所有一天之内玩不完的设施。

sentences.en: And we finished a park that would probably take like, let's say, eight to 10 hours to finish.
sentences.zh: 我们完成了一个通常需要，比如说，8到10小时才能玩完的公园。

sentences.en: We did it all multiple times in like the span of like three hours.
sentences.zh: 我们在大约3小时内把所有项目都玩了好几遍。

sentences.en: I had a headache. My friends were dehydrated.
sentences.zh: 我头疼。我的朋友们脱水了。

sentences.en: We had had seldom a conversation amongst us.
sentences.zh: 我们之间几乎没怎么交谈。

sentences.en: And it was so strange getting back in the car.
sentences.zh: 回到车里感觉太奇怪了。

sentences.en: And this felt like the most depressing theme park experience we'd ever had.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是我们经历过的最令人沮丧的主题公园体验。

sentences.en: And we got back to the house. And I guess because my friends and I like doing this, we sort of tried to understand and analyze what had gone wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们回到家。我想是因为我和朋友们喜欢这样做，我们试图理解和分析出了什么问题。

sentences.en: We're like, why do we feel like this? And we came to the conclusion.
sentences.zh: 我们想，为什么我们会有这种感觉？我们得出了结论。

sentences.en: We're like, oh, we assumed that the theme park, we loved the theme park because of the roller coasters.
sentences.zh: 我们想，哦，我们以为我们喜欢主题公园是因为过山车。

sentences.en: What we didn't realize was We loved the theme parks Because it forced us to stand in line For an hour as friends And just be And we just talk There's literally You can't do anything else You just have to stand there for an hour And just like talk to each other And then you hear people screaming And they've designed them Now like once I did that I started like learning about theme parks And how brilliant ones Do this to you on purpose They make you wait in certain ways And in certain places And then the screams of the writers Make you anticipate something And become excited and it's all the ingredients for like living a good life, I feel, is instead of chasing like what seems like the exciting rollercoastery thing.
sentences.zh: 我们没意识到的是，我们喜欢主题公园是因为它强迫我们作为朋友排队一小时，只是待在一起，我们只是聊天。真的，你什么也做不了，你只能在那儿站一小时，只是像这样和对方聊天，然后你听到人们尖叫，他们现在设计这些设施，一旦我做了那件事，我就开始了解主题公园，以及出色的公园是如何故意这样对你的。他们让你以特定的方式在特定的地方等待，然后乘坐者的尖叫声让你期待着什么，变得兴奋，我觉得这都是过上好日子的要素，而不是去追逐那些看起来像过山车一样刺激的东西。

sentences.en: You spend your time with the people you love, and you look forward to amazing things that you're going to do hopefully with them or maybe just for yourself.
sentences.zh: 你花时间和所爱的人在一起，期待着你希望和他们一起，或者也许只是为你自己去做的一些了不起的事情。

sentences.en: And then when you get there, you enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 然后当你到达那里时，你享受它。

sentences.en: And then on the other side, you take a long walk and you commiserate and you share the experience with each other and you get to process what has happened to you so that when you do it again, it becomes novel and interesting and beautiful.
sentences.zh: 然后在另一边，你走一段长路，互相倾诉，分享这段经历，你有机会处理发生在你身上的事情，这样当你再次做这件事时，它就变得新奇、有趣且美丽。

sentences.en: And so that's where I realized the downsides and the upsides.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我意识到弊端和益处的地方。

sentences.en: So I appreciate many of the things that have come with my life, don't get me wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以我很感激我生活中得到的许多东西，别误会我。

sentences.en: But I won't lie to you. I have as much fun in a comedy club with 70 people in it as I do in an arena with 12,000 people in it.
sentences.zh: 但我不会骗你。我在一个有70人的喜剧俱乐部里玩得和在有12000人的体育场里一样开心。

sentences.en: In fact, I have more fun in the comedy club.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我在喜剧俱乐部玩得更开心。

sentences.en: It's so paradoxical that adding friction to an experience can make the experience better.
sentences.zh: 给体验增加阻力反而能让体验变得更好，这太矛盾了。

sentences.en: But that's kind of what you've described.
sentences.zh: 但这正是你所描述的。

sentences.en: And as you were talking about it, I was thinking about this study I read ages ago where they took one group of people.
sentences.zh: 当你谈论它时，我想起了很久以前读过的一项研究，他们找了一组人。

sentences.en: They had this boring community forum. And they took one group of people and they let those people straight into this boring community forum.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个无聊的社区论坛。他们让一组人直接进入这个无聊的社区论坛。

sentences.en: And then they asked them in a survey after, how was the community?
sentences.zh: 然后在之后的调查中问他们，社区怎么样？

sentences.en: And all the people said boring. And they took another group of people and they made them wait to get into the forum.
sentences.zh: 所有人都说无聊。他们找了另一组人，让他们排队进入论坛。

sentences.en: They made them complete tests and go through this rigorous process to fight to get into the forum.
sentences.zh: 他们让他们完成测试，经历这个严格的过程，为了进入论坛而奋斗。

sentences.en: The people went into the same forum. And then in surveys after, they described the forum as being so much better than the people who weren't made to go through the gauntlet to get in.
sentences.zh: 这些人进入了同一个论坛。然后在之后的调查中，他们描述论坛比那些没有经历过重重关卡才进去的人所描述的要好得多。

sentences.en: And it's this idea that friction adds value to the thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是阻力增加了事物价值的观点。

sentences.en: We like fight for it. Like the 40 minute queue is what makes us so grateful for the roller coaster.
sentences.zh: 我们为它奋斗。就像40分钟的排队让我们对过山车如此感激。

sentences.en: And when you get robbed of that because you get to play life in easy mode or.
sentences.zh: 而当你因为以简单模式玩生活而被剥夺了这一点时，或者……

sentences.en: Exactly. That's exactly what it is. That's the curse.
sentences.zh: 没错。就是这样。这就是诅咒。

sentences.en: Yeah. It's great. But also, yeah, the point about connection.
sentences.zh: 是的。这很棒。但还有，关于联系的那一点。

sentences.en: I never thought that so much of the enjoyment of going to the theme park is standing there and just small talking for an hour with my friends.
sentences.zh: 我从没想过，去主题公园的乐趣很大一部分在于站在那儿，和朋友们闲聊一小时。

sentences.en: It's just being. You mentioned the word death threats on The Daily Show.
sentences.zh: 那只是存在着。你提到了《The Daily Show》的死亡威胁。

sentences.en: Yeah. When you did get onto The Daily Show, which was a real first for a show like that, it didn't go so well at first.
sentences.zh: 是的。当你进入《The Daily Show》时，这对于那样的节目来说确实是第一次，起初并不顺利。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, it was terrible. I didn't realize this.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，太糟糕了。我没意识到这一点。

sentences.en: I was looking at the stats and I read that.
sentences.zh: 我当时在看统计数据，我读到了。

sentences.en: It was absolutely terrible. It was like, man, it was, you know, when they say be careful what you wish for, because I was like, oh, I'd love a challenge and this will be an interesting, and oh, it was a challenge.
sentences.zh: 那绝对是太糟糕了。就像，伙计，就像，你知道，当他们说小心你所祈求的，因为我当时想，哦，我喜欢挑战，这会很有趣，哦，那真是一个挑战。

sentences.en: It was absolutely terrible because I stepped into a role that I quickly learned wasn't just a position, but it was almost, I don't know how, like it was like a post in a way.
sentences.zh: 那绝对是太糟糕了，因为我进入了一个角色，我很快意识到这不仅仅是一个职位，而几乎是，我不知道怎么说，就像一个岗位。

sentences.en: It wasn't just like you're hosting a show.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是主持一档节目。

sentences.en: No, no. I very quickly learned like Jon Stewart to many people, was, you know, he was the most trusted man in America.
sentences.zh: 不，不。我很快了解到，对许多人来说，Jon Stewart是，你知道，他是美国最受信任的人。

sentences.en: And he was the voice of a generation. And he, you know, the politicians who sort of looked to him and they're like, well, what would Jon Stewart think?
sentences.zh: 他是那一代人的声音。而且他，你知道，那些政客们会看着他，他们会想，Jon Stewart会怎么想？

sentences.en: Wow, I mean, that was... And even if you remove the legend that is Jon Stewart, just taking over any show comes with a moment where people don't like, no one likes change, you know?
sentences.zh: 哇，我的意思是，那是……即使你抛开Jon Stewart这个传奇，接手任何节目都会伴随着人们不喜欢的一刻，没人喜欢改变，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So like when Johnny Carson handed over, people weren't happy, you know?
sentences.zh: 所以当Johnny Carson交接时，人们不高兴，你知道吗？

sentences.en: When Leno handed over, people weren't happy.
sentences.zh: 当Leno交接时，人们也不高兴。

sentences.en: It always happens. Is race an element in this?
sentences.zh: 这总是会发生。种族是其中的一个因素吗？

sentences.en: I'm sure for some people. But I think it's, you know, I'm careful to say like it's about race.
sentences.zh: 我相信对某些人来说是。但我认为，你知道，我小心地说这与种族有关。

sentences.en: And I think it's more, it's all the things that make you different.
sentences.zh: 我认为更多的是，所有让你与众不同的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah. You know, so me being different in my color to Jon Stewart probably makes a person feel like I'm more different to him when I'm sitting in the desk.
sentences.zh: 是的。你知道，所以我的肤色与Jon Stewart不同，可能让一个人觉得当我坐在桌子后面时，我与他更不同。

sentences.en: The show has changed. The show has been really...
sentences.zh: 节目变了。节目真的……

sentences.en: Yeah, and that I love, if there's one thing I love, it's understanding or trying to understand human beings.
sentences.zh: 是的，我喜欢这一点，如果说有什么是我喜欢的，那就是理解或试图理解人类。

sentences.en: Because I think we're very complicated, but we're also simple at the same time.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为我们非常复杂，但同时也很简单。

sentences.en: And that was a wonderful moment for me to like learn like, wow, even people, because these people who are hating, by the way, it's not like these were conservatives or anything.
sentences.zh: 那对我来说是一个美妙的时刻，去学习，哇，即使是人们，因为这些人正在仇恨，顺便说一句，并不是说他们是保守派什么的。

sentences.en: It was like liberal people who are, you know, and some of the things they were saying to me in emails or like online.
sentences.zh: 他们就像是自由派的人，你知道，他们通过电子邮件或在线对我说的一些话。

sentences.en: They were emailing you. Yeah, oh yeah, people, they'll find ways.
sentences.zh: 他们给你发邮件？是的，哦，是的，人们，他们会找到方法的。

sentences.en: But you, I would sit there and be like, wow, you really hate me.
sentences.zh: 但我会坐在那儿想，哇，你真的恨我。

sentences.en: I've done nothing to you, but you hate me.
sentences.zh: 我没对你做过什么，但你恨我。

sentences.en: But then I realized, no, you hate the idea of me and you hate what I've done to your world.
sentences.zh: 但后来我意识到，不，你恨的是我的概念，你恨我给你的世界带来的改变。

sentences.en: I'm the representative, I'm the idea of how your world has changed.
sentences.zh: 我是代表，我是你的世界如何改变的概念。

sentences.en: Here's this idea that you've loved, Jon Stewart.
sentences.zh: 这是你所爱的一个概念，Jon Stewart。

sentences.en: He's now gone and I am the reason he's gone. even though that's not the case.
sentences.zh: 他现在走了，而我是他离开的原因。即使事实并非如此。

sentences.en: I am the reason he's gone. And because I'm the reason he's gone, you are now angry.
sentences.zh: 我是他离开的原因。因为我是他离开的原因，你现在很生气。

sentences.en: Death threat. Oh, yeah. But I mean, that was extreme.
sentences.zh: 死亡威胁。哦，是的。但我的意思是，那太极端了。

sentences.en: And you get that because The Daily Show is involved in politics, you know, or we comment on politics rather.
sentences.zh: 你会得到那个，因为《The Daily Show》涉及政治，你知道，或者我们评论政治。

sentences.en: And when we do that, man, you know, people would just be like, go back to where you came from.
sentences.zh: 当我们这样做时，伙计，你知道，人们只会说，滚回你来的地方去。

sentences.en: You, you know, how dare you and you're coming here and end with this and blah, blah, blah, blah, blah. again my gift and my curse was that I came from South Africa so I know like top quality racism so you know like when I came to America and like people were saying these things to me I was like oh oh I was like okay this is okay it's interesting you know but but it was really hard and I'm lucky that I had the people I had making the show with me because they really, really, really taught me, or I learned from the experience, that you genuinely, you cannot choose what's going to happen to you, but you almost definitely can choose who you're going to handle it with.
sentences.zh: 你，你知道，你怎么敢，你来到这里，还有这个，等等等等。再次，我的礼物和我的诅咒是我来自南非，所以我知道顶级质量的种族主义，所以你知道，当我来到美国，人们对我说这些话时，我想，哦，哦，我想，好吧，这很有趣，你知道，但，但这真的很难，我很幸运，我有那些和我一起制作节目的人，因为他们真的，真的，真的教会了我，或者我从经验中了解到，你真的无法选择会发生什么，但你几乎肯定可以选择和谁一起去处理它。

sentences.en: And that is the only thing that I now do in my life.
sentences.zh: 而这就是我现在生活中唯一做的事情。

sentences.en: And it determines everything. I will take a shit job if I'm going to work with great people, because a great job with the worst people is not going to feel great on the other side of it.
sentences.zh: 它决定了一切。如果能和很棒的人一起工作，我愿意接受一份烂工作，因为和最糟糕的人一起做一份很棒的工作，在另一边感觉不会很好。

sentences.en: And even thinking of it makes me happy. I think about the terrible times we had together in that building.
sentences.zh: 即使想到它也让我快乐。我想到我们在那栋楼里一起度过的糟糕时光。

sentences.en: You know, like reviewers hated us and people calling for the show to be canceled.
sentences.zh: 你知道，评论家讨厌我们，人们呼吁取消节目。

sentences.en: And we were just like there commiserating, trying our best and doing our best.
sentences.zh: 而我们只是在那儿倾诉，尽我们所能，做到最好。

sentences.en: And now when people see it as a successor, they go like, oh, you won the Emmys and you, you know, and it was this and it was successful. and then the digital footprint of the show changed everything.
sentences.zh: 现在当人们把它视为继任者时，他们会说，哦，你赢得了艾美奖，你，你知道，它是成功的。然后节目的数字足迹改变了一切。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, you know, these billions of impressions and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，你知道，这些数十亿的印象等等。

sentences.en: Yeah, that came afterwards. And now that's easy to see as an end product.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是后来才有的。现在很容易将其视为最终产品。

sentences.en: But when we were in the trenches, there was none of that.
sentences.zh: 但当我们身处战壕时，根本没有那些东西。

sentences.en: If I was a fly on the wall on the worst day in the trenches, is there a day that springs to mind?
sentences.zh: 如果我是战壕里最糟糕日子里的一只苍蝇，有什么日子浮现在脑海吗？

sentences.en: A day where you maybe considered, reconsidered your decision?
sentences.zh: 一个你可能考虑过，重新考虑你的决定的日子？

sentences.en: A day where you didn't want to get out of bed?
sentences.zh: 一个你不想起床的日子？

sentences.en: I was reading the stats around this to give people context.
sentences.zh: 我正在阅读关于这个的统计数据，给人们提供背景。

sentences.en: The show had lost 700,000 viewers a night when you first took over.
sentences.zh: 你刚接手时，节目每晚流失了70万观众。

sentences.en: Every night. Don't say it like that. You make it sound like we lost them every night.
sentences.zh: 每晚。别那样说。你听起来好像我们每晚都在流失他们。

sentences.en: It's from an interview you did in GQ. I know.
sentences.zh: 这是你接受GQ采访时说的。我知道。

sentences.en: And by the 100th episode, it had lost 37% of its viewers.
sentences.zh: 到第100集时，它已经流失了37%的观众。

sentences.en: Listen, it went on to become a smash hit across this digital revolution.
sentences.zh: 听着，它后来在这次数字革命中成为了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: No, no, but you're right. But I think that's important.
sentences.zh: 不，不，但你是对的。但我认为这很重要。

sentences.en: I think it's important context because I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是重要的背景，因为我不知道。

sentences.en: I just watched the show. I saw it on social media and I thought, he's killing it.
sentences.zh: 我只是看节目。我在社交媒体上看到它，我想，他做得太棒了。

sentences.en: Oh, no, man. No, it was a mission. Yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，伙计。不，那是一个任务。是的。

sentences.en: And there were many days. Again, I mean, I'm just so grateful and I'm so lucky.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多天。再说一次，我的意思是，我非常感激，我非常幸运。

sentences.en: There were days where I remember there was one day we like made a joke on the show, not even on the show.
sentences.zh: 有几天，我记得有一天我们在节目里开了一个玩笑，甚至不是在节目里。

sentences.en: No, someone on the team had tweeted something on the show account.
sentences.zh: 不，团队里的某个人在节目账号上发了推文。

sentences.en: And now there were like articles written about it.
sentences.zh: 现在有关于它的文章写出来了。

sentences.en: And they were like, this is why Trevor Noah shouldn't be there.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这就是为什么Trevor Noah不应该在那儿。

sentences.en: I wasn't even the person who tweeted. It's the show account.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不是发推文的人。那是节目账号。

sentences.en: But I'm not gonna come on and be like, that's not me.
sentences.zh: 但我不会出来说，那不是我。

sentences.en: We're a team, whatever. My name is on the show.
sentences.zh: 我们是一个团队，无论如何。我的名字在节目上。

sentences.en: And I remember turning to one of the writers, Dan Amira, still the head writer at the show.
sentences.zh: 我记得转向其中一位编剧，Dan Amira，现在还是节目的首席编剧。

sentences.en: And I said to Dan, I was like, man, I think I should just quit.
sentences.zh: 我对Dan说，我当时想，伙计，我想我应该辞职。

sentences.en: I was like, it'll just be easier for all of you because you guys were having a great time.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，这对你们所有人来说都会更容易，因为你们过得很开心。

sentences.en: I come along. I've made your lives terrible.
sentences.zh: 我来了。我让你们的生活变得糟糕。

sentences.en: I should just quit. I should just go, you know.
sentences.zh: 我应该辞职。我应该走，你知道。

sentences.en: And then I'll never forget Dan. He just looked at me and he's very dry.
sentences.zh: 然后我永远不会忘记Dan。他只是看着我，他非常冷幽默。

sentences.en: One of the funniest human beings you'll ever meet.
sentences.zh: 你见过的最有趣的人之一。

sentences.en: Really dry in his delivery. And he looks at me and he goes, but if you leave, this thing might get shut down. and then I don't get lunch anymore.
sentences.zh: 他的表达非常冷淡。他看着我，他说，但如果你离开，这东西可能会被关掉，然后我就没午饭吃了。

sentences.en: I said, I'm sorry, what? I'm like pouring my heart out here.
sentences.zh: 我说，对不起，什么？我在这儿倾诉我的心声。

sentences.en: And he's like, I like the lunch here.
sentences.zh: 他说，我喜欢这儿的午餐。

sentences.en: I said, you can just, what? What are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 我说，你能不能，什么？你在说什么？

sentences.en: And he said it to me in such a matter-of-fact way.
sentences.zh: 他以一种非常客观的方式对我说了。

sentences.en: And I remember being stunned, and I looked at him, and he said, how did he say it to me again?
sentences.zh: 我记得我很震惊，我看着他，他说，他又是怎么对我说的？

sentences.en: I don't know the exact words, but the sentiment was basically, he said, he said, these people don't like you, right?
sentences.zh: 我不记得确切的词，但意思基本上是，他说，他说，这些人不喜欢你，对吧？

sentences.en: And I was like, yeah, clearly. And he said, so if you leave, are they going to like you?
sentences.zh: 我说，是的，很明显。他说，所以如果你离开，他们会喜欢你吗？

sentences.en: I was like, no. Then he's like, so if leaving won't make them like you and staying won't make them like you, why not just stay?
sentences.zh: 我说，不。然后他说，所以如果离开不会让他们喜欢你，留下也不会让他们喜欢你，为什么不留下来？

sentences.en: He's like, because I like working with you.
sentences.zh: 他说，因为我喜欢和你一起工作。

sentences.en: So just stay. And that was just like one of those many moments where, you know, you talk about millimeters.
sentences.zh: 所以留下来。那就像那许多时刻中的一个，你知道，你谈论毫米。

sentences.en: It was just him saying to me, just stay, just stay. and I stayed.
sentences.zh: 只是他对我说了，留下来，留下来。我就留下来了。

sentences.en: And now everything seems obvious, but that building was full of people who told me to just stay.
sentences.zh: 现在一切看起来都很明显，但那栋楼里满是告诉我留下来的人。

sentences.en: That building was full of people who were like, I know.
sentences.zh: 那栋楼里满是人，他们就像，我知道。

sentences.en: One of them was Jon Stewart. I'll never forget, Jon, one of the best things he ever did for me was, it's almost like he predicted this.
sentences.zh: 其中一个是Jon Stewart。我永远不会忘记，Jon，他为我做的最好的事情之一是，这几乎就像他预言了这一点。

sentences.en: That's why I call him Yoda. I call him my Jewish Yoda, because we have this relationship where it's like, I came into this order where I was learning this new thing called It's, you know, like the force and being a Jedi and it seemed impossible.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我叫他Yoda。我叫他我的犹太Yoda，因为我们有这种关系，就像，我进入了这个秩序，我正在学习这个叫“原力”和成为绝地武士的新东西，这看起来不可能。

sentences.en: And he was this ordained figure in a way.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，他是一个受命的人物。

sentences.en: But I remember he called me into his office one day and he said to me, he said, I want to show you something.
sentences.zh: 但我记得有一天他把我叫进办公室，他对我说，他说，我想给你看点东西。

sentences.en: And he showed me an article that someone had written about him leaving the show.
sentences.zh: 他给我看了一篇别人写的关于他离开节目的文章。

sentences.en: Like he was, you know, because this was just before he left.
sentences.zh: 就像他，你知道，因为这就在他离开之前。

sentences.en: And the article was like why Jon Stewart cannot leave the show and why America needs him and why Jon Stewart has to. and it was just this effusive article about like the 10 ways that john stewart is the heart of american he cannot leave and john showed me that and he's like huh and he's john's like doesn't take himself seriously at all so john was like huh and i was like yeah and he's like huh huh and i'm like yeah congrats i mean you crushed it he's like no no i crushed it i'm important to america and we laughed and then he goes hold on now and he types something in and then he pulls up an article from like years ago, years and years and years ago, but it was like not, wait, it wasn't that far.
sentences.zh: 文章标题是为什么Jon Stewart不能离开节目，为什么美国需要他，为什么Jon Stewart必须。那是一篇关于Jon Stewart是美国的心脏的溢美之词，他不能离开，Jon给我看了那个，他说，嗯，而且他是，Jon是不把自己当回事的人，所以Jon说，嗯，我说，是的，他说，嗯，嗯，我说，是的，恭喜，我的意思是，你太棒了，他说，不，不，我太棒了，我对美国很重要，我们笑了，然后他说，等一下，现在，他输入了一些东西，然后他调出了一篇很久以前的文章，很多很多年以前，但它不是，等等，没那么远。

sentences.en: It was like three years prior, two years prior.
sentences.zh: 那是大约三年前，两年前。

sentences.en: So he was like at his prime, but it was like two, three years before that.
sentences.zh: 所以他处于巅峰时期，但那是大约两三年前。

sentences.en: And it was like, why Jon Stewart needs to leave The Daily Show?
sentences.zh: 标题是为什么Jon Stewart需要离开《The Daily Show》？

sentences.en: It's over for him. He's the worst of America.
sentences.zh: 对他来说结束了。他是美国最差的。

sentences.en: He's not good for this country. This whole article just like slamming him.
sentences.zh: 他不适合这个国家。整篇文章都在抨击他。

sentences.en: And he's like, you see? And I was like, oh yeah, I guess, you know, things can, he's like, no, no, no, you're not looking at the right thing.
sentences.zh: 他说，你看到了吗？我说，哦，是的，我想，你知道，事情可以，他说，不，不，不，你没看对地方。

sentences.en: And he's like, look who wrote it. and it was the same journalist.
sentences.zh: 他说，看是谁写的。是同一个记者。

sentences.en: So when John was in, they were like, this guy needs to leave.
sentences.zh: 所以当John在任时，他们说，这家伙需要离开。

sentences.en: And then when John was leaving, they were like, oh, this guy needs to stay.
sentences.zh: 然后当John要离开时，他们说，哦，这家伙需要留下来。

sentences.en: And he looked at me and he said to me, please understand that to me, he said to many people, I have always been obvious, but he said, I know my road and I wasn't.
sentences.zh: 他看着我说，请理解，对我来说，他说，对许多人来说，我一直很明显，但他说，我知道我的路，我不是。

sentences.en: And he wasn't. You know, when John took over the show, Craig Kilbourne had been the previous host.
sentences.zh: 他不是。你知道，当John接手节目时，Craig Kilbourne是上一任主持人。

sentences.en: People thought John couldn't do it. If you said that today, people would burn you at a stake.
sentences.zh: 人们认为John做不到。如果你今天说这个，人们会把你绑在火刑柱上烧死。

sentences.en: Be like, are you crazy? What do you mean John Stewart can't do it?
sentences.zh: 会说，你疯了吗？你是什么意思Jon Stewart做不到？

sentences.en: That's what people said about him. And he was one of those people who said to me, he's like, hey man, I've been there and maybe people don't remember it because it was like pre-internet.
sentences.zh: 这就是人们对他说的。他是那些对我说的人之一，他说，嘿，伙计，我经历过，也许人们不记得了，因为那是前互联网时代。

sentences.en: But he was like, put your head down. And this is part of the journey.
sentences.zh: 但他就像是，低下头。这是旅程的一部分。

sentences.en: And I leaned on him. I leaned on the other people.
sentences.zh: 我依靠他。我依靠其他人。

sentences.en: And it was just like, you know, just like a slow, you know, boring slog, you know, filled with many funny and sad moments.
sentences.zh: 这就像，你知道，就像一个缓慢的，你知道，无聊的苦差事，你知道，充满了许多有趣和悲伤的时刻。

sentences.en: And then one day it seems obvious to people from the outside.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天，从外面看，一切似乎都很明显。

sentences.en: And when you go home on those days and you're alone in your apartment or at home in your house, and you're not around the guy that wants the lunch and the colleagues at work, what is that like?
sentences.zh: 当你那些日子回家，独自在公寓或家里时，你不在那个想要午餐的家伙和同事身边，那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: I read that you're someone that suffered with depression periodically throughout your life, your adult life as well.
sentences.zh: 我读到你是一个在成年生活中周期性地遭受抑郁症困扰的人。

sentences.en: Were you suffering in that period when you were alone?
sentences.zh: 你在独自一人的那段时间里受苦吗？

sentences.en: I didn't realize at the time that the depression that I was suffering from was ADHD depression.
sentences.zh: 我当时没意识到我所遭受的抑郁症是ADHD抑郁症。

sentences.en: It wasn't like depression, depression. And I've learned since that there's a difference.
sentences.zh: 它不像抑郁症，抑郁症。我后来了解到是有区别的。

sentences.en: So I related to many ideas in and around depression.
sentences.zh: 所以我与抑郁症及其周围的许多想法产生了共鸣。

sentences.en: But I remember being confused because I was like, I'm not depressed perpetually, but I definitely experienced these moments.
sentences.zh: 但我记得我很困惑，因为我当时想，我不是永久抑郁，但我确实经历了这些时刻。

sentences.en: I didn't know that ADHD can do that to you.
sentences.zh: 我不知道ADHD会那样对你。

sentences.en: I didn't know that it can be like a byproduct of untreated ADHD and not knowing that you have ADHD.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它可能是未经治疗的ADHD的副产品，而不知道你有ADHD。

sentences.en: So that's just like a footnote there.
sentences.zh: 所以那只是一个脚注。

sentences.en: But it's funny you say that when you went home and you see, I wasn't alone.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是你说，当你回家时，你看，我并不孤单。

sentences.en: And that's probably the reason I survived.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我幸存下来的原因。

sentences.en: So David was with me every single day. He had moved from South Africa.
sentences.zh: 所以David每天都和我在一起。他从南非搬来了。

sentences.en: We started like a comedy night together.
sentences.zh: 我们一起开始了喜剧之夜。

sentences.en: That's how long we had been working together.
sentences.zh: 我们一起工作了那么久。

sentences.en: So we would walk out of that building together On the hottest nights in New York And on the coldest nights in New York And we would go back And we lived together in the same apartment And then we'd open like our notebooks And we'd be like, alright What could we have done better?
sentences.zh: 所以我们会一起走出那栋楼，在纽约最热的夜晚，在纽约最冷的夜晚，我们会回去，我们住在同一个公寓里，然后我们会打开我们的笔记本，我们会说，好吧，我们能做得更好吗？

sentences.en: And we would just sit there And we'd be like, what could we have done better?
sentences.zh: 我们只是坐在那儿，我们会说，我们能做得更好吗？

sentences.en: And we'd get home at like 8 or 9pm And then we'd work until midnight Go to bed, get back to the office at 7, 8 the next day And do it all over again And then we'd come home in the evening And be like, what were the wins?
sentences.zh: 我们会在晚上8点或9点回家，然后工作到午夜，睡觉，第二天7点、8点回到办公室，一切重来，然后我们晚上回家，说，赢在哪里？

sentences.en: What could we have done better? and we would just do this over and over.
sentences.zh: 我们能做得更好吗？我们会一遍又一遍地这样做。

sentences.en: But I was never alone. And so I never think of it, you know, that's why I wish like more people would share their stories in that way is because I think we live in a world where so many people sell an idea of perseverance as an individualistic pursuit when it's not.
sentences.zh: 但我从不孤单。所以我从不那样想它，你知道，这就是为什么我希望更多的人能以那种方式分享他们的故事，因为我认为我们生活在一个世界里，很多人把坚持不懈作为一种个人主义的追求来兜售，而事实并非如此。

sentences.en: I think too many people forget the pats on the back and the hugs and the encouragements and the load liftings, they forget all of it.
sentences.zh: 我认为太多人忘记了拍拍肩膀、拥抱和鼓励以及减轻负担，他们忘记了这一切。

sentences.en: They see their suffering, they see their success, and then they go out and sell to the world how you got to persevere.
sentences.zh: 他们看到他们的痛苦，他们看到他们的成功，然后他们走出去向世界兜售你如何坚持不懈。

sentences.en: Let me tell you what, in the darkest times, let me tell you what I did, Steve, and I looked at myself in the mirror and I said, Trevor, you're going to do it, Trevor.
sentences.zh: 让我告诉你，在最黑暗的时刻，让我告诉你我做了什么，Steve，我看着镜子里的自己，我说，Trevor，你会做到的，Trevor。

sentences.en: You're going to be the man at the Daily Show.
sentences.zh: 你会成为《The Daily Show》的那个人。

sentences.en: You're going to... Yeah, but everyone forgets.
sentences.zh: 你会……是的，但每个人都忘了。

sentences.en: They're like, no, your friend was there going like, do you want to go get some chicken wings?
sentences.zh: 他们就像，不，你的朋友在那儿说，你想去吃炸鸡翅吗？

sentences.en: Let's go get some chicken wings. There was somebody accepting you despite your failure.
sentences.zh: 我们去吃炸鸡翅吧。有人在接受你，尽管你失败了。

sentences.en: There was somebody who was reminding you of that part of you that you always wish to be, which is somebody who can solve a puzzle, is somebody who enjoys what they're doing, is somebody who perseveres.
sentences.zh: 有人在提醒你那个你一直希望成为的自己，那就是一个能解决难题的人，是一个享受自己所做之事的人，是一个坚持不懈的人。

sentences.en: But there they're looking at that side of me.
sentences.zh: 但他们在那儿看着我的那一面。

sentences.en: And so I wasn't alone. It was me, it was David, it was Joseph Opio, guy who was random, is now one of my best friends, a writer from Uganda who did the Daily Show, like a version of the Daily Show in Uganda.
sentences.zh: 所以我并不孤单。是我，是David，是Joseph Opio，一个随机的家伙，现在是我最好的朋友之一，一个来自乌干达的编剧，他做了《The Daily Show》，就像乌干达版的《The Daily Show》。

sentences.en: What a, like this weird world coming together.
sentences.zh: 多么，就像这个奇怪的世界走到了一起。

sentences.en: You meet us today, you'll think we've known each other our whole lives, but he was also, he was just there.
sentences.zh: 你今天遇见我们，你会认为我们一辈子都认识，但他也是，他就在那儿。

sentences.en: And he's like, I believe in us. He's like, I think we can do this.
sentences.zh: 他说，我相信我们。他说，我想我们可以做到。

sentences.en: I think we can do it. I think we can do it.
sentences.zh: 我想我们可以做到。我想我们可以做到。

sentences.en: But if you were going at home alone? Then I wouldn't be here with you.
sentences.zh: 但如果你独自一人在家？那我就不会和你在这儿了。

sentences.en: I will put all my money on that. I would not be here with you.
sentences.zh: 我会把我所有的钱都押在那上面。我不会和你在这儿。

sentences.en: I don't even think I would have taken the Daily Show.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不认为我会接手《The Daily Show》。

sentences.en: I wouldn't have done the Daily Show. When you say you wouldn't be here with me, what do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 我不会做《The Daily Show》。当你说明明你不会和我在这儿时，你是什么意思？

sentences.en: You wouldn't be calling me here to have an interview with me?
sentences.zh: 你不会叫我来这里接受采访吗？

sentences.en: Because I wouldn't have done the things that I've done.
sentences.zh: 因为我不会做我做过的事情。

sentences.en: Because I couldn't have done them alone.
sentences.zh: 因为我不能独自完成它们。

sentences.en: Because nobody could have done them alone.
sentences.zh: 因为没有人能独自完成它们。

sentences.en: Nobody has done the things they've done alone.
sentences.zh: 没有人独自完成了他们所做的事情。

sentences.en: You know? Like everyone, I've seen people tell these stories of climbing Mount Everest and my ascent and my...
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？就像每个人，我见过人们讲述这些攀登珠穆朗玛峰的故事，我的攀登，我的……

sentences.en: Yo, all those Sherpas that went with you.
sentences.zh: 哟，所有那些和你一起去的夏尔巴人。

sentences.en: Let's talk about them. No one's climbing Everest alone.
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈他们。没有人独自攀登珠穆朗玛峰。

sentences.en: No one's discovering, you know, the South Pole alone.
sentences.zh: 没有人独自发现南极。

sentences.en: No, you weren't. In fact, the person was the guy who just like first navigated the South Pole was led there by somebody.
sentences.zh: 不，你没有。事实上，第一个导航南极的人是被某人带到那里的。

sentences.en: You know what I mean? All these stories that we tell, self-made.
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？我们讲述的所有这些故事，白手起家。

sentences.en: Oh, I love that phrase. It's my favorite.
sentences.zh: 哦，我喜欢那个短语。这是我最喜欢的。

sentences.en: Self-made billionaire. Oh, really? Oh, it's an interesting choice of words.
sentences.zh: 白手起家的亿万富翁。哦，真的吗？哦，这是一个有趣的词选择。

sentences.en: So you just did this all by yourself. You made the thing by yourself with your hands.
sentences.zh: 所以你只是独自一人完成了这一切。你用你的双手独自制造了东西。

sentences.en: You made many more of them by yourself. You drove the trucks.
sentences.zh: 你独自制造了更多。你开了卡车。

sentences.en: You thought of all the ideas. You put it in the stores.
sentences.zh: 你想到了所有的想法。你把它放进商店。

sentences.en: You gave it to the people. You took the money.
sentences.zh: 你把它给了人们。你拿了钱。

sentences.en: You invested it. You grew it all by yourself, all by yourself.
sentences.zh: 你投资了它。你独自一人，完全独自一人让它成长。

sentences.en: All the ideas were from your head, all by yourself.
sentences.zh: 所有的想法都来自你的头脑，完全独自一人。

sentences.en: And then you got there. Come on. There's no such thing.
sentences.zh: 然后你到了那儿。得了吧。没有那种事。

sentences.en: And I don't think it diminishes your achievement.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这削弱了你的成就。

sentences.en: I just think it's important because it helps people understand that they need other people to get to where they're trying to get to.
sentences.zh: 我只是认为这很重要，因为它帮助人们理解他们需要其他人才能到达他们想要到达的地方。

sentences.en: And maybe sometimes the reason you're not experiencing that is because you're trying to do it alone.
sentences.zh: 也许有时你没有经历这一点的原因是因为你试图独自完成它。

sentences.en: I hear people all the time go like, I'm going to put my head down and I'm going to crush it.
sentences.zh: 我一直听到人们说，我要低下头，我要大干一场。

sentences.en: Okay, alone, good luck.
sentences.zh: 好吧，独自一人，祝你好运。

sentences.en: Good luck. And I think it creates an unrealistic expectation for people.
sentences.zh: 祝你好运。我认为这给人们创造了一个不切实际的期望。

sentences.en: People who studied together in school got better marks.
sentences.zh: 在学校一起学习的人分数更高。

sentences.en: There was just like a simple thing that we learned in our school when I was growing up.
sentences.zh: 我长大时在学校学到了一件简单的事情。

sentences.en: If you had a study partner, you just learned more.
sentences.zh: 如果你有一个学习伙伴，你学到的更多。

sentences.en: The idea of the Sherpas is such a good analogy Because the Sherpas never really get the credit in the story They never mentioned in the article But they're lifting most of the bloody weight And they're literally keeping you alive Yeah They've ascended Everest More than the most celebrated Everest ascender How are they not the ones It's the equivalent of finding out that like Somebody ran carrying Usain Bolt But then we don't consider them the fastest man alive Yeah You know And so I don't know.
sentences.zh: 夏尔巴人的想法是一个很好的类比，因为夏尔巴人在故事中从未真正得到赞誉，他们在文章中从未被提及，但他们承担了大部分该死的重量，他们实际上让你活着。是的，他们攀登珠穆朗玛峰的次数比最著名的珠穆朗玛峰攀登者还要多。他们怎么不是那些人？这相当于发现有人背着Usain Bolt跑，但我们不认为他们是世界上跑得最快的人。是的，你知道，所以我不知道。

sentences.en: So I'm always cautious to think of that because it doesn't, like I say, it doesn't diminish what you've done.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是谨慎地思考这一点，因为它不会，就像我说的，它不会削弱你所做的事情。

sentences.en: But man, you're not doing it alone. And to realize that I think helps you to understand why it's important to have those people and why it then brings joy.
sentences.zh: 但伙计，你不是独自完成的。意识到这一点，我认为有助于你理解为什么拥有那些人很重要，以及为什么它会带来快乐。

sentences.en: Why did you leave The Daily Show? Because the moment you left The Daily Show, you'd won these huge awards.
sentences.zh: 你为什么离开《The Daily Show》？因为你离开《The Daily Show》的那一刻，你赢得了这些巨大的奖项。

sentences.en: The show had caused this sort of digital revolution, which we hadn't seen before. where the Daily Show had become, you know, from my experience of the Daily Show was much more of an online show than it had ever been before.
sentences.zh: 节目引发了这种数字革命，这是我们以前没见过的。在我的经验中，《The Daily Show》比以往任何时候都更像是一档在线节目。

sentences.en: Most of the time I watched the Daily Show, I'd be watching it on YouTube or I'd be watching it on clips that were going around the internet.
sentences.zh: 我大部分时间看《The Daily Show》，都是在YouTube上看，或者看在互联网上传播的片段。

sentences.en: You know, the billions and billions of views it was doing at that point.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它当时获得的数十亿次观看。

sentences.en: Why would someone leave that situation? I don't know why someone would leave it.
sentences.zh: 为什么有人会离开那种情况？我不知道为什么有人会离开它。

sentences.en: Why did you leave it? Because it was time.
sentences.zh: 你为什么离开它？因为是时候了。

sentences.en: It was just time. How'd you know?
sentences.zh: 只是时间到了。你怎么知道的？

sentences.en: I don't know. that's something I've always felt I've known in life.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。那是我一生中一直觉得我知道的事情。

sentences.en: And I don't know why. Like the fight? Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么。喜欢战斗？是的。

sentences.en: But not in a negative way. This is more...
sentences.zh: 但不是以消极的方式。这更多是……

sentences.en: Okay, so here's the thing. I think part of it comes from where I am from.
sentences.zh: 好吧，事情是这样的。我认为部分原因来自我来自哪里。

sentences.en: And maybe you'll relate to this as somebody from the UK.
sentences.zh: 也许作为来自英国的人，你会对此产生共鸣。

sentences.en: In South Africa, TV shows end.
sentences.zh: 在南非，电视节目会结束。

sentences.en: We've never had a TV show, except maybe like one soap opera, But we never had TV shows that run for 10 seasons or 20 seasons.
sentences.zh: 我们从来没有过电视节目，除了可能像一部肥皂剧，但我们从来没有过运行10季或20季的电视节目。

sentences.en: That's not a thing. It ends. And it doesn't end because it's bad.
sentences.zh: 那不是一回事。它结束了。它结束不是因为它不好。

sentences.en: It ends. It just ends. And I look at some of my favorite creators of things, you know, like I look at like Seinfeld.
sentences.zh: 它结束了。它只是结束了。我看看我最喜欢的一些创作者，你知道，就像Seinfeld。

sentences.en: They were like, all right, it's done. The network was like, we can give you more.
sentences.zh: 他们就像，好吧，结束了。电视网就像，我们可以给你更多。

sentences.en: We can do more. They're like, yeah, but it's done.
sentences.zh: 我们可以做更多。他们就像，是的，但结束了。

sentences.en: We just feel like it's done.
sentences.zh: 我们只是觉得它结束了。

sentences.en: You know? Sometimes things can be done. And for me, I think there were multiple reasons.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？有时事情可以结束。对我来说，我认为有多个原因。

sentences.en: One was definitely the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 一个是绝对是疫情。

sentences.en: I took for granted that the pandemic was a moment where many people were forced to be at home.
sentences.zh: 我理所当然地认为疫情是一个许多人被迫待在家里的时刻。

sentences.en: But then, you know, the silver lining of that terrible period for many people was that they got to like, just like pause for a moment.
sentences.zh: 但后来，你知道，那个对许多人来说可怕时期的亮点是他们能够，只是像暂停一下。

sentences.en: You know, many people will tell you the story of how they're like, man, during the pandemic, I just like paused.
sentences.zh: 你知道，许多人会告诉你他们是如何，就像，伙计，在疫情期间，我只是暂停了。

sentences.en: And I, you know, we didn't, I didn't. I was making the show from home.
sentences.zh: 而我，你知道，我们没有，我没有。我在家里制作节目。

sentences.en: And I was just going at it. And I'm really glad and I'm lucky that I got to do that because it sort of shielded me from some of the panic that came with the pandemic of what are you doing?
sentences.zh: 我只是在做。我真的很高兴，我很幸运我能做到这一点，因为它在某种程度上保护我免受疫情带来的一些恐慌，你在做什么？

sentences.en: What are you not doing? Where's life going?
sentences.zh: 你没做什么？生活要去哪里？

sentences.en: I was just like, I'm just doing my show.
sentences.zh: 我只是想，我只是在做我的节目。

sentences.en: I'm just doing the show. I'm doing the show.
sentences.zh: 我只是在做节目。我在做节目。

sentences.en: I'm doing the show. Find a way to do it from home.
sentences.zh: 我在做节目。找到一种在家里做的方法。

sentences.en: Shoot it using iPhones. We didn't even have like cameras.
sentences.zh: 用iPhone拍摄。我们甚至没有摄像机。

sentences.en: We didn't have a crew. We didn't have anyone.
sentences.zh: 我们没有剧组。我们没有任何人。

sentences.en: It was just me, David, because he lived in the same building.
sentences.zh: 只有我，David，因为他住在同一栋楼里。

sentences.en: And then the other David. And it was just three people, you know, physically making a thing that's supposed to take many, many, many people, you know, but here you are and you're this, but you're virtual and you're not in the same room as people and you can't travel.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个David。只有三个人，你知道，实际上在制作一个本应需要许多许多人制作的东西，你知道，但你在这儿，你是虚拟的，你和人们不在同一个房间里，你不能旅行。

sentences.en: And I was experiencing all of this. I couldn't go back to South Africa.
sentences.zh: 我正在经历这一切。我不能回到南非。

sentences.en: I couldn't travel the world. And one of the big things I learned during the pandemic was I had made my life about work and I had made everything else secondary.
sentences.zh: 我不能环游世界。我在疫情期间学到的重要事情之一是，我把我的生活变成了工作，我让其他一切都成了次要的。

sentences.en: So I would see my friends if I did not have work.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我没有工作，我会见我的朋友。

sentences.en: I would travel with my friends if I did not have work.
sentences.zh: 如果我没有工作，我会和我的朋友一起旅行。

sentences.en: I would come to your wedding if I did not have work.
sentences.zh: 如果我没有工作，我会参加你的婚礼。

sentences.en: But work was the thing. And everyone in my life knew this.
sentences.zh: 但工作是那件事。我生活中的每个人都知道这一点。

sentences.en: They were like, oh yeah, work. You know, Trevor, if you're not working, can you?
sentences.zh: 他们就像，哦，是的，工作。你知道，Trevor，如果你不工作，你能吗？

sentences.en: They'd almost say that to me. And on the other side of the pandemic, I realized I was like, I can do the Daily Show.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎会那样对我说。在疫情的另一边，我意识到我当时想，我可以做《The Daily Show》。

sentences.en: I looked up and I was like, wow, it's been eight years of me being at the Daily Show.
sentences.zh: 我抬头看，我想，哇，我在《The Daily Show》已经八年了。

sentences.en: Seven years of me hosting. one year of me being a contributor at times when Jon Stewart was there.
sentences.zh: 我主持了七年。有一年我是在Jon Stewart在的时候做贡献者。

sentences.en: But I was like, you sort of can do this forever, but maybe.
sentences.zh: 但我当时想，你某种程度上可以永远这样做，但也许。

sentences.en: But what else can you do? Where else can you be?
sentences.zh: 但你还能做什么？你还能去哪儿？

sentences.en: How can you spend your time? What would you like to do and how would you like to do it?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能花你的时间？你想做什么，你想怎么做？

sentences.en: I learned so many things at The Daily Show.
sentences.zh: 我在《The Daily Show》学到了很多东西。

sentences.en: I'm eternally grateful for them. But I also would like to learn more things. even in the years that I haven't been there, I've relearned and re-remembered that politics isn't a binary.
sentences.zh: 我永远感激他们。但我也想学更多的东西。即使在我不在那里的几年里，我也重新学习并重新记住了政治不是二元的。

sentences.en: It's not blue and red. That's an illusion.
sentences.zh: 不是蓝色和红色。那是一种幻觉。

sentences.en: There aren't two ideas for every problem.
sentences.zh: 每一个问题并不只有两种观点。

sentences.en: That's fake. There are a multitude of ways to discuss any issue and any topic.
sentences.zh: 那是假的。讨论任何议题和话题都有多种方式。

sentences.en: But if you stay in one place for long enough, then in a good way and in a bad way, you start to perceive that as as reality and so you know there were many things when it when it came to me leaving the daily show but i i just felt like yeah it's time you know scared scared yeah of of sometimes people get scared when they have such a high post in society um that they might be losing something they could never get back or they might you know it oh that's fascinating i'm thinking about the average person listening to this now who's in their job and they might might be a lawyer who's climbed the ladder yeah and they've got this sort of internal voice saying something isn't right here but this fear that keeps them trapped in place is the loss aversion even if you're miserable this power of loss aversion can just hold people in place i read this crazy study with dr daniel kahn and i believe it was daniel kahneman the famous yeah yeah right He did the studies where if you drop like a dollar on the floor, the pain of losing the dollar is equal to the pain of finding three.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在一个地方待得足够久，无论好坏，你都会开始把这种状态视为现实。所以，你知道，我离开The Daily Show有很多原因，但我只是觉得，是时候了。你知道，人们在社会上身居高位时，有时会感到害怕，担心失去一些永远无法挽回的东西，或者担心……哦，这太引人入胜了。我想到现在听节目的普通人，他们可能是一名律师，已经爬到了职业生涯的高处，内心有个声音在说‘这里有些不对劲’，但这种恐惧让他们被困在原地，这就是损失厌恶。即使你过得很痛苦，这种损失厌恶的力量也能让人原地踏步。我读过一项关于Daniel Kahneman博士的疯狂研究，我相信是那位著名的Daniel Kahneman，对，没错。他做过研究，如果你在地上掉了一美元，失去这一美元的痛苦，等同于捡到三美元带来的快乐。

sentences.en: Yes. So in life, you don't just need equal reward to sacrifice something.
sentences.zh: 是的。所以在生活中，你需要的不仅仅是等量的回报来做出牺牲。

sentences.en: You need two or three times the reward to leave.
sentences.zh: 你需要两到三倍的回报才愿意离开。

sentences.en: Well, I will say this. First and foremost, I was lucky I wasn't miserable.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我会这么说。首先，我很幸运，我并不痛苦。

sentences.en: You know, I wasn't like, I didn't have like a, I hate this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我并不是那种‘我讨厌这个’的状态。

sentences.en: No, but I did want to turn and focus my life on something more.
sentences.zh: 不，但我确实想转变方向，把生活重心放在更有意义的事情上。

sentences.en: More? Yeah, like I wanted to spend more time with my loved ones.
sentences.zh: 更多？是的，比如我想花更多时间陪伴我爱的人。

sentences.en: I wanted to spend more time with my people.
sentences.zh: 我想花更多时间陪伴我的人民。

sentences.en: I wanted to spend more time in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 我想花更多时间在南非。

sentences.en: I wanted to spend more time learning other languages and traveling.
sentences.zh: 我想花更多时间学习其他语言和旅行。

sentences.en: I wanted to spend more time practicing comedy in other countries.
sentences.zh: 我想花更多时间在其他国家练习喜剧。

sentences.en: Was that a feeling? Yeah. And what is that feeling?
sentences.zh: 那是一种感觉吗？是的。那是什么样的感觉？

sentences.en: Because I'm trying to understand the feeling or the emotion that tells you that.
sentences.zh: 因为我正试图理解那种告诉你这些的感觉或情绪。

sentences.en: So I guess it goes to the now sort of cliche, but still, I think, very apt phrase.
sentences.zh: 我想这归结于那句老生常谈，但我认为依然非常贴切的话。

sentences.en: You don't know what you've got till it's gone.
sentences.zh: 失去了才懂得珍惜。

sentences.en: The pandemic showed me like all the things.
sentences.zh: 疫情让我看到了所有的一切。

sentences.en: I even talk about this for people. It showed me all the things that I didn't value that I should have. like when the pandemic hits if we're honest we didn't care that we couldn't go to the movies or we couldn't like it's not it's not about the stuff it's that we couldn't do it with our people you couldn't see your friends you couldn't be with other human beings you couldn't be in a space together where people are cheering or singing or laughing or you you couldn't be with people and I don't know about you but during the pandemic I wasn't sitting there thinking to myself oh, I work.
sentences.zh: 我甚至和别人谈论过这个。它让我看到了所有我本该重视却没重视的东西。比如疫情来袭时，说实话，我们并不在乎不能去看电影或不能做其他事，重点不在于这些东西，而在于我们不能和我们的人在一起。你见不到朋友，不能和其他人在一起，不能待在一个大家一起欢呼、唱歌或大笑的空间里。你无法与人相处。我不知道你怎么样，但在疫情期间，我并没有坐在那里想‘哦，我工作’。

sentences.en: Work is the thing I could do more of. No, I was thinking to myself, wow, my people.
sentences.zh: 工作是我可以多做一点的事情。不，我当时在想，哇，我的人民。

sentences.en: All my friends that are South African were trapped in South Africa, couldn't leave, couldn't come to me.
sentences.zh: 我所有的南非朋友都被困在南非，无法离开，无法来找我。

sentences.en: I couldn't go to them, couldn't see my family.
sentences.zh: 我无法去找他们，无法见到我的家人。

sentences.en: And I wasn't even big on that. It's not even like I was like, I've always got to go home to see my family.
sentences.zh: 我以前甚至没那么在意这些。并不是说我一直觉得必须回家看望家人。

sentences.en: I just go when I go. But now I realize like, wow, this is just, again, it's fleeting.
sentences.zh: 我只是想去的时候就去。但现在我意识到，哇，这一切真的转瞬即逝。

sentences.en: And I had to ask myself, Trevor, what are you trying to achieve in your life?
sentences.zh: 我不得不问自己，Trevor，你一生想要实现什么？

sentences.en: Where do you want it to go? Where do you want it to end?
sentences.zh: 你想让它走向何方？你想让它如何收场？

sentences.en: You know, what's more important to you, the ratings and the success of this show and this idea, or the ratings and the success of your friendships and your relationships?
sentences.zh: 你知道，什么对你更重要？是这个节目的收视率和成功，还是你友谊和人际关系的收视率和成功？

sentences.en: You know, and I do think in life, you have to let go of something old to grab onto something new.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我确实认为在生活中，你必须放下旧的东西才能抓住新的东西。

sentences.en: And that was a decision for me that because I couldn't, I can't be in two places at once.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是一个决定，因为我无法同时身处两地。

sentences.en: And the daily show is all consuming. You cannot be, you know, sort of part time in it as an idea.
sentences.zh: 而且The Daily Show是全方位的消耗。你不能以一种‘兼职’的心态来对待它。

sentences.en: You know, in fact, John and I joke now, but now he gets to do it weekly.
sentences.zh: 你知道，事实上，Jon和我现在开玩笑，但他现在每周做一次。

sentences.en: And I think if anything, he'd never go back to doing it daily because he knows how all consuming it can be.
sentences.zh: 我想如果说有什么的话，他永远不会再回去做日播了，因为他知道这有多消耗人。

sentences.en: Like I didn't just do the daily show when I was there.
sentences.zh: 就像我当时在The Daily Show时，我不仅仅是在做节目。

sentences.en: I would do the daily show when I was there and then I would leave and I would read the news and I'll keep up with the news and I'll try and keep up with all the news.
sentences.zh: 我做完节目离开后，我会读新闻，跟进新闻，试图跟上所有的新闻。

sentences.en: And I'm reading the Guardian and I'm reading BBC and then I'm reading like right-wing sites.
sentences.zh: 我读《卫报》，读BBC，然后读右翼网站。

sentences.en: I'm reading Breitbart and I'm reading what's on conservative media.
sentences.zh: 我读Breitbart，读保守派媒体的内容。

sentences.en: And then I'm reading, you know, The Telegraph and The Economist.
sentences.zh: 然后我读《每日电讯报》和《经济学人》。

sentences.en: And that's all I'm doing, consuming news, news, news, news, news, news, news, news, get more news, get more news.
sentences.zh: 我所做的就是消费新闻，新闻，新闻，新闻，获取更多新闻。

sentences.en: Barely read a fiction book in years. It's like more news.
sentences.zh: 好几年几乎没读过小说。就像是更多的新闻。
