sentences.en: I need information and news. Okay. Economist, analysis, what's happening?
sentences.zh: 我需要信息和新闻。好的。《经济学人》，分析，发生了什么？

sentences.en: How do I put this together? What's happening?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么把这些拼凑起来？发生了什么？

sentences.en: Al Jazeera. Okay. Okay. Think about that.
sentences.zh: 半岛电视台。好的。好的。想想看。

sentences.en: What's going on in the times of India? What's happening?
sentences.zh: 《印度时报》发生了什么？发生了什么？

sentences.en: What's happening? What's happening? What's happening?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？发生了什么？发生了什么？

sentences.en: It's a law. Yeah. It's too much. It's a law in the brain.
sentences.zh: 这是一种定律。是的。太多了。这是大脑的一种定律。

sentences.en: It's too much. and especially for someone with your brain if I say so myself from what how you've described it someone who's so sort of hypersensitive and aware um and someone who appears to me to be a little bit of an empath I you said you know when we said yeah right yeah you're good at yeah you feel things yeah I the you know what it did teach me and this is something I tell everyone until this day give yourself a break from the news give yourself a break we've we've we've been told and we've been conditioned to believe that we all need to keep up with the news, it's a lie.
sentences.zh: 太多了。尤其是对于像你这样的大脑，如果我这么说的话，从你的描述来看，一个如此敏感和清醒的人，一个在我看来有点共情能力的人。你刚才说，当我说‘对，没错’时，你很擅长感受事物。你知道它教会了我什么吗？直到今天我还在告诉每个人：给自己放个假，别看新闻，给自己放个假。我们一直被告知，也被灌输了一种观念，认为我们都需要跟上新闻，那是谎言。

sentences.en: It's an illusion.
sentences.zh: 那是一种幻觉。

sentences.en: You'll know what's happening. In fact, if you read the news once a week...
sentences.zh: 你会知道发生了什么。事实上，如果你每周读一次新闻……

sentences.en: I promise you, you'll be as informed as somebody who's reading it every single day.
sentences.zh: 我保证，你了解到的信息量和每天读新闻的人是一样的。

sentences.en: You know why? Because when you're reading it every day, you are caught in the cycle of it trying to discover what it doesn't know yet.
sentences.zh: 你知道为什么吗？因为当你每天读新闻时，你陷入了试图发现未知事物的循环中。

sentences.en: Developing story, developing story, developing story.
sentences.zh: 突发新闻，突发新闻，突发新闻。

sentences.en: You'll be shocked at what you learn when you just read a story that sort of had the time that it needed to breathe.
sentences.zh: 当你读到一篇经过沉淀、有足够时间去呼吸的故事时，你会惊讶于自己学到了什么。

sentences.en: There's less predicting, there's less guessing, there's less pontificating.
sentences.zh: 预测少了，猜测少了，夸夸其谈也少了。

sentences.en: It's just like, this is what happened and this is what we know and that's it when was the first time you went to therapy first time i went to therapy was uh 2015 2014 somewhere there yeah why did you go to therapy i i asked this because um for a set of reasons really but um men in particular and in fact if you look at the stats men of color are often the least likely to go to therapy and there's of complex reasons why that is.
sentences.zh: 它只是说：这就是发生的事，这就是我们所知道的，仅此而已。你第一次去心理咨询是什么时候？我第一次去咨询是在2015年或2014年左右。为什么去咨询？我问这个是因为……原因有很多，但特别是男性，事实上如果你看统计数据，有色人种男性往往最不可能去心理咨询，这背后有复杂的原因。

sentences.en: But I think it's quite important for men that have been to therapy, including myself, to talk about why they went and also sort of the journey they've been on with it, but also the role that it's played.
sentences.zh: 但我认为对于去过心理咨询的男性（包括我自己）来说，谈谈为什么去、他们经历的旅程以及咨询所起的作用，是非常重要的。

sentences.en: So I'll say it in two parts. So I went to therapy because I fell in love with the idea that I could learn more about myself and why I was the way I was from somebody who was skilled in understanding it.
sentences.zh: 所以我分两部分来说。我去咨询是因为我爱上了这样一种想法：我可以从一个擅长理解这些的人那里，更多地了解自己以及我为什么会是现在的样子。

sentences.en: In the same way that I loved physical therapy, I was like, wow, you can move your body differently.
sentences.zh: 就像我喜欢物理治疗一样，我当时想，哇，你可以让身体以不同的方式活动。

sentences.en: If you've ever had physical therapy, you know what I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 如果你做过物理治疗，你就知道我在说什么。

sentences.en: And if you haven't, you should go one day if you have anything wrong with you long before you consider surgery and things.
sentences.zh: 如果你没做过，如果你身体有任何不适，在考虑手术之前，你应该去试一次。

sentences.en: You'll be shocked. You'll be shocked at how your neck hasn't been moving the way it's supposed to.
sentences.zh: 你会感到震惊的。你会惊讶于你的脖子竟然一直没有按照它应该的方式活动。

sentences.en: You'll be shocked to realize that your back has been stuck for a while.
sentences.zh: 你会惊讶地发现你的背部已经僵硬很久了。

sentences.en: You haven't been breathing. You'll find that your knees haven't been...
sentences.zh: 你一直没有好好呼吸。你会发现你的膝盖……

sentences.en: You say that. No, but really, it's actually crazy to realize how much over time you've settled into a restriction that's stopping you from being yourself fully physically, but mentally as well.
sentences.zh: 你这么说。不，但真的，意识到随着时间的推移，你已经习惯了一种限制，这种限制不仅在身体上，而且在心理上阻止你成为完整的自己，这真的很疯狂。

sentences.en: Patterns, and as you said, games of snap, where you don't even realize you're now just reacting.
sentences.zh: 模式，正如你所说的，像玩‘拍手游戏’一样，你甚至没有意识到自己只是在做出反应。

sentences.en: Things are happening and you're reacting to them. and I read a bunch of books.
sentences.zh: 事情发生了，你就在做出反应。我读了很多书。

sentences.en: I was like, wow, this is fascinating. But I was like, none of it like tells me about me per se.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，哇，这太迷人了。但我发现没有一本书能真正告诉我关于我自己的事。

sentences.en: It's very broad. And so I decided, let me go to this place to try and learn about who I am or if there's even a puzzle that I can learn a little bit more about.
sentences.zh: 它们太笼统了。所以我决定，让我去那个地方，试着了解我是谁，或者看看是否有一个关于我自己的谜题，我可以多了解一点。

sentences.en: How did that feel the first time you went, but also telling your friends that you're going to therapy?
sentences.zh: 第一次去的时候感觉如何？还有，告诉朋友你要去心理咨询感觉如何？

sentences.en: Because especially in 2015, it's kind of fallen away slowly as more people talk about it.
sentences.zh: 因为特别是在2015年，随着越来越多的人谈论它，这种偏见已经慢慢消失了。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah. But there is a stigma associated with it.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，是的。但它确实伴随着一种污名。

sentences.en: And that stigma is... Well, everyone asked me, they said, why, what's wrong?
sentences.zh: 而那种污名是……嗯，每个人都问我，他们说，为什么？出什么事了？

sentences.en: That's what everyone said to me.
sentences.zh: 每个人都这么问我。

sentences.en: Everyone said the same thing. What's wrong?
sentences.zh: 每个人都说了同样的话。出什么事了？

sentences.en: One of my favourite ones, this wasn't a friend, but I did an interview with a British newspaper.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的一个例子，虽然不是朋友，但我接受了一家英国报纸的采访。

sentences.en: I forget which one it's called. Maybe it's the Telegraph, I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我忘了叫什么名字。可能是《每日电讯报》，我不确定。

sentences.en: It's slightly conservative. But anyway, we did this interview.
sentences.zh: 它稍微有点保守。但不管怎样，我们做了这次采访。

sentences.en: I'll never forget this. And the woman, very British, very posh, you know, older woman.
sentences.zh: 我永远不会忘记这一点。那位女士，非常英国，非常讲究，你知道，年长的女士。

sentences.en: And she said to me, she's like, you've been quite outspoken about going to therapy.
sentences.zh: 她对我说，她说，你对去心理咨询这件事一直很直言不讳。

sentences.en: And do you still go to therapy? And I was like, yes.
sentences.zh: 你还在去吗？我说，是的。

sentences.en: And she's like, why? What's wrong with you?
sentences.zh: 她说，为什么？你有什么毛病吗？

sentences.en: And I said, do you not go to therapy? And she said, I don't need to.
sentences.zh: 我说，你不去心理咨询吗？她说，我不需要。

sentences.en: And I was like, well, everyone can benefit from therapy.
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，每个人都能从心理咨询中受益。

sentences.en: She's like, I respectfully disagree. I think the therapizing that we're currently experiencing in the world is completely unnecessary.
sentences.zh: 她说，我恭敬地不同意。我认为我们目前在世界上经历的这种‘心理咨询热’完全是不必要的。

sentences.en: And sometimes you just need to take it and move on.
sentences.zh: 有时候你只需要承受它，然后继续前进。

sentences.en: And I was like, that is the most British thing I've ever heard in my life.
sentences.zh: 我说，那是我这辈子听过最‘英国’的话了。

sentences.en: But I get it. That's what a lot of people felt and think.
sentences.zh: 但我明白。这就是很多人感受和认为的。

sentences.en: They'd be like, why? What are you doing?
sentences.zh: 他们会问，为什么？你在做什么？

sentences.en: What I've come to realize is that therapy as an idea holds a stigma, but the thing that it is doing is not just necessary, but it's actually welcomed by everybody.
sentences.zh: 我后来意识到，心理咨询作为一个概念带有污名，但它所做的事情不仅是必要的，而且实际上受到所有人的欢迎。

sentences.en: When you go and you have a conversation with your friends and you commiserate about something that's going on in your life, It's a form of therapy.
sentences.zh: 当你和朋友交谈，倾诉生活中发生的事情时，这是一种心理咨询。

sentences.en: When you confide in your loved one, the two of you are in bed at the end of a long day and you're telling them about how stressful your job is and you're telling them about your doubts about staying in it or not, that's a form of therapy.
sentences.zh: 当你向爱人吐露心声，在漫长的一天结束后，你们躺在床上，你告诉他们工作有多大压力，告诉他们你对是否留在那里的疑虑，那也是一种心理咨询。

sentences.en: And I think because we've given it this formalized title that's associated with psychotic breaks on the most extreme things, we've now made it seem like it's reserved for people who are only broken, broken, broken.
sentences.zh: 我认为，因为我们给它起了一个正式的名称，并将其与精神崩溃等极端情况联系起来，我们现在让它看起来像是只为那些‘破碎’的人保留的。

sentences.en: But we've forgotten how necessary it is.
sentences.zh: 但我们忘记了它是多么必要。

sentences.en: You go around the world and you see cultures, many of them, cultures of color, had the idea and the tradition of therapy long before it was formalized as a concept.
sentences.zh: 你环游世界，你会看到很多文化，许多有色人种的文化，在它被正式化为一个概念之前，就已经有了心理咨询的想法和传统。

sentences.en: In African cultures, you would speak to the elders.
sentences.zh: 在非洲文化中，你会和长辈交谈。

sentences.en: That's what you do. You go and you sit down with the elders.
sentences.zh: 这就是你所做的。你去和长辈坐下来。

sentences.en: You tell them about your problems. You go there with your wife.
sentences.zh: 你告诉他们你的问题。你和妻子一起去。

sentences.en: You go there with your family. Any dispute, you go and talk about it there.
sentences.zh: 你和家人一起去。任何纠纷，你都会去那里谈论。

sentences.en: And they give you their advice and it's based on generations of knowledge and it's based on a communal understanding of who you are and who they are.
sentences.zh: 他们会给你建议，这些建议基于几代人的知识，基于对你是谁、他们是谁的共同理解。

sentences.en: They've known you since you were a child even.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至从你小时候就认识你了。

sentences.en: It's a form of therapy. And so I think because we've given it this, like the label people, I go to therapy.
sentences.zh: 这是一种心理咨询。所以我认为，因为我们给它贴上了标签，人们会说‘我去心理咨询’。

sentences.en: I've realized if you just change that, take that sentence out and tell it to somebody and go, oh yeah, no, there's a wonderful elder who I speak to and they give me advice.
sentences.zh: 我意识到如果你改变一下，去掉那句话，告诉别人说，‘哦，有一个很棒的长辈，我经常和他们交谈，他们给我建议’。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, like half the people who looked at you funny would be like, that's very good.
sentences.zh: 突然间，那些用奇怪眼光看你的人会说，那很好。

sentences.en: You must listen to your elders. That's very good.
sentences.zh: 你必须听长辈的话。那很好。

sentences.en: You know, and then in another culture, you say to somebody, oh, I go to somebody who spiritually understands how, like, my brain works and they connect me with myself.
sentences.zh: 你知道，然后在另一种文化中，你对某人说，‘哦，我去找一个在精神上理解我大脑如何运作的人，他们让我与自己建立连接’。

sentences.en: They'd be like, that's very good. You do that.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，那很好。你去做吧。

sentences.en: We all do it, you know. Bartenders have been therapists for hundreds of years.
sentences.zh: 我们都这样做，你知道。调酒师几百年来一直充当着心理咨询师的角色。

sentences.en: You know, people have gone and gotten drunk at a bar.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们去酒吧喝醉。

sentences.en: Hairdresses, you know. Hairdresses. It's a natural thing.
sentences.zh: 理发师，你知道。理发师。这很自然。

sentences.en: It's just, you know, I understand the stigma because there's a terrifying notion that comes with saying that you're broken But I don't think it's about saying that we're broken It's just about like understanding our cracks Did you understand your cracks from it?
sentences.zh: 只是，你知道，我理解那种污名，因为说自己‘破碎’带有一种可怕的观念。但我认为这并不是说我们破碎了，只是为了理解我们身上的裂痕。你通过它理解了自己的裂痕吗？

sentences.en: I think I understood them theoretically My problem was never understanding them My problem was never like understanding them on an intellectual level I think I've always been good at that, maybe even too good The thing I've had to learn in therapy is the feeling part, not the thinking part What do you mean by the feeling part?
sentences.zh: 我想我在理论上理解了它们。我的问题从来不是理解它们。我的问题从来不是在智力层面上理解它们。我想我一直很擅长这个，甚至可能太擅长了。我在心理咨询中学到的是‘感受’的部分，而不是‘思考’的部分。你说的‘感受’部分是什么意思？

sentences.en: So I've always been very good I would be able to break down any situation to you As thoughts and, you know, and analytics in a way You go like, Trevor, what happened there?
sentences.zh: 所以我一直很擅长。我能够向你剖析任何情况。

sentences.en: I would even be able to explain like an outburst Well, what happened was clearly over time This action had been repeated and I didn't appreciate it And so at that point I'd reached my breaking point And I reacted like this, you know But I didn't realize until I went to therapy that I limited how much I was saying the feeling that I was having.
sentences.zh: 作为思想，你知道，以一种分析的方式。你问，Trevor，那里发生了什么？

sentences.en: I felt sad. I felt mad. I felt. And then like you said about tracing it back, you then now, once you understand that feeling, and once you acknowledge it, you're then able to now.
sentences.zh: 我甚至能解释一次爆发。‘嗯，发生的事情很明显，随着时间的推移，这种行为被重复了，我没有欣赏它。所以在那一刻，我达到了崩溃点，我做出了这样的反应，你知道。’但我直到去心理咨询才意识到，我限制了自己表达感受的程度。

sentences.en: And then even ask yourself, why do I feel this thing?
sentences.zh: 我感到悲伤。我感到愤怒。我感到……然后就像你说的关于追溯它，一旦你理解了那种感觉，一旦你承认了它，你就能……

sentences.en: Why do I even feel? And start realizing that some people can make you feel when others can't.
sentences.zh: 然后甚至问自己，为什么我会有这种感觉？

sentences.en: Two people can say the exact same sentence to you.
sentences.zh: 为什么我会有这种感觉？并开始意识到有些人可以让你产生感觉，而另一些人却不能。

sentences.en: Only one can have an effect. Why? And that was and continues to be my journey and my joyous challenge.
sentences.zh: 两个人可以对你说完全相同的一句话。

sentences.en: It's like learning how to feel, not just think through everything.
sentences.zh: 只有一个人能产生影响。为什么？这就是，并且继续是我的旅程和我快乐的挑战。

sentences.en: It's like really just feel. How do I feel?
sentences.zh: 就像学习如何去感受，而不是仅仅通过思考来处理一切。

sentences.en: Oh, I'm tired. Oh, I'm resentful. Wow, I'm sad about that.
sentences.zh: 就像真的去感受。我感觉如何？

sentences.en: Oh, I'm feeling a little hopeless. Wow, this feels a little melancholic.
sentences.zh: 哦，我累了。哦，我感到怨恨。哇，我对此感到难过。

sentences.en: This is like really getting into those feelings.
sentences.zh: 哦，我感到有点绝望。哇，这感觉有点忧郁。

sentences.en: Men don't do that. Do they just drink or they just go?
sentences.zh: 这就像真正进入那些感受中。

sentences.en: Yeah. Men just get like pissed. Masturbate, gamble.
sentences.zh: 男人不那样做。他们只是喝酒或者直接……

sentences.en: Yeah. Porn. It's like, yeah. I'm angry at you.
sentences.zh: 是的。男人只是变得很生气。自慰，赌博。

sentences.en: When was the last time a male friend looked at another male friend and said, you hurt me?
sentences.zh: 是的。色情。就像，是的。我生你的气。

sentences.en: You know? Hey man, that hurts. I know you think my haircut looked funny, but the way you said it in front of those other people, it hurts.
sentences.zh: 上一次男性朋友看着另一个男性朋友说‘你伤害了我’是什么时候？

sentences.en: Hey, the way you commented on my job and how you think it's the dumbest thing, that hurt me.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？‘嘿伙计，那很伤人。我知道你觉得我的发型看起来很滑稽，但你在其他人面前说出来的方式，伤害了我。’

sentences.en: It hurt me because I love how you see me and I want to see myself being special in your life.
sentences.zh: ‘嘿，你评论我工作的方式，以及你认为那是多么愚蠢的事情，那伤害了我。’

sentences.en: And I felt insignificant. You hurt me, man.
sentences.zh: ‘它伤害了我，因为我喜欢你看待我的方式，我想在你的生活中看到自己是特别的。’

sentences.en: Men are terrified of that. You know? And so we'd rather say, you pissed me off.
sentences.zh: ‘我感到微不足道。你伤害了我，伙计。’

sentences.en: Punch you in the head. Because that's acceptable in society.
sentences.zh: 男人对那个感到恐惧。你知道吗？所以我们宁愿说，‘你惹毛我了’。

sentences.en: We heard that. You know? You said your therapist or therapy helped you to identify this link between ADHD and depression.
sentences.zh: 然后揍你的头。因为那在社会上是可以接受的。

sentences.en: When did you find out you had ADHD? I got diagnosed two years ago.
sentences.zh: 我们听到了。你知道吗？你说你的心理咨询师或心理咨询帮助你确定了ADHD和抑郁症之间的联系。

sentences.en: And my friend got diagnosed first, told me about it, changed his whole life.
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候发现自己有ADHD的？我两年前被诊断出来的。

sentences.en: And then when he was describing some of the symptoms, I was like, huh?
sentences.zh: 我朋友先被诊断出来，告诉了我，这改变了他的一生。

sentences.en: I was like, well, that's weird. That sounds a lot like me.
sentences.zh: 当他描述一些症状时，我心想，嗯？

sentences.en: And we're very different personality-wise.
sentences.zh: 我心想，嗯，这很奇怪。这听起来很像我。

sentences.en: And then I asked him, I said, I don't understand.
sentences.zh: 而且我们在性格上非常不同。

sentences.en: I've never noticed these things in you. And he was like, yeah, he was very good at hiding them.
sentences.zh: 然后我问他，我说，我不明白。

sentences.en: He was very good at masking them. And it hit home so much that it made me think I need to get diagnosed.
sentences.zh: 我从来没在你身上注意到这些。他说，是的，他非常擅长隐藏它们。

sentences.en: I was like, let me go and see. I was like, it might not be.
sentences.zh: 他非常擅长掩盖它们。这让我感触很深，让我觉得我需要去诊断一下。

sentences.en: But let me go and find out. And then I remembered that when I was a kid, my school told my mom that I needed to go for a psychiatric evaluation.
sentences.zh: 我心想，让我去看看。我心想，可能不是。

sentences.en: Because when I was really young, the teachers complained.
sentences.zh: 但让我去查清楚。然后我记得我小时候，学校告诉我妈妈我需要去进行精神评估。

sentences.en: They said I was just all over the place. and my mom took me to a psychiatrist and the psychiatrist diagnosed me with ADHD, but back then it was called hyperactivity.
sentences.zh: 因为我小时候，老师们总是抱怨。

sentences.en: And my mom, the therapist was like, oh, your son has ADHD or is hyperactive and so you must stay away from these foods and you must do this and you must do that and you could give him treatment.
sentences.zh: 他们说我总是坐不住。我妈妈带我去看精神科医生，医生诊断我患有ADHD，但那时它被称为多动症。

sentences.en: And my mom was like, we'll pray for him.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈，那个咨询师说，‘哦，你儿子有ADHD或多动症，所以你必须远离这些食物，你必须做这个，你必须做那个，你可以给他治疗。’

sentences.en: Let's keep it moving.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈说，‘我们会为他祈祷。’

sentences.en: She just didn't know and she was like, no, this is not a thing. you know?
sentences.zh: 继续生活吧。

sentences.en: And then I, now as an adult went, wait a minute, was that what that was?
sentences.zh: 她只是不知道，她觉得，不，这不是什么大不了的事。你知道吗？

sentences.en: And then I went, went through the like real assessment.
sentences.zh: 然后我，现在作为一个成年人，心想，等一下，那是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Like, I mean, not like an online quiz, you know, the one where you sit down, it's multiple visits, you do different types of tests, multimodal tests, and you go through it all.
sentences.zh: 然后我进行了真正的评估。

sentences.en: And then I learned about my ADHD. And I think that's another thing I like, I'm a little worried about now in society.
sentences.zh: 我是说，不是那种在线测试，你知道，那种你坐下来，多次访问，做不同类型的测试，多模式测试，然后经历整个过程的评估。

sentences.en: It's just like when we talk about therapy and AI and everything, we flatten these words.
sentences.zh: 然后我了解了我的ADHD。我认为这是我现在在社会上有点担心的另一件事。

sentences.en: And so what then starts to happen is now I meet people everywhere.
sentences.zh: 就像当我们谈论心理咨询和AI等等时，我们把这些词扁平化了。

sentences.en: Everyone's going like, I've got ADHD. I've got ADHD.
sentences.zh: 于是发生的事情是，我现在到处都能遇到人。

sentences.en: I've got, I can't watch a movie for more than 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 每个人都说，‘我有ADHD。我有ADHD。’

sentences.en: I've got ADHD. I lost my keys. Yeah. And it's like, no, you can be forgetful and not have ADHD.
sentences.zh: ‘我有……我不能看电影超过10分钟。我有ADHD。我丢了钥匙。’是的。就像，不，你可能只是健忘，而不是有ADHD。

sentences.en: You can have a short attention span and not have ADHD.
sentences.zh: 你可以注意力不集中，但没有ADHD。

sentences.en: You can be many things and not have ADHD, right?
sentences.zh: 你可以有很多表现，但没有ADHD，对吧？

sentences.en: But even when you have ADHD, you don't all have the same ADHD.
sentences.zh: 但即使你有ADHD，你们的ADHD也不尽相同。

sentences.en: You know, some people are inattentive, some people are hyperactive, some people have learned coping mechanisms, some people haven't.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些人是不注意型，有些人是多动型，有些人学会了应对机制，有些人没有。

sentences.en: In women and men, it presents differently at times.
sentences.zh: 在女性和男性身上，它的表现有时也不同。

sentences.en: So I think we must also be careful, you know, like now it's just become like...
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们也必须小心，你知道，现在它已经变得像……

sentences.en: Yeah. And then like on TikTok, hey, how did you deal with your ADHD?
sentences.zh: 是的。然后像在TikTok上，‘嘿，你是怎么处理你的ADHD的？’

sentences.en: And it's like, wait, wait, wait, wait, wait, let's, you know, it's good that we're talking about these things.
sentences.zh: 就像，等等，等等，等等，等等，让我们，你知道，谈论这些事情是好的。

sentences.en: But let's not be quick to, you know, to all have it and have the same version of it and all think that all of our treatments are exactly the same, etc.
sentences.zh: 但不要急于，你知道，大家都觉得自己有，都有同一个版本，都认为我们的治疗方法完全一样，等等。

sentences.en: But that Yeah, that's so I think I mine was, I think it's now three, four years ago.
sentences.zh: 但那……是的，我想我的诊断是三、四年前的事了。

sentences.en: This link between ADHD and depression, I've you're the first person I've interviewed I've heard about this before but you're the first person that I've spoken to who has said that their depression was linked to their ADHD yeah can you explain to me the link and how that sort of manifests so I I didn't understand it but you know as I understand ADHD now what what fundamentally happened in my brain and I guess it'll happen to some people as well is I would have an inability to choose where to place my focus, right?
sentences.zh: ADHD和抑郁症之间的这种联系，我……你是第一个我采访过的提到这个的人。我以前听说过，但你是第一个告诉我他们的抑郁症与ADHD有关的人。是的，你能向我解释一下这种联系以及它是如何表现出来的吗？我当时不明白，但正如我现在理解ADHD一样，我大脑中根本发生了什么，我想这对某些人也会发生，就是我无法选择将注意力放在哪里，对吧？

sentences.en: One of the things. So I would either be hyper-focused by something that I shouldn't, or I would have no focus for the thing that I should.
sentences.zh: 这是其中之一。所以我要么会过度专注于我不该关注的事情，要么对该关注的事情完全没有注意力。

sentences.en: So I could be having a conversation with you here.
sentences.zh: 所以我可能正在这里和你交谈。

sentences.en: And let's say there was a car outside revving its engine.
sentences.zh: 假设外面有一辆车在轰鸣引擎。

sentences.en: At some point, that's all I'd be able to think about, even though you're speaking to me.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，即使你在跟我说话，我能想到的也只有那个。

sentences.en: That's all I'd be able to think about is like, who's revving this engine?
sentences.zh: 我能想到的只有：谁在轰鸣这个引擎？

sentences.en: Who's driving this car? What is going on out there?
sentences.zh: 谁在开这辆车？外面发生了什么？

sentences.en: What kind of car is that? Sounds like a V6.
sentences.zh: 那是什么车？听起来像V6。

sentences.en: Is that a truck? What are they? Huh? Is something wrong?
sentences.zh: 那是卡车吗？他们是什么？嗯？有什么不对劲吗？

sentences.en: No. And now you'd be talking. And then at the end of the sentence, I'll just hear the last three words you said.
sentences.zh: 不。现在你还在说话。然后在句子结束时，我只能听到你说的最后三个词。

sentences.en: And then I'll try and like put it all together and act like I was paying attention.
sentences.zh: 然后我会试着把它们拼凑起来，假装我在专心听。

sentences.en: But what my brain was also doing in that paying attention thing was it was focusing on a recurring thought or recurring idea that I couldn't let go of.
sentences.zh: 但我大脑在那种‘专心听’的过程中，实际上是在专注于一个我无法放下的重复想法或概念。

sentences.en: And that's sometimes where the depression would kick in is that I would be perpetually stuck in a loop of either meaninglessness or what I like to call personally, it's like my zoom was stuck on my lens.
sentences.zh: 这就是抑郁症有时会介入的地方，我会永远陷入一种无意义的循环中，或者我个人称之为‘我的变焦镜头卡住了’。

sentences.en: You know, and I think the way you see life is literally like a lens.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为你看待生活的方式就像一个镜头。

sentences.en: I shouldn't have done that with my hands in a video.
sentences.zh: 我不应该在视频里用手做那个动作。

sentences.en: That's going to be... We can Photoshop it.
sentences.zh: 那会……我们可以用Photoshop处理掉。

sentences.en: Yeah, just going to meme that. But anyway, like I think of a lens, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，只是会做成梗图。但不管怎样，我想的是镜头，对吧？

sentences.en: And what you're doing with a lens all the time when you're getting focused and when you're zooming is you're trying to place your focus on the object that you're trying to place it on.
sentences.zh: 当你聚焦和变焦时，你一直在做的是试图将焦点放在你试图放置的对象上。

sentences.en: If you zoom out too wide, you can't see the object.
sentences.zh: 如果你拉得太远，你就看不见那个对象。

sentences.en: If you zoom in too much, you also can't see the object.
sentences.zh: 如果你拉得太近，你也看不见那个对象。

sentences.en: You've got to find the right zoom so that you know, okay, we're now looking at a cup.
sentences.zh: 你必须找到正确的变焦，这样你知道，好的，我们现在在看一个杯子。

sentences.en: If you zoom in too much, you just go like, I'm looking at silver.
sentences.zh: 如果你拉得太近，你只会说，我在看银色。

sentences.en: I'm looking at a color. You zoom out too much.
sentences.zh: 我在看一种颜色。你拉得太远了。

sentences.en: You can't even see that we're in this room.
sentences.zh: 你甚至看不出我们在房间里。

sentences.en: I'm looking at people. You're like, no, there's a cup.
sentences.zh: 我在看人。你会说，不，那里有个杯子。

sentences.en: Oh, I didn't see it. And so what was happening in my brain was I would get stuck in a Zoom and I would just loop.
sentences.zh: 哦，我没看见。所以发生在我大脑里的事情是，我会卡在某个变焦里，然后我就循环了。

sentences.en: So sometimes it would be me going, huh, that was an interesting day at work.
sentences.zh: 所以有时会是我在想，‘嗯，今天工作真有意思。’

sentences.en: Oh, I go to work tomorrow and I go to work the next day, then the next day, and then the next day, then there's a weekend, but then I'm back at work.
sentences.zh: ‘哦，我明天去上班，然后后天去上班，然后接着去，然后接着去，然后有个周末，但然后我又回去上班了。’

sentences.en: Wait a minute. It's just weeks and weekends forever.
sentences.zh: ‘等一下。这只是永远的周和周末。’

sentences.en: It just keeps on going. And then And then one day you're like, you're 90 and then you're dead.
sentences.zh: ‘它只是不断地继续。然后……然后有一天你90岁了，然后你就死了。’

sentences.en: And wait, why am I going to work tomorrow?
sentences.zh: ‘等等，为什么我明天要去上班？’

sentences.en: What's the point of, what is happening here?
sentences.zh: ‘这有什么意义？这里发生了什么？’

sentences.en: This makes absolutely no sense. And then I'll just sit there and I couldn't get that out of my head.
sentences.zh: ‘这完全没有道理。’然后我就坐在那里，无法把那个想法从脑子里赶走。

sentences.en: I literally could not get that thought out of my head.
sentences.zh: 我真的无法把那个想法从脑子里赶走。

sentences.en: And I would just sit there like, what is the point of this?
sentences.zh: 我就坐在那里想，这有什么意义？

sentences.en: What are we doing?
sentences.zh: 我们在做什么？

sentences.en: Couldn't get it out of my head. And how does that feel when you can't get that out of your head?
sentences.zh: 无法把它从脑子里赶走。当你无法把它从脑子里赶走时，那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: What is the feeling? For me, it felt like life was meaningless Like the concept of it was meaningless I was like, we're a blip What are we doing here?
sentences.zh: 那是什么感觉？对我来说，感觉生活毫无意义。那个概念本身就是无意义的。我想，我们只是一个闪现。我们在做什么？

sentences.en: All of this means nothing All of this is pointless You know?
sentences.zh: 这一切都毫无意义。这一切都毫无价值。你知道吗？

sentences.en: Is that an exact example of something that would make you...
sentences.zh: 这是一个让你……的准确例子吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, no, no, this is an exact example This is something that would get stuck in my head Because I...
sentences.zh: 是的，不，不，这是一个准确的例子。这就是会卡在我脑子里的东西。因为我……

sentences.en: Because I didn't know with ADHD that I was hyper-focusing on this thing.
sentences.zh: 因为我不知道我有ADHD，我正在过度专注于这件事。

sentences.en: So in the same way that I could hyper-focus on learning about, I don't know, a discipline, industrial design or artificial intelligence, I would just, you know what I'm talking about with that.
sentences.zh: 所以就像我可以过度专注于学习，我不知道，一门学科，工业设计或人工智能，我就会，你知道我在说什么。

sentences.en: I'd get hyper-focused and then I'd learn everything about it.
sentences.zh: 我会过度专注，然后我会学习关于它的一切。

sentences.en: And I'd read every book and I'd talk to every person I could and I would watch everything.
sentences.zh: 我会读每一本书，我会和每一个我能交谈的人交谈，我会看每一件事。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, in like three months, you'd meet me and I'd go like, yep, I've read that book.
sentences.zh: 突然间，在三个月内，你见到我，我会说，‘是的，我读过那本书。’

sentences.en: I've read that book. I've read that book.
sentences.zh: ‘我读过那本书。我读过那本书。’

sentences.en: And I'm obsessed with this thing. And then one day it just disappears.
sentences.zh: 而且我沉迷于这件事。然后有一天它就消失了。

sentences.en: Now that's fine for like learning, let's say, but it would be terrible for an idea of like sadness or an idea of feeling like life is going nowhere or...
sentences.zh: 现在这对于学习来说很好，比如说，但对于悲伤的概念，或者感觉生活无处可去的感觉，那将是可怕的……

sentences.en: It can't be good for being famous.
sentences.zh: 这对成名来说肯定不好。

sentences.en: It's like the worst thing for being famous because you have constant like meaningless feedback and the brain is trying to interpret a lot of it.
sentences.zh: 这对于成名来说是最糟糕的事情，因为你有持续的、无意义的反馈，而大脑正试图解释其中的很多内容。

sentences.en: Exactly. If you get one of those things stuck in your head, gosh.
sentences.zh: 没错。如果你脑子里卡住了其中一个想法，天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah. And then mine also, like, it depends on some people have it, some don't, but like pattern recognition, people with ADHD generally can be very good with pattern recognition.
sentences.zh: 是的。然后我的也是，这取决于，有些人有，有些人没有，但比如模式识别，有ADHD的人通常非常擅长模式识别。

sentences.en: Probably why they're good comedians. And so what happens then, unfortunately, is you can also start to see the patterns in life that can make life seem meaningless.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是为什么他们是优秀的喜剧演员。所以不幸的是，接下来发生的事情是，你也可以开始看到生活中那些让生活看起来毫无意义的模式。

sentences.en: But once I got my ADHD diagnosis and once I understood what was happening, I really did start to see it as a lens.
sentences.zh: 但一旦我得到了ADHD诊断，一旦我理解了发生了什么，我真的开始把它看作一个镜头。

sentences.en: And anytime I find myself in those moments now, because I don't take medication, you know, I took medication like once or twice.
sentences.zh: 现在每当我发现自己处于那些时刻时，因为我不吃药，你知道，我吃过一两次药。

sentences.en: I was like, it didn't help me in my comedy.
sentences.zh: 我心想，它对我的喜剧没有帮助。

sentences.en: I actually need to be erratic and unfocused when I'm doing comedy.
sentences.zh: 我在做喜剧时实际上需要古怪和不专注。

sentences.en: And I'm lucky that I live a life where I don't have to be in an office at a time and do a thing in a certain way.
sentences.zh: 我很幸运，我过的生活不需要我在某个时间待在办公室，以某种方式做某件事。

sentences.en: And, you know, but in coping or in like learning how to deal with it, I've learned just about like that lens.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，但在应对或学习如何处理它时，我学到了关于那个镜头的东西。

sentences.en: And I'll talk to myself. You know, I go, there's me and there's the observer.
sentences.zh: 我会和自己对话。你知道，我说，有‘我’，还有‘观察者’。

sentences.en: Like I'm the observer of my thoughts. I'm not the thoughts. and then I'll talk to myself.
sentences.zh: 就像我是我思想的观察者。我不是那些思想。然后我会和自己对话。

sentences.en: So I'll be like, man, you do this tomorrow, and then the next day, and then life is me.
sentences.zh: 所以我会说，‘伙计，你明天做这个，然后后天，然后生活就是我。’

sentences.en: Then I go like, it is, it is meaningless, unless you zoom in.
sentences.zh: 然后我说，‘它是，它是无意义的，除非你变焦。’

sentences.en: And then if you zoom in a little bit more, all of a sudden, wow, it's almost like the most meaningful thing.
sentences.zh: 然后如果你再放大一点，突然间，哇，这几乎是最有意义的事情。

sentences.en: This conversation with this person is the most meaningful conversation you will ever have in your life.
sentences.zh: 这次与这个人的谈话是你一生中将要进行的最有意义的谈话。

sentences.en: This is it. This is everything that it is.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。这就是它的一切。

sentences.en: This hug that you're getting from your friend is the most important thing you will ever experience.
sentences.zh: 你从朋友那里得到的这个拥抱是你将要经历的最重要的事情。

sentences.en: This meal that you're having, just taste these ingredients what what is taste feel it on your on your on your taste buds and and like one of the tools they they teach you like with adhd sometimes you know when when it when it makes you go into anxiety or depression is to just notice things practice being present walk down the street and like look like really look and say out loud what you're seeing and at first it's very stupid that is a red door that is a green roof that is a pigeon sitting on the gutter that is a gutter, that is a gray car that is driven by.
sentences.zh: 你正在吃的这顿饭，只是品尝这些成分，什么……什么是味道，在你的味蕾上感受它，然后……他们教你的工具之一，有时你知道，当ADHD让你陷入焦虑或抑郁时，就是去注意事物。练习活在当下。走在街上，像……真正地看，并大声说出你所看到的。起初这很愚蠢：那是一扇红色的门，那是一个绿色的屋顶，那是一只鸽子坐在排水沟上，那是一个排水沟，那是一辆灰色的车，由……驾驶。

sentences.en: And you'll be shocked at how just doing that gets your brain out of that loop.
sentences.zh: 你会惊讶于仅仅这样做就能让你的大脑摆脱那个循环。

sentences.en: And then something's going to catch your eye or something will spark.
sentences.zh: 然后会有什么东西吸引你的眼球，或者有什么东西会激发灵感。

sentences.en: And by the end of that walk, you won't be in the mood that you were in when you started that walk.
sentences.zh: 在那次散步结束时，你不会处于你开始散步时的那种情绪中。

sentences.en: Did you ever feel hopeless when you spiraled into this sort of rumination?
sentences.zh: 当你陷入这种反刍时，你有没有感到绝望？

sentences.en: Was there ever a moment through this journey of understanding your depression that you felt hopeless.
sentences.zh: 在你理解抑郁症的这段旅程中，有没有那么一刻你感到绝望？

sentences.en: I did and I didn't. This is going to sound really weird to you.
sentences.zh: 我有，也没有。这听起来对你来说会很奇怪。

sentences.en: I have this strange thing that'll happen to me sometimes in life where I feel like it's all meaningless and it's nothing and it's whatever.
sentences.zh: 我生活中偶尔会发生一件奇怪的事情，我觉得一切都毫无意义，什么都不是，什么都无所谓。

sentences.en: It's very, very random. Oftentimes, I've just learned sometimes it's fatigue.
sentences.zh: 这非常、非常随机。通常，我只是了解到有时是疲劳。

sentences.en: I've learned rules now for myself and for anyone out there really, especially if you have ADHD.
sentences.zh: 我现在为自己和任何外面的人，特别是如果你有ADHD，制定了规则。

sentences.en: Before you go through anything or before you think about anything intently and intensely when you're struggling, ask yourself a few simple questions.
sentences.zh: 在你经历任何事情之前，或者在你挣扎时深入、强烈地思考任何事情之前，问自己几个简单的问题。

sentences.en: Have you slept? Have you eaten well? Like, have you eaten good food?
sentences.zh: 你睡了吗？你吃得好吗？比如，你吃过好食物吗？

sentences.en: Have you moved your body? And have you spent a little time breathing?
sentences.zh: 你活动身体了吗？你花点时间呼吸了吗？

sentences.en: If you answer yes to all of those questions, you can continue to pontificate about the meaning of life and everything that you're going through.
sentences.zh: 如果你对所有这些问题都回答‘是’，你可以继续夸夸其谈关于生命的意义和你正在经历的一切。

sentences.en: If you have not, just fulfill all of them and then see if you're still feeling the same on the other side.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有，就把它们全部满足，然后看看你在另一边是否还有同样的感觉。

sentences.en: And you'll be shocked how oftentimes you aren't.
sentences.zh: 你会惊讶于很多时候你并没有。

sentences.en: So the one thing that would happen to me, this is so ridiculous, I know.
sentences.zh: 所以有一件事会发生在我身上，这太荒谬了，我知道。

sentences.en: Sometimes when I'd be in that place, I'd feel a little hopeless, right?
sentences.zh: 有时当我处于那个地方时，我会感到有点绝望，对吧？

sentences.en: And I would think to myself, I hate this.
sentences.zh: 我会心想，我讨厌这个。

sentences.en: This sucks. I don't know what I want to do with life anymore.
sentences.zh: 这太烂了。我不知道我以后想用生活做什么。

sentences.en: Never like suicidal, but just like, I just don't know if this life thing, what is this?
sentences.zh: 从来没有自杀倾向，只是觉得，我只是不知道这个‘生活’是什么，这是什么？

sentences.en: And then I would go, if it was going to end tomorrow, then what would I do like today then?
sentences.zh: 然后我会想，如果它明天就要结束了，那我今天会做什么？

sentences.en: I'd be like, you know what I'm going to do?
sentences.zh: 我会心想，你知道我要做什么吗？

sentences.en: I'm going to go on stage. I'm going to tell that joke that I've been terrified to tell.
sentences.zh: 我要上台。我要讲那个我一直害怕讲的笑话。

sentences.en: I'm just going to say it because I'm leaving anyway.
sentences.zh: 我只是要说出来，因为反正我要离开了。

sentences.en: Life is ending. It's all going away because it's all going to shit, right?
sentences.zh: 生活正在结束。一切都要消失了，因为一切都要完蛋了，对吧？

sentences.en: Just go and say that. Go tell that joke.
sentences.zh: 去说出来吧。去讲那个笑话。

sentences.en: I'll be like, you know what I should also do?
sentences.zh: 我会心想，你知道我还应该做什么吗？

sentences.en: I should also throw a party. I mean, life's ending anyway.
sentences.zh: 我还应该开个派对。我的意思是，反正生活要结束了。

sentences.en: Just throw like one, just like one, just like fuck off party that you just like go into it.
sentences.zh: 只是开一个，就像一个，就像一个‘去你的’派对，你只是……进入其中。

sentences.en: And I think of all the things, and I mean this genuinely.
sentences.zh: 我想到了所有的事情，我是真心的。

sentences.en: I think of all the things that I would do with like giant middle fingers on my way out. and the smile that it brings to my face, I can't explain to you because every time it makes me realize that that's all I should be trying to do.
sentences.zh: 我想到了所有我会在离开时竖起巨大中指的事情。它带给我的微笑，我无法向你解释，因为每次它都让我意识到，那才是我应该尝试去做的事情。

sentences.en: Not in a way where I don't consider other people, but it's what I should be trying to do.
sentences.zh: 不是以一种我不考虑别人的方式，但那是我应该尝试去做的事情。

sentences.en: And it's made me realize that at times, not everyone, but for me, and I think some people would probably feel this, sometimes what's happened in our lives, and I know I had this, is like you feel like you don't realize that you've stopped sort of like running, jumping, smiling, screaming.
sentences.zh: 它让我意识到，有时，不是每个人，但对我来说，我想有些人可能会有这种感觉，有时我们生活中发生的事情，我知道我有过，就是你觉得你没有意识到你已经停止了……奔跑、跳跃、微笑、尖叫。

sentences.en: You've stopped being everything you can be.
sentences.zh: 你已经停止成为你能成为的一切。

sentences.en: And you've just, you've started existing as one version of yourself.
sentences.zh: 你只是开始作为你自己的一种版本存在。

sentences.en: And sometimes just having the idea of just like, you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 有时只是有那种想法，就像，你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Take all your clothes off and run through the streets screaming.
sentences.zh: 脱掉你所有的衣服，在街上尖叫着跑过。

sentences.en: And what would you say? And who would you say it to?
sentences.zh: 你会说什么？你会对谁说？

sentences.en: And why would you say? You'd be shocked at how that gives you an inkling of what you're not doing for yourself.
sentences.zh: 你为什么要说？你会惊讶于这如何让你隐约感觉到你没有为自己做什么。

sentences.en: Some people might be like, I'll tell my dad to go screw himself.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能会想，‘我会告诉我的父亲去死吧。’

sentences.en: I would say to you, oh, this is probably you realizing that you don't set boundaries with your dad and you don't communicate well.
sentences.zh: 我会对你说，哦，这可能是你意识到你没有和父亲设定界限，你沟通得不好。

sentences.en: Maybe you don't tell your dad how you hurt your feelings.
sentences.zh: 也许你没有告诉你的父亲你是如何伤害你的感情的。

sentences.en: Or I, man, I'll go to work and I'll, yeah, maybe this is not the job for you.
sentences.zh: 或者我，伙计，我会去工作，我会，是的，也许这不是适合你的工作。

sentences.en: You know, I'll party all night. Maybe you're not taking enough time to have fun. you'll be shocked at how like sometimes you're not a tantrum but it's just like your screw you choice is what you sort of should be doing in a responsible way and that I promise you now in all those moments where I felt like it's hopeless with the moments where I've come back even more I think to myself huh maybe I should try aiming to get to that place and therein in a strange way lies the meaning for me it's such a beautiful thing that they can be really important answers in such a desperate state but but i completely understand what you're saying because i played out the example in my head that this was my last day and i thought what are the things i'd love to do and again it's such a so clear to me that those are the things that i i'm missing right now from my life my experience exactly you mentioned dads in there and you did reunite with your biological father yeah sort of 24 years old 25 years old when you reunited with him i believe yeah 20 something somewhere there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我会整晚派对。也许你没有花足够的时间去玩乐。你会惊讶于有时你不是在发脾气，但这只是你的‘去你的’选择，是你应该以负责任的方式去做的事情。我向你保证，在所有那些我感到绝望的时刻，都是我回来得更强烈的时刻。我想，嗯，也许我应该尝试瞄准那个地方。在那其中，以一种奇怪的方式，对我来说存在着意义。在如此绝望的状态下能有如此重要的答案，这真是一件美丽的事情，但我完全理解你在说什么，因为我在脑海中演练了这个例子，如果这是我的最后一天，我想，我最想做的事情是什么？同样，对我来说非常清楚，那些就是我现在生活中、经历中缺失的事情。正是如此。你在那里提到了父亲，你确实与你的亲生父亲团聚了。是的，大概24岁、25岁时，当你与他团聚时，我相信，是的，20多岁，某个时候。

sentences.en: What's that like? Is that complicated? Or is that...
sentences.zh: 那是什么感觉？很复杂吗？还是……

sentences.en: Oh, definitely. And why did you reunite with him?
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是。你为什么要和他团聚？

sentences.en: Because... Well, I reunited with him because my mother gave me a key piece of advice, which was valuable.
sentences.zh: 因为……嗯，我与他团聚是因为我母亲给了我一条关键建议，这很有价值。

sentences.en: And she said to me, she said, don't take for granted the answers that a person can hold of you that you may not even know you needed for yourself.
sentences.zh: 她对我说，她说，不要认为一个人对你持有的答案是理所当然的，你可能甚至不知道你需要它们。

sentences.en: And I think parents have that with us, especially if parents are willing to engage with you.
sentences.zh: 我认为父母对我们有这种影响，特别是如果父母愿意与你互动。

sentences.en: These are human beings that have fundamentally shaped you.
sentences.zh: 这些人是根本上塑造了你的人。

sentences.en: You are half of them. You know, they are half of you. it's it's it's a weird thing that you that you can take for granted and so for me like the the gift of reconnecting with my father was reconnecting with him as as a man a young man albeit a man you know scared i scared isn't the right word i i was i was unsure but i wasn't scared you know it's like it's that that feeling of the unknown what what's going to happen what are we like will we get along we not get along i remember him but as a boy and does he even remember me does he even like me does he you have all these ideas is there a part of you that wants to know if he if he loves you if he cares about you i think i think definitely and i but i but i think we don't even think of it like that and i didn't even think of it like that does that make sense because i because i assumed the love because i'd seen it my whole life from him so i assumed the love but i didn't i think the thing that's adjacent to that love is the choosing yeah you know sometimes you you assume that parents love you but you're not sure that they choose you maybe and so that was that was interesting for me and then seeing parts of myself that I didn't even know came from another person.
sentences.zh: 你是他们的一半。你知道，他们是你的一半。这是一件奇怪的事情，你可以认为理所当然。所以对我来说，与父亲重新建立联系的礼物是作为一个男人与他重新建立联系，一个年轻人，尽管是一个男人，你知道，害怕……‘害怕’不是正确的词，我……我……我不确定，但我并不害怕，你知道，这就像那种对未知的恐惧，会发生什么？我们像什么？我们会相处吗？我们不会相处吗？我记得他，但作为一个男孩，他甚至还记得我吗？他甚至喜欢我吗？你有所有这些想法。你内心有一部分想知道他是否爱你，是否关心你吗？我想，我想绝对是。但我……但我认为我们甚至不会那样想，我甚至没有那样想。这有意义吗？因为我……因为我假设了爱，因为我一生都从他那里看到了它。所以我假设了爱，但我没有……我认为与那种爱相邻的是‘选择’。是的，你知道，有时你假设父母爱你，但你不确定他们是否‘选择’了你。也许。所以这对我来说很有趣，然后看到了我自己身上我甚至不知道来自另一个人的部分。

sentences.en: It's fascinating, frustrating, and liberating at the same time.
sentences.zh: 这既迷人、令人沮丧，又令人解放。

sentences.en: Although he wasn't around all the time, did you learn lessons from him when you met him, when you started to sort of rekindle your relationship with him?
sentences.zh: 虽然他并不总是陪在你身边，但当你见到他，当你开始重新点燃与他的关系时，你从他那里学到了教训吗？

sentences.en: I think I did, but not lessons that were taught, lessons that were witnessed.
sentences.zh: 我想我学到了，但不是被教导的教训，而是被见证的教训。

sentences.en: I think most of the lessons that we learn from our parents aren't taught, to be honest.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我认为我们从父母那里学到的大多数教训都不是被教导的。

sentences.en: What did you learn from him? I definitely think from him I learned how important it is to maintain your friendships.
sentences.zh: 你从他那里学到了什么？我绝对认为从他那里我学到了维持友谊是多么重要。

sentences.en: You know, he's lived a long life. He's older than my mom.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他过着漫长的一生。他比我妈妈大。

sentences.en: But even as he's gone into his old age, he still has friends.
sentences.zh: 但即使在他进入老年后，他仍然有朋友。

sentences.en: He still has community. He still has like, he showed me how wonderful that thing is, you know, because friendship, I feel like friendship has in many ways been given the short end of the stick in the world of relationships.
sentences.zh: 他仍然有社区。他仍然有……他向我展示了那件事是多么美妙，你知道，因为友谊，我觉得友谊在人际关系的世界里在很多方面被亏待了。

sentences.en: You know, people understand the value of like parents and children and then people understand like romantic relationship.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们理解父母和子女的价值，然后人们理解浪漫关系。

sentences.en: They go, oh, that's the most of course your spouse.
sentences.zh: 他们说，哦，那是最……当然是你的配偶。

sentences.en: But your friendships are one of the few relationships that don't necessarily rely on like a transaction in a way.
sentences.zh: 但你的友谊是少数不一定依赖于某种交易的关系之一。

sentences.en: It's like purely choice.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是选择。

sentences.en: Patricia, she is so central. She's your mother.
sentences.zh: Patricia，她是如此核心。她是你的母亲。

sentences.en: Yeah. She's so central to your story, to much of the wisdom you have.
sentences.zh: 是的。她对你的故事，对你拥有的许多智慧是如此核心。

sentences.en: You talk about continuing the legacy of her legacy, I guess, and everything that she's instilled in you.
sentences.zh: 你谈到继续她的遗产，我想，以及她灌输给你的一切。

sentences.en: She sounds like a superwoman in every sense of the word.
sentences.zh: 她听起来在任何意义上都是个女超人。

sentences.en: The apparent resilience, and I say apparent because I don't know how to define the perseverance in the face of so many struggles, other than using the word resilience is astounding.
sentences.zh: 那种明显的韧性，我说‘明显’是因为我不知道如何定义在这么多挣扎面前的毅力，除了使用‘韧性’这个词，是令人震惊的。

sentences.en: I found Richard, this picture either, but I found this beautiful photo view, which reminded me a little bit of one.
sentences.zh: 我找到了Richard，这张照片，但我找到了这张美丽的你的照片，它让我想起了一点。

sentences.en: Oh, that one you can, because I've posted it online.
sentences.zh: 哦，那张你可以，因为我已经把它发布在网上了。

sentences.en: There you go. One of the things I've struggled with is with the disconnect between me and my parents is I've struggled with the thought that there's going to be words unsaid.
sentences.zh: 给你。我挣扎的一件事是，我和父母之间的脱节，我挣扎于‘会有未说出口的话’的想法。

sentences.en: Oh. And I asked some of my guests about this because I think because I'm trying to navigate it in myself and within my own life.
sentences.zh: 哦。我问过我的一些嘉宾这个问题，因为我想因为我正在试图在自己内心和自己的生活中导航它。

sentences.en: If you had a 60 second phone call with Patricia and you knew it was going to be your last, what would the words be?
sentences.zh: 如果你和Patricia有一个60秒的通话，而且你知道这将是最后一次，那会是什么话？

sentences.en: What would you choose to say? Oh, I think it would just be, I love you.
sentences.zh: 你会选择说什么？哦，我想那只会是，我爱你。

sentences.en: I love you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you.
sentences.zh: 我爱你。谢谢。谢谢。谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you. I love you. I love you. Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。我爱你。我爱你。非常感谢。

sentences.en: I love you.
sentences.zh: 我爱你。

sentences.en: And genuinely, that's pretty much it. because I'm really lucky that I've said and I continue to try to say, you know, most of what I should to my mom.
sentences.zh: 真诚地说，差不多就是这样。因为我很幸运，我已经说了，并且我继续尝试说，你知道，大部分我应该对我妈妈说的话。

sentences.en: And there's always new things that come up and then I try to say them and we have beautiful conversations.
sentences.zh: 总是有新的事情出现，然后我尝试说出来，我们有美丽的对话。

sentences.en: You know, like these days we take like drives, like drive her to go and buy a new chicken for her.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像这些天我们开车，比如开车带她去给她买一只新鸡。

sentences.en: She's got like a little chicken. It's not even a farm.
sentences.zh: 她有像一只小鸡。那甚至不是一个农场。

sentences.en: I don't even know what to call it. It's like a little squad of chickens.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道该叫它什么。这就像一小队鸡。

sentences.en: But I'll just take her for a drive and then we just talk about life and we just, we talk and we share and we laugh and we, but we spend like, it's like the nothing moments, you know, no agenda, no, like, there's no thing we have to do or not do.
sentences.zh: 但我只是带她去兜风，然后我们只是谈论生活，我们只是，我们谈论，我们分享，我们大笑，我们，但我们花像，这就像‘无事’时刻，你知道，没有议程，没有，就像，没有我们必须做或不做的事情。

sentences.en: I sort of slip into her life, you know, I find her in the garden and I just stand around while she does her gardening and then listen, talk, share.
sentences.zh: 我有时会悄悄走进她的生活，你知道，我发现她在花园里，我就站在旁边，听她说话，分享彼此的生活，看她打理花园。

sentences.en: But really that's, if that was the call now, it would just be, thank you, thank you.
sentences.zh: 但说真的，如果现在要打个电话，那也只会是说声谢谢，谢谢你。

sentences.en: I love you so much. Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 我太爱你了。非常感谢。

sentences.en: I love you. I love you. Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 我爱你。我爱你。太感谢了。

sentences.en: And I guess that early experience where she was shot by your really kind of allowed you to get the perspective.
sentences.zh: 我想那段早期的经历，她被枪击的事，确实让你获得了一种视角。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely. Before most of us would have the perspective.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。比我们大多数人更早拥有了这种视角。

sentences.en: She sounds like a remarkable person. When you talk about continuing her legacy, how do you do that?
sentences.zh: 她听起来是个了不起的人。当你谈到延续她的精神遗产时，你是怎么做的？

sentences.en: Well, she would challenge me and say, my goal is to improve on her legacy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她会挑战我，说我的目标是超越她的遗产。

sentences.en: My mom's definitely remarkable. But as she would say, it's by the grace of God.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈确实很了不起。但正如她所说，那是上帝的恩典。

sentences.en: It's not by her hand alone. And I think one of the things that I've loved most about my relationship with my mom is that I've come to learn that part of what makes her so exceptional is the fact that she's a flawed human being.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是她个人的功劳。我觉得我和我妈妈的关系中，我最喜欢的一点是，我逐渐认识到她之所以如此卓越，部分原因在于她也是一个有缺陷的人。

sentences.en: She's not perfect. There are some wounds that she's inflicted on me that I need to now deal with in my life because she's been my parents, you know?
sentences.zh: 她并不完美。她曾给我造成过一些创伤，我现在生活中必须去处理这些问题，因为她毕竟是我的父母，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And this is sometimes the paradox that we struggle with in our lives as people.
sentences.zh: 这有时是我们作为人所挣扎的悖论。

sentences.en: I think we've been so indoctrinated into this like binary way of thinking that we didn't want to go, we had great parents or we had terrible parents.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们被灌输了一种二元对立的思维方式，要么觉得父母很伟大，要么觉得父母很糟糕。

sentences.en: Sometimes you had a parent who was great at some things and terrible at other things, you know?
sentences.zh: 但有时你的父母在某些方面很棒，在另一些方面却很糟糕，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And if they did love you, they were doing their best.
sentences.zh: 如果他们确实爱你，那他们就是在尽力而为。

sentences.en: Sometimes they didn't. And I think that's tough for some people to acknowledge.
sentences.zh: 有时他们没有做到。我觉得这对某些人来说很难承认。

sentences.en: But if they loved you they were doing their best and they tried their best and they failed at other things and that's fine but you know my goal and my dream is to as my mom always said to me and my brothers like be better than the last how are you thinking about fatherhood well I go back and forth on it because on the one hand sometimes I think you see like the zooming the lens sometimes I think about like the planet and the world.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们爱你，他们就是在尽力，他们尝试过，也在其他事情上失败过，这没关系。但你知道，我的目标和梦想，正如我妈妈一直对我兄弟们说的那样，就是‘要比上一代更好’。你如何看待为人父母？嗯，我对此想法反复不定。一方面，有时我会把镜头拉远，去思考这个星球和世界。

sentences.en: I'm like, are you bringing kids? You're going to bring kids?
sentences.zh: 我在想，你要带孩子来到这个世界吗？你真的要生孩子吗？

sentences.en: No, I'm like, yeah, but the world's probably been terrible for everyone who's been in it at every single given time.
sentences.zh: 不，我在想，是的，但这个世界对每个时代的人来说可能都很糟糕。

sentences.en: So is that a reason to not have a child?
sentences.zh: 所以，这是不生孩子的理由吗？

sentences.en: And then I asked myself the other question.
sentences.zh: 然后我问自己另一个问题。

sentences.en: I'm like, okay, but what do I think I'm bringing to this child?
sentences.zh: 我在想，好吧，但我能给这个孩子带来什么？

sentences.en: And then I thought to myself, wow, do I want to have a kid with ADHD?
sentences.zh: 然后我心想，哇，我想要一个患有ADHD的孩子吗？

sentences.en: How hard was that for them? And what is it going to be like?
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说有多难？那会是什么样子？

sentences.en: And then I'm like, ah, but maybe it'll be great because you know ADHD and maybe they'll have it and maybe they won't.
sentences.zh: 然后我又想，啊，但也许这会很棒，因为你知道ADHD，也许他们会有，也许不会。

sentences.en: So I go back and forth on all of these things.
sentences.zh: 所以我对所有这些事情都反复纠结。

sentences.en: The one thing I would hope is that I will give my child two things that are important, and that is, number one, being chosen, and number two, being considered.
sentences.zh: 我唯一希望的是，我能给我的孩子两样重要的东西，第一是‘被选择’，第二是‘被关怀’。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people have children. but they may not choose them and they don't consider them.
sentences.zh: 我觉得很多人有了孩子，但他们可能并没有‘选择’他们，也没有真正‘关怀’他们。

sentences.en: And that's where you'll hear parents saying things like, I brought you into this world.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你会听到父母说‘是我把你带到这个世界上的’。

sentences.en: It's like, yeah, exactly. So you should consider me a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 就像是，是的，没错。所以你应该多关怀我一点。

sentences.en: Many parents treat children as if the children owe them for introducing them into existence when I think it's the other way around.
sentences.zh: 许多父母对待孩子，好像孩子欠他们的一样，因为是他们把孩子带到了这个世界上，而我认为事实恰恰相反。

sentences.en: So yeah, I think to myself, I like the idea of it and I do like the puzzle of it.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我心想，我喜欢这个想法，也喜欢其中的挑战。

sentences.en: But just like I learned from The Daily Show and every other major undertaking, if I know that it's going to be terrible, then I'll probably have a great time.
sentences.zh: 但就像我从《The Daily Show》和其他重大事业中学到的那样，如果我知道这会很艰难，那我反而可能会过得很开心。

sentences.en: But if I think that it's going to be rewarding and wonderful, I'm going to hate a lot of the moments in it.
sentences.zh: 但如果我以为这会是充满回报和美好的，我反而会讨厌其中的很多时刻。

sentences.en: How does Romantical fit into all of this for you?
sentences.zh: 浪漫关系在这一切中对你来说处于什么位置？

sentences.en: Because you're, well, you were, you know, during those Daily Show days, working every hour of the day.
sentences.zh: 因为你，嗯，你曾经，你知道，在《The Daily Show》那段日子里，每时每刻都在工作。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah. You were fighting in every sense of the word to make this show a success. you're living in an apartment with a guy who's also doing the same I don't know where it fits I can't see it it didn't in many ways you know and that was the price I paid you know does it fit now yeah I think it definitely does I think it definitely does like it's a weird thing to say but as I have become more comfortable with the notion that I could be not in a relationship forever like you know as people say by yourself but I don't think of that because of friends and community but as i've gotten more comfortable with that i think i've become more able to be in a relationship because i i think more and more i've thought of a relationship as something i can bring value to as opposed to the thing that's supposed to just do everything for me you know and i think before i was only looking at it that way without realizing it trevor um these books are beautiful for so many different reasons.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。你在用尽一切方式去让这个节目成功。你和一个同样在拼命工作的人住在一起。我不知道它处于什么位置，我看不出来。在很多方面它确实没位置，你知道，那是我付出的代价。现在它有位置了吗？是的，我想绝对有的。我想绝对有的。这话说出来很奇怪，但随着我越来越习惯‘我可能永远不会处于一段关系中’这个概念，你知道，就像人们说的‘独自一人’，但我并不这么认为，因为我有朋友和社区。但随着我越来越适应这一点，我觉得我反而更有能力去经营一段关系了，因为我越来越倾向于把关系看作是我能贡献价值的东西，而不是那种理应为我做一切的事情，你知道吗？我觉得以前我只是那样看待它，却没意识到这一点。Trevor，这些书因为很多不同的原因而显得非常优美。

sentences.en: Born a Crime is one of the most, it's so funny because it's not my story, but it's everyone's story in so many ways.
sentences.zh: 《Born a Crime》是最棒的书之一，这很有趣，因为它讲的不是我的故事，但在很多方面，它又是每个人的故事。

sentences.en: And I think that's why it's such a beautiful book.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是为什么它是一本如此优美的书。

sentences.en: It's the story of a guy who didn't feel like he fit in, his relationship with his mother, his love for his mother, his journey to the very, very top of a mountain, and all of the important wisdom that he's learned along the way that I think is so relatable, even though it's not my story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不觉得自己合群的人的故事，关于他与母亲的关系，他对母亲的爱，他攀登人生巅峰的旅程，以及他在这一路上学到的所有重要智慧，我觉得即使这不是我的故事，也让人感同身受。

sentences.en: And some books don't achieve that, but your books achieve that so well.
sentences.zh: 有些书做不到这一点，但你的书做得非常好。

sentences.en: Oh, thank you. And this book is the first time I've ever described a book as being truly, truly beautiful.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢。这本书是我第一次真正称之为‘优美’的书。

sentences.en: It comes out on the 8th of October. It's called Into the Uncut Grass.
sentences.zh: 它在10月8日出版。书名叫《Into the Uncut Grass》。

sentences.en: And it's so wise, powerful, but beautiful.
sentences.zh: 它既充满智慧、力量，又非常优美。

sentences.en: A book that... And silly. I hope people remember that it's silly.
sentences.zh: 一本……而且很天真。我希望人们记得它很天真。

sentences.en: I would love to read this to my kids, but it's funny because I thought, when I first opened it, I thought, okay, you know, there's illustrations throughout the book.
sentences.zh: 我很想读给我的孩子们听，但这很有趣，因为我刚打开它时，心想，好吧，你知道，书里到处都是插图。

sentences.en: And then I started reading the words and you realize that it's both applicable and powerful to a young person, but also something you could read alone at my age of 32.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始读文字，你就会意识到它既适用于年轻人，也是一本像我这样32岁的人可以独自阅读的书。

sentences.en: It's such a beautiful book. Thank you. Very kind.
sentences.zh: 这是一本非常优美的书。谢谢。你太客气了。

sentences.en: It follows in the tradition of the boy, the fox, and the mole.
sentences.zh: 它延续了《The Boy, the Mole, the Fox and the Horse》的传统。

sentences.en: It's like, yeah, it's books that I loved, you know, the boy, the little prince, you know.
sentences.zh: 就像是，是的，这些都是我喜欢的书，你知道，《The Boy》，《The Little Prince》，你知道。

sentences.en: There's so many books like that that I think inspired me to think about rediscovering our childlike curiosity ability to to think beyond ourselves our imagination like almost like re-remembering yourself before many of the hurts you know and then and then going from there and so and connection is such a prevalent theme throughout this the journey of connection of love and all of those things and i'm going to link that below so everyone needs to read that book it's so beautiful read it for yourself read it for your kids and read it with your partner we have a closing tradition on this podcast where the last guest leaves a question for the next guest not knowing who they're going to be leaving oh wow okay tell us about the lowest point of your life how did you overcome it what lessons did you learn from the experience Hmm. i funny enough i think we talked about it i i would safely say the lowest point of my life was my mother being shot so it's crazy that we did speak about it um how did i overcome it i don't think i would be so um arrogant as to say that i have overcome it i think i'm constantly working to overcome it do you ever overcome these things i don't know to be honest with you i really don't know because I, you know, it's strange because I don't know what that means or doesn't mean.
sentences.zh: 有很多这样的书，我想它们启发了我去重新发现我们孩童般的好奇心，去思考超越自我的能力，去发挥想象力，就像是重新找回那个在遭受许多伤害之前的自己，然后从那里出发。连接是一个贯穿始终的主题，关于连接、爱以及所有这些的旅程。我会把链接放在下面，每个人都需要读那本书，它太美了。为你自己读，为你的孩子读，和你伴侣一起读。我们这个播客有一个结束传统，上一位嘉宾会给下一位嘉宾留一个问题，不知道对方是谁。哦，哇，好吧。告诉我们你人生中最糟糕的时刻是什么？你是如何克服它的？你从中学到了什么教训？嗯，有趣的是，我想我们谈到了，我可以肯定地说，我人生中最糟糕的时刻是我母亲被枪击。所以我们谈到这个真是太疯狂了。嗯，我是如何克服的？我觉得我还没那么傲慢到说我已经‘克服’了它，我觉得我一直在努力克服它。你真的能克服这些事情吗？老实说，我不知道。我真的不知道，因为，你知道，这很奇怪，我不知道那意味着什么，或者不意味着什么。

sentences.en: Does it mean you don't think of it anymore?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着你不再去想它了？

sentences.en: Does it mean it doesn't affect you anymore?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着它不再影响你了？

sentences.en: I don't know what the answer to that question is.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这个问题的答案是什么。

sentences.en: You know, maybe overcoming something means that it now no longer negatively influences you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许克服某事意味着它现在不再对你产生负面影响了。

sentences.en: I don't know. I don't think that we have like one fixed idea of overcoming something that isn't tangible.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。我不认为我们对‘克服’这种无形的东西有一个固定的概念。

sentences.en: You know, it's not like scaling a mountain.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这不像爬山。

sentences.en: So the honest answer I would give is, yeah, I just give myself grace and I try and work at it.
sentences.zh: 所以我会给出的诚实答案是，是的，我只是对自己宽容一点，然后努力去处理它。

sentences.en: I try and understand that it's all a work in progress.
sentences.zh: 我试着理解这一切都是一个正在进行的过程。

sentences.en: You know, one of my favorite things I learned recently, and I guess it speaks to this, is I should remember the name.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我最近学到的最喜欢的东西之一，我想这与此有关，我应该记住那个名字。

sentences.en: I always remember stories and not like the names of things or the dates, but there's a beautiful art form that I learned about when I was in Japan recently.
sentences.zh: 我总是记得故事，而不是事物的名字或日期，但我最近在日本时学到了一种优美的艺术形式。

sentences.en: And basically, it's a practice of repairing pottery and ceramics that have broken.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这是一种修复破碎陶器和瓷器的做法。

sentences.en: And what happens is you break a plate or you break a vase or something.
sentences.zh: 当你打碎了一个盘子或一个花瓶之类的东西时，会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: And what they do is they put it back together.
sentences.zh: 他们会把它重新拼凑起来。

sentences.en: These artisans who do it. But they don't just glue it back together. they glue it back together and they sort of adorn it with like a golden bondage.
sentences.zh: 那些工匠会这样做。但他们不仅仅是用胶水粘回去，他们用金漆来修补裂缝。

sentences.en: And what you get is an object that is somehow more beautiful than before it was broken.
sentences.zh: 于是你得到的是一个比破碎前更优美的物体。

sentences.en: And it's this beautiful Japanese tradition.
sentences.zh: 这是一种优美的日本传统。

sentences.en: I'm sure you could find the name and put it out there, but if you could help me with it.
sentences.zh: 我相信你能找到它的名字并把它写出来，如果你能帮我一下的话。

sentences.en: But to me, it was one of the most beautiful concepts and a different way to think about being quote unquote fixed or overcoming or, you know, it is the art of Kintsugi in Japan.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，这是最优美的概念之一，也是一种看待‘被修复’、‘克服’或‘变得更好’的不同方式。那是日本的‘金继’艺术。

sentences.en: And learning about this blew my mind because it was such a, it was a paradox shifting way for me to think about overcoming or being better.
sentences.zh: 了解这一点让我大开眼界，因为它对我思考克服或变得更好是一种悖论式的转变。

sentences.en: And it wasn't the idea that we are perfect the way we were before something happened to us.
sentences.zh: 它不是说我们在事情发生前是完美的。

sentences.en: But rather it is that we get to wear our cracks with a new type of pride and a new type of beauty.
sentences.zh: 而是说我们可以带着一种新的自豪感和一种新的美感来展示我们的裂痕。

sentences.en: And that's maybe how I think of overcoming now, is I think of myself like a ceramic that has been cracked many times.
sentences.zh: 也许这就是我现在看待克服的方式，我把自己看作是一件被多次裂开的陶瓷。

sentences.en: And because of the love in my life and because of great therapists and because of good people and because I've worked and And I've managed to find ways to put gold bondage in those cracks to somehow find a little more beauty in myself than I had before the thing that happened to me.
sentences.zh: 因为我生命中的爱，因为伟大的治疗师，因为好人，因为我努力工作，我设法找到了在那些裂缝中填入金漆的方法，从而在某种程度上比事情发生前在自己身上发现了更多的美。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, every time I see those, it actually makes me emotional when I look at each one and I think about the story sort of of the person that each vessel contains.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，每次我看到这些，当我看着每一个裂痕，想到每个容器所承载的故事时，我真的会感到情绪激动。

sentences.en: My last question is a very complex question, but it was inspired by what you just said about Kintsugi, the Japanese tradition, which is I spoke to a guy called Mo Gorda on my podcast who had lost his son.
sentences.zh: 我的最后一个问题是一个非常复杂的问题，但它受到了你刚才说的关于‘金继’这种日本传统的启发，那就是我在我的播客上采访过一个叫Mo Gawdat的人，他失去了他的儿子。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah. I love Mo. Yeah, I love your conversation with him.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。我爱Mo。是的，我喜欢你和他的对话。

sentences.en: That was great. It's one of my favorite of all time because for many reasons, but many of them you've touched on today.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。那是我有史以来最喜欢的对话之一，原因有很多，但其中许多你今天都提到了。

sentences.en: And in that conversation, he said something to me about the loss of his son.
sentences.zh: 在那次谈话中，他对我说了关于他儿子去世的事。

sentences.en: He said, there's this thing called the eraser test.
sentences.zh: 他说，有一个东西叫‘橡皮擦测试’。

sentences.en: I don't know if you've ever heard about it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你有没有听说过。

sentences.en: They ask a group of people who've been through a lot of difficult experiences that... if there was a button yes um in front of them that could it would erase all of those experiences really difficult experiences at times would they press it now if i put a button in front of you and it would erase what happened to your mother being shot at that age um would you press it yes i would you would yeah i would and this is this is a fundamental philosophical argument that i have with people this is purely like philosophy and it's the way i see the world and i think the way some people see the world.
sentences.zh: 他们问一群经历过很多困难经历的人……如果他们面前有一个按钮，可以擦除所有那些非常困难的经历，他们会按吗？现在，如果我把你面前放一个按钮，它可以擦除你母亲在那时被枪击的经历，你会按吗？是的，我会。你会吗？是的，我会。这是一个我和人们争论的基本哲学问题，这纯粹是哲学，这是我看待世界的方式，也是我认为某些人看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: I understand that many of the times, or I understand that like oftentimes people come out of a bad experience with a new learning or something that has improved them in many ways.
sentences.zh: 我明白很多时候，或者我明白人们往往会从糟糕的经历中获得新的学习，或者某种在许多方面改善了他们的东西。

sentences.en: But I think we should never take for granted how many times that doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们永远不应该认为这是理所当然的，因为很多时候这种情况并没有发生。

sentences.en: You know, I think we should never take for granted how many people are broken by a bad thing. and I think we've done something in society and maybe it's because we want to valorize it or maybe it's because we want to make people feel like they're not victims or we want to make it seem like there was some purpose or meaning.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为我们永远不应该认为有多少人被糟糕的事情摧毁是理所当然的。我觉得我们在社会中做了一些事情，也许是因为我们想美化它，或者因为我们想让人们觉得他们不是受害者，或者我们想让它看起来好像有什么目的或意义。

sentences.en: Maybe it's tied to religion. I think we at times have sort of valorized this idea.
sentences.zh: 也许这和宗教有关。我觉得我们有时美化了这个想法。

sentences.en: It happened to you for a reason, you know?
sentences.zh: ‘这件事发生在你身上是有原因的’，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And so now you get this kid who was abused by their parents or someone in their family and you're like, it happened to you for a reason.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你看到一个被父母或家人虐待的孩子，你会说，‘这件事发生在你身上是有原因的’。

sentences.en: It made you the person you are today, you know? or somebody who suffered a horrible trauma or like a car accident, a terrorist attack, whatever it is, hey, it happened to you for a reason.
sentences.zh: ‘它造就了今天的你’，你知道吗？或者某人遭受了可怕的创伤，比如车祸、恐怖袭击，无论是什么，嘿，‘这件事发生在你身上是有原因的’。

sentences.en: You're gonna, you know, look at you, you will be stronger or look at you today, you wouldn't be this person.
sentences.zh: ‘你会变得更坚强’，或者‘看看今天的你，如果没有那件事，你就不会是现在这样的人’。

sentences.en: You know what people forget to talk about?
sentences.zh: 你知道人们忘了谈论什么吗？

sentences.en: Is the fact that, yeah, you could have been a different version of you.
sentences.zh: 事实是，是的，你本可以成为一个不同的自己。

sentences.en: You could have been happier. You could have been less wounded.
sentences.zh: 你本可以更快乐。你本可以少受点伤。

sentences.en: You could have carried less burden. You could have been less hurtful because of that.
sentences.zh: 你本可以少背负一些负担。你本可以因为那件事而少伤害别人。

sentences.en: And I think we should never take that for granted.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们永远不应该认为这是理所当然的。

sentences.en: I think we should encourage people to find the best.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们应该鼓励人们去寻找最好的一面。

sentences.en: And we should always say to ourselves, hey, what can I get from the situation?
sentences.zh: 我们应该总是对自己说，嘿，我能从这种情况中得到什么？

sentences.en: What can I learn from it? How can I grow from it?
sentences.zh: 我能从中学习什么？我能如何从中成长？

sentences.en: But I am not a fan of anybody saying that they will keep it because it's made them who they are.
sentences.zh: 但我并不赞成任何人说他们会保留这些经历，因为它们造就了现在的他们。

sentences.en: Just because you've survived a storm doesn't mean that you should want to keep that storm.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为你从风暴中幸存下来，并不意味着你应该想要保留那场风暴。

sentences.en: And that's why I say it's a philosophical argument.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我说这是一个哲学论点。

sentences.en: It really is. but I don't like how we've done that to people because in some way, I feel like it makes people think that they now have to be grateful for a terrible thing that has happened to them or a terrible thing that they've experienced or people around them have experienced because they've come out more resilient on the other side of it.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。但我并不喜欢我们对人们做这种事的方式，因为在某种程度上，我觉得这让人们认为他们现在必须对发生在他们身上的可怕事情，或者他们经历过的可怕事情，或者他们周围的人经历过的可怕事情感到感激，仅仅因为他们在经历之后变得更有韧性了。

sentences.en: Everything happens to you for a reason. Yeah, and so if I could replace it, I go, no, I forget that.
sentences.zh: ‘一切发生皆有原因’。是的，所以如果我能替换它，我会说，不，我忘了那个。

sentences.en: I don't go like everything happens to you or doesn't.
sentences.zh: 我不会说‘一切发生皆有原因’。

sentences.en: I go back to what I said, my friend, phrase my friend taught me, who do you choose to be?
sentences.zh: 我回到我刚才说的，我朋友教我的那句话，‘你选择成为谁？’

sentences.en: I would say forget the eraser test. I would say to you, it can never be an eraser test.
sentences.zh: 我会说，忘了橡皮擦测试吧。我会对你说，这永远不可能是橡皮擦测试。

sentences.en: Why don't we replace it with a pencil test, a pen test, a marker test, whatever device you want to use.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不把它换成铅笔测试、钢笔测试、记号笔测试，或者任何你想用的工具呢？

sentences.en: And you go, if you could press this button and decide what story you write on the other side of the thing that happened to you, would you now write that story?
sentences.zh: 然后你说，如果你能按下这个按钮，决定你在发生在你身上的事情之后写下什么故事，你现在会写那个故事吗？

sentences.en: And what story would you write? I think that's more important because the eraser thing makes people now feel like they have to disown a part of themselves, which most people will not want to do.
sentences.zh: 你会写什么故事？我认为这更重要，因为橡皮擦测试会让人们觉得他们必须否认自己的一部分，而大多数人是不愿意这样做的。

sentences.en: But then it makes you feel like you have to like claim this thing as being part of yourself.
sentences.zh: 但它又让你觉得你必须把这件事当作你自己的一部分来认领。

sentences.en: No, I would press that button. I would erase my mother being shot.
sentences.zh: 不，我会按那个按钮。我会擦除我母亲被枪击的事。

sentences.en: I would erase me having ADHD. I would erase the tough times that my country went out, erase apartheid.
sentences.zh: 我会擦除我患有ADHD的事。我会擦除我国家经历的艰难时期，擦除种族隔离。

sentences.en: I wouldn't be like, I would keep apartheid, Stephen, because if it wasn't for apartheid, I wouldn't be here with you today.
sentences.zh: 我不会说，‘Stephen，我会保留种族隔离，因为如果没有种族隔离，我就不会今天在这里和你在一起了’。

sentences.en: No, no, no, no, no, no. I would erase it.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，不，不，不。我会擦除它。

sentences.en: And maybe we'd be dealing with something else.
sentences.zh: 也许我们会处理别的事情。

sentences.en: But if I could, I would press that button because I, yeah.
sentences.zh: 但如果可以，我会按那个按钮，因为我，是的。

sentences.en: I don't think we need to celebrate it. I think we need to work on it.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们需要庆祝它。我认为我们需要去解决它。

sentences.en: And, you know, we need to strive to heal ourselves.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们需要努力去治愈自己。

sentences.en: But I don't think your tribulations are what make you.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为你的苦难造就了你。

sentences.en: You survived. And I'm proud of you for surviving.
sentences.zh: 你幸存了下来。我为你幸存下来感到骄傲。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that you needed to go through what you had to go through.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着你需要经历你所经历的一切。

sentences.en: So beautifully said. You have a wonderful podcast.
sentences.zh: 说得太好了。你有一个很棒的播客。

sentences.en: I could talk to you all day. But if people want to hear more from you, they have to go and listen to your podcast.
sentences.zh: 我可以和你聊一整天。但如果人们想听到更多你的声音，他们必须去听你的播客。

sentences.en: It's called What Now? It's on Spotify. You speak to a whole range of people like me. but you do it in a very different way, but in the way and with the same set of components as to what's made you such a hit with so many people.
sentences.zh: 它叫《What Now?》。在Spotify上。你和像我这样的人交谈，但你用一种非常不同的方式，用和你让这么多人喜欢你的同样的要素来做这件事。

sentences.en: I can't tell you how much, you know, my team, my family, my sister, my brothers, they're such tremendous fans of you because you have this wonderful blend of wisdom.
sentences.zh: 我无法告诉你，你知道，我的团队、我的家人、我的姐妹、我的兄弟，他们是多么崇拜你，因为你有一种美妙的智慧融合。

sentences.en: I now know where it all comes from. Humility, vulnerability, and you are authentic.
sentences.zh: 我现在知道这一切来自哪里了。谦逊、脆弱，而且你是真实的。

sentences.en: And authentic is a complicated word, but you are authentic as anyone could hope to be. and that's why everyone has to go listen to your podcast it's the third link that i'm going to put down below it's called what now um and it's one of my favorites trevor thank you so much from the guy who made easily one of the best ever thank you very much no no i mean this i mean this for real you know i always say like i go if you want to see a professional podcast go go to diary of a ceo if you want to come explore my mind come listen to what now people want to explore your mind no but for real i'm like congratulations i appreciate you thank you so much and i can't tell you how much of an honor this was sometimes i get quite nervous to interview people and you're oh wow thank you i got nervous too because i respect you so much so thank you so much for the time i appreciate you yeah man and don't don't spend as much time alone you're not like you know i know you've always been there and i know it can feel in a weird way it can feel like the comfortable place but like it doesn't need to be i'm learning this yeah you'll be shocked at like how much lies on the other side of it you know in a weird way you'll you'll you'll be shocked at what finding that belonging can do for you.
sentences.zh: ‘真实’是一个复杂的词，但你和任何人所能期望的一样真实。这就是为什么每个人都必须去听你的播客，这是我放在下面的第三个链接，它叫《What Now》。嗯，这是我最喜欢的播客之一。Trevor，非常感谢你，来自那个制作了绝对是史上最好播客之一的人。非常感谢。不，不，我是认真的，我是认真的。你知道，我总是说，如果你想看一个专业的播客，去听《Diary of a CEO》；如果你想来探索我的思想，来听《What Now》。人们想探索你的思想。不，我是认真的，祝贺你。我很感激你，非常感谢。我无法告诉你这是一种多么大的荣幸。有时采访别人我会很紧张，而你……哦，哇，谢谢。我也很紧张，因为我非常尊重你，所以非常感谢你的时间，我很感激你。是的，伙计，别花那么多时间独处。你不是……你知道，我知道你一直都在那里，我知道在某种奇怪的方式下，它感觉像是一个舒适的地方，但它不需要是这样。我正在学习这一点。是的，你会惊讶于它另一面有多少东西，你知道，在某种奇怪的方式下，你会惊讶于找到那种归属感能为你做什么。

sentences.en: It comes with risk the same way it does in a romantic relationship.
sentences.zh: 它伴随着风险，就像在浪漫关系中一样。

sentences.en: But man, it's easily the most rewarding.
sentences.zh: 但伙计，这绝对是最有回报的。

sentences.en: If I could evangelize one thing to people out there, it would be find your people, find your place.
sentences.zh: 如果我能向人们传达一件事，那就是找到你的同伴，找到你的位置。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, I think that's what's happening these days.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我认为这就是现在正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: People are finding that place in negativity.
sentences.zh: 人们在消极情绪中找到了那个位置。

sentences.en: People are finding community in negativity.
sentences.zh: 人们在消极情绪中找到了社区。

sentences.en: Now we all hate together. We all hate tweet together.
sentences.zh: 现在我们一起仇恨。我们一起在推特上发泄仇恨。

sentences.en: And we're all like angry at women together.
sentences.zh: 我们一起对女性感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And we all hate that music artist together.
sentences.zh: 我们一起讨厌那个音乐艺术家。

sentences.en: And we all, yeah, let's hate together. But it's not sustainable because it gobbles us up.
sentences.zh: 我们一起，是的，让我们一起仇恨吧。但这不可持续，因为它会吞噬我们。

sentences.en: It's like, it's just like chews us up and spits us out.
sentences.zh: 它就像，它就像嚼碎我们然后吐出来。

sentences.en: But if you can find the things that you love doing for you, and then you find the people who love doing it as well, and it makes you feel good, the thing on the other side is it's magic.
sentences.zh: 但如果你能找到你喜欢做的事情，然后找到也喜欢做这些事情的人，这让你感觉很好，另一面的东西就是魔法。

sentences.en: In fact, they've shown studies. I know you love studies.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们已经做了研究。我知道你喜欢研究。

sentences.en: Studies, multiple studies have shown, and I think a meta-analysis as well, has shown that people who have a strong group of friends actually have better romantic relationships because the burden of your relationship is now lessened by having this community as opposed to people who merge with one person and then all their hopes, aspirations, dreams, fears, frustrations are just poured on them.
sentences.zh: 研究，多项研究表明，我想还有一个荟萃分析也表明，拥有强大朋友圈的人实际上有更好的浪漫关系，因为你的关系的负担现在被这个社区减轻了，而不是像那些只与一个人融合，然后把所有的希望、抱负、梦想、恐惧、挫折都倾注在对方身上的人。

sentences.en: You reach a breaking point, but you can actually have, it's not replacing it, by the way.
sentences.zh: 你会达到一个临界点，但你实际上可以拥有，顺便说一句，这不是替代它。

sentences.en: You have a better romantic relationship when you maintain and you have a strong friendship.
sentences.zh: 当你维持并拥有强大的友谊时，你会拥有更好的浪漫关系。

sentences.en: So I encourage it. Do it. I promise you I will.
sentences.zh: 所以我鼓励这样做。去做吧。我向你保证我会的。

sentences.en: Do it. I promise. It's going to be great.
sentences.zh: 去做吧。我保证。这会很棒的。

sentences.en: Thank you, Trent. Thank you, man. Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，Trent。谢谢，伙计。太感谢了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much. I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 太感谢了。我真的很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
